NEW-146. The Mapmaker's Apprentice   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) the villager who meets the apprentice: any villager 14+. The apprentice is a visiting young adult (sex at random) who may become a new adult villager.
EVENT TEXT
A young traveller walks into the village carrying a map drawn on a stretched hide. It's half finished. The island's coast is drawn in, wobbly but recognizable. The inland is entirely blank, except for one word in the middle: "?"
"I'm a mapmaker," the traveller says. "Well. An apprentice. Well. I'm trying." (He/She) asks (name) for work, any work at all, in exchange for being allowed to walk every trail on the island.
(Name) looks at the map. (His/Her) own hut, (he/she) notices, is drawn as a small blob labelled "goat?" (Name) isn't sure whether to be insulted or amused. Should (he/she) give this hopeful apprentice a chance?
Choice A: Offer Them Water and Shade
Choice B: Ask About Their Map
Choice C: Ask If They Want to Stay On
Choice D: Swap Trail Walks for Harvest Help

CHOICE A: OFFER THEM WATER AND SHADE
First popup: (Name) decides that, before anything else, this sunburned person needs a drink...
Ending A1 -- MAP CLUTCHED TIGHT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The apprentice is given water, shade and a meal, and falls asleep almost at once, with the map clutched to (his/her) chest like a baby. (Name) gently corrects "goat?" to "hut" while (he/she) sleeps.
Ending A2 -- SMOKED EEL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The apprentice shares a pouch of smoked eel from (his/her) travels, which is chewy, strange and delicious. It adds a little food, and the children dare each other to eat it.

CHOICE B: ASK ABOUT THEIR MAP
First popup: (Name) asks how the apprentice is making the map. The apprentice brightens immediately and pulls out a long knotted cord...
Ending B1 -- PACES AND KNOTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The apprentice shows how (he/she) measures distance by counting paces, and tying a knot in the cord every hundred steps, so (he/she) always knows how far (he/she) has walked. It's a simple, clever method, and it teaches the village something useful about maps. The builders start using it to lay out new huts.
Ending B2 -- WHO TAUGHT ME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When (name) asks who taught (him/her) to make maps, the apprentice goes evasive. (He/She) won't say, and nobody insists. "Someone very good," is all (he/she) offers, "who didn't want to be found."

CHOICE C: ASK IF THEY WANT TO STAY ON
First popup: Seeing how happy the apprentice is walking the trails, (name) asks whether (he/she) might want to stay a while...
Ending C1 -- FINISHING FROM HERE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: new villager (adult): the apprentice
The apprentice decides to finish the map from here, using the village as a base, and joins the village permanently as a new adult villager. The finished map, some seasons later, is hung in pride of place. (Name)'s hut is correctly labelled. Mostly.
Ending C2 -- THE NEXT STRETCH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The apprentice thanks them, but there is so much inland left to map, and (he/she) can't bear to stop. (He/She) walks on in the morning to map the next stretch, promising to bring back a copy.

CHOICE D: SWAP TRAIL WALKS FOR HARVEST HELP
First popup: (Name) agrees to the deal: help with the work in the mornings, walk the trails in the afternoons...
Ending D1 -- BETWEEN WALKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (normal)
Between trail walks, the apprentice helps with the harvest, and adds a good amount of food to the stores. (He/She) also maps every field in the village, which the farmers find extremely useful for arguing about who owns what.
Ending D2 -- THE WARPED HIDE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the second day, rain warps the hide map badly, and the apprentice is in despair. The villagers help restretch it on a frame by the fire, slowly, until it's flat again, and send (him/her) onward with it, dry.

MIXER SEED NEW-146
Premise: A young traveller walks in with a half-finished map on a stretched hide. The inland is blank except for one word, "?", and a villager's hut is labelled "goat?"
Roles: host: any villager 14+ | apprentice: a visitor who may become a new adult villager

NEW-147. The Injured Visitor   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) the villager who finds the traveller: any villager 14+ (prefer a healer). The traveller is a visitor (sex at random) who may become a new adult villager.
EVENT TEXT
A traveller limps into the village from the volcanic side of the island. (His/Her) sandals are shredded to ribbons, and (his/her) feet are cut in a dozen places by the sharp black rock out there.
(He/She) is grateful, embarrassed and very hungry, in roughly that order, and apologizes three times before (name) can even ask (his/her) name. "I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to bleed on your path."
(Name) looks down at the trail of small red footprints leading back toward the volcano, and winces. The traveller needs help, and fast. What should (name) do?
Choice A: Bring Them to the Healer's Mat
Choice B: Ask How They Crossed the Black Rock
Choice C: Let Them Heal Here for Good
Choice D: Trade Rest for Light Work

CHOICE A: BRING THEM TO THE HEALER'S MAT
First popup: (Name) half-carries the traveller to the healers, who take one look at the feet and send for warm water...
Ending A1 -- A SOFT MAT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The traveller's feet are washed, salved and wrapped in clean leaves, and (he/she) rests on a soft mat for the first time in days. (He/She) apologizes twice more, then falls asleep mid-apology.
Ending A2 -- THE NUTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The traveller insists on sharing the sack of nuts (he/she) carried all the way across the lava, even though (he/she) can barely sit up. "Please. I'll feel better." It adds a little food, and (he/she) does seem to feel better.

CHOICE B: ASK HOW THEY CROSSED THE BLACK ROCK
First popup: Once (his/her) feet are wrapped, (name) asks how anyone crosses that rock at all...
Ending B1 -- SAFE STONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The traveller explains how to tell which black rock is safe to step on and which will slice a foot open: the smooth, rope-like rock is safe, the jagged glassy kind is not, and the brittle crust over hollows is worst of all. It teaches the village something genuinely useful about avoiding injuries like (his/hers), and the healers ask (him/her) to repeat it to every child who goes near the volcano.
Ending B2 -- WHY THAT WAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When (name) asks why (he/she) risked the crossing at all, the traveller looks away. (He/She) would rather not say, and nobody asks again.

CHOICE C: LET THEM HEAL HERE FOR GOOD
First popup: As the days go by and the feet slowly heal, (name) notices the traveller looking around the village with something like longing...
Ending C1 -- STAYING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: new villager (adult): the traveller
Once (his/her) feet have healed, the traveller decides to join the village permanently as a new adult villager. (He/She) never goes near the volcano side again, and becomes the village's most passionate advocate for good sandals.
Ending C2 -- HOME AGAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As soon as (he/she) can walk without wincing, the traveller thanks the village, many times, and heads home. By the long way. Not across the rock.

CHOICE D: TRADE REST FOR LIGHT WORK

NEW-151. The First Rain After Drought   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) a farmer: any villager 18+ (prefer high Farming).
EVENT TEXT
For weeks the ground has been cracked and grey. The stream shrank to a trickle. The farmers planted anxiously, watered by hand, and watched the sky every evening for clouds that never came.
Then, this afternoon, the sky finally opens.
Children dance in the puddles, shrieking. (Name) and the other farmers stand in the fields with their faces turned up to the rain, laughing like fools, soaked to the skin.
Then the rain does not stop. It gets heavier. And heavier. And from inside the storehouse, whose roof has dried out and gone brittle over the long drought, comes a sound everyone recognizes: drip... drip... drip-drip-drip. The rain is a blessing, but the stores are getting wet, and the paths are turning to mud. What should (name) do first?
Choice A: Cover the Storehouse
Choice B: Run from Hut to Hut
Choice C: Mark How Fast the Ground Drinks
Choice D: Patch the Dripping Roofs

CHOICE A: COVER THE STOREHOUSE
First popup: (Name) shouts for help, and a team of soaked villagers races to drag palm mats over the storehouse roof, while others run for the fields...
Ending A1 -- SAVED GOURDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The mats go on just in time, and the quick-thinking villagers in the fields pull the ripe gourds in before the downpour can split them open. The storehouse stays dry, and the rescued gourds add a little food to the stores. (Name) collapses on a bench, soaked and grinning.
Ending A2 -- THE SOAKED BASKET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
Water gets in under the mats anyway, running in rivulets down the inside walls. By the time anyone notices, a basket of dried fish at the back is soaked through and swimming. It has to be thrown out. After weeks of praying for rain, nobody quite knows how to feel about this.

CHOICE B: RUN FROM HUT TO HUT
First popup: (Name) runs through the village, splashing through puddles, checking that everyone is safe and dry...
Ending B1 -- SQUEEZED TOGETHER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everyone is safe. Families whose roofs are leaking squeeze together in the driest huts to wait out the rain, sharing blankets and stories and complaining cheerfully about each other's feet. It is crowded, damp and surprisingly happy.
Ending B2 -- THE SLICK PATH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)
Running back from the far huts, (name) slips on the field path, which has turned from dust into slick mud in an instant, and goes down hard. (His/Her) leg twists under (him/her) badly. (He/She) has to be carried to the healers, and will need their care for a while before (he/she) can walk properly again.

CHOICE C: MARK HOW FAST THE GROUND DRINKS
First popup: While everyone else panics, (name) stands in the rain with a bundle of sticks, pushing them into the ground in different fields to see where the water soaks in and where it pools...
Ending C1 -- THE TERRACES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
By the time the rain finally eases, (name) has noticed a clear pattern: the terraced plots on the slope soaked up the rain like a sponge, while the flat ones by the stream flooded and washed away. It's a useful lesson for next season's planting, and the farmers start building terraces on the flat ground.
Ending C2 -- NO PATTERN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The sticks in different fields disagree completely: one flat field flooded, another didn't; one terrace soaked it up, another ran with mud. The farmers decide to wait for the next rain before guessing at anything. (Name) is very wet and has learned nothing, but (he/she) doesn't seem to mind.

CHOICE D: PATCH THE DRIPPING ROOFS
First popup: (Name) gathers every pair of hands that isn't busy, and they set to work on the leaking roofs with fresh thatch and sap, in the pouring rain...
Ending D1 -- DRY BY NIGHT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The workers patch the worst roofs before dark, and the storehouse stays dry through the night. The village goes to sleep to the sound of rain on solid thatch, which, after the long drought, is the most beautiful sound anyone has ever heard.
Ending D2 -- HUNGRY WORKERS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
The patching goes on and on, right through dinner and into the night. The soaked, shivering, hungry workers have to be fed twice, and it all comes out of the stores, leaving a little less food. Nobody begrudges it.

NEW-152. The Fog That Held   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) a fisher: any villager 18+.
EVENT TEXT
A fog rolls in from the sea, so thick that (name) can't see (his/her) own feet. It doesn't lift by midday. It doesn't lift by evening. By the second morning, it's still there, grey and wet and silent, swallowing every sound.
The fishing canoes can't find the reef markers. Most of them felt their way back to the beach by sound. One canoe hasn't come back at all.
(Name) stands at the water's edge, listening to the fog, and hears nothing. Not a paddle. Not a voice. Should (name) save what can be saved on shore, or try to guide the missing canoe home?
Choice A: Bring the Catch Inside

Choice C: Note Where the Fog Thins

Ending D1 -- BEFORE NIGHTFALL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D2 -- THE BORROWED BASKETS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)

WHO: (Name) the granary keeper: any villager 18+.
EVENT TEXT
A howling wind comes up in the night, the kind that makes huts creak and babies cry. In the morning, (name) walks out to the grain shelter and stops dead.

And every bird on the island seems to have heard the news. They are arriving in flocks. They look very pleased. (Name) doesn't know where to start. What should (he/she) do first?
Choice A: Sweep Up the Spilled Grain
Choice B: Check on the Granary Keeper's Family
Choice C: Watch Which Way the Wind Tears
Choice D: Rethatch the Granary

Ending A1 -- SAVED FROM THE FLOORS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Quick work saves the grain that landed on the swept floors of the huts and the clean stones of the cooking area. It goes back into the stores as usable food, and somehow, in the sweeping, a few forgotten baskets from the back of the shelter turn up as well. The birds leave, disappointed.
Ending A2 -- THE RAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
Then the rain follows the wind. Before the roof can be covered, a whole basket of stored grain is soaked, swells up and starts to sprout, and must be thrown out. The birds, at least, are delighted.

Ending B1 -- WITH NEIGHBOURS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everyone is fine, just shaken. The keeper's family move in with neighbours until the roof is fixed, bringing their sleeping mats and a lot of grain in their hair.
Ending B2 -- THE ROOF POLE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)

CHOICE C: WATCH WHICH WAY THE WIND TEARS

Ending C1 -- THE SEA SIDE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
(Name) notices the wind always rips the thatch from the sea side first, peeling it back like a banana skin. Talking to the builders, (he/she) realizes the other huts nearest the sea have the same worn edges. It's a useful pattern, and the builders start tying the sea-facing edges down twice as tight.
Ending C2 -- DISAGREEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name)'s notes and the builders' memories disagree about which side went first, and nobody can prove it either way. They decide to wait for more evidence before changing anything. The birds, meanwhile, keep eating.

CHOICE D: RETHATCH THE GRANARY

Ending D1 -- BEFORE NIGHTFALL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The workers rethatch the granary roof before nightfall, tighter and thicker than before. When the wind comes back the next night, the roof doesn't even rustle. The birds give up and leave.
Ending D2 -- SHORT OF ROPE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
Halfway through, the village runs out of rope. A passing trader has plenty, but wants grain for it. Some stored grain is traded away, leaving less food in the stores, but the roof gets finished, and finished properly.

WHO: (Name) the teacher: any villager 18+ (in The Tree of Life, the nursery teacher if there is one).
EVENT TEXT
The afternoon is scorching. Not just hot: the kind of heat where the air wobbles and the birds stop singing and the dogs lie flat in the shade like dropped blankets.
Inside the lesson hut, it's an oven. The children are wilting over their counting pebbles. (Name), the teacher, is sweating straight through (his/her) wrap, and has asked "What are seven and five?" three times. Nobody can remember. (Name) can't remember either.
Outside, the fruit on the drying racks is starting to blacken in the sun. The children, the fruit, the heat itself: what should (name) deal with first?
Choice A: Shade the Drying Racks
Choice B: Check on Every Child
Choice C: Track the Hottest Hours
Choice D: Open Up the Hut Walls

Ending A1 -- SAVED FRUIT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Quick hands move the fruit into the shade before the sun can scorch it, and save it as usable food for the stores. The children are very proud. (Name) declares that this counts as a counting lesson, because they counted the fruit. Seven racks and five racks. Twelve.
Ending A2 -- THE SPOILED FISH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
The fruit is saved, but the heat has already got into the storehouse. When (name) checks, a basket of fish has spoiled in the heat, and smells so terrible that the children run screaming. It has to be thrown out, quickly, and far away.

Ending B1 -- UNDER THE TREES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE C: TRACK THE HOTTEST HOURS

Ending C1 -- AFTER DAWN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)

Ending C2 -- WILD GUESSES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D1 -- THE BREEZE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The workers cut windows and raise the lower walls on props, and before evening, the sea breeze blows straight through the lesson hut. The children cheer. It's so pleasant that the adults start sneaking in to nap there in the afternoons.
Ending D2 -- THE COCONUTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
The work crew, sweltering in the heat, drinks its way through a whole pile of stored coconuts before the job is done, leaving less food in the stores. But the breeze blows through the hut by evening, and nobody complains.

NEW-155. The Flooded Path   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) a worker: any villager 18+.
EVENT TEXT
After a night of heavy rain, the stream has jumped its banks. It now flows straight across the main path between the huts and the fields, knee-deep, brown and fast, full of floating sticks and leaves and one very confused frog.
Half the village is on one side of it. The other half is on the other side. The harvest baskets are on the wrong side entirely.
(Name) stands at the edge of the brown water, rolling up (his/her) wrap, and considers how deep "knee-deep" really is. How should (name) get everyone, and the harvest, across?
Choice A: Carry the Harvest Across
Choice B: Check Both Banks
Choice C: Mark How High the Water Rose
Choice D: Lay Stepping Stones

CHOICE A: CARRY THE HARVEST ACROSS
First popup: (Name) and a team of workers hoist the harvest baskets onto their shoulders and wade into the brown water...
Ending A1 -- THE FENCE FRUIT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The baskets make it across safely, and on the far side, (name) finds a heap of fallen fruit that the flood has washed up against the garden fence, all perfectly good. It's gathered up and adds a little food to the stores. The frog is rescued too.
Ending A2 -- THE TIPPED BASKET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
Halfway across, someone stumbles on a hidden root, and a basket tips into the brown water. By the time they fish it out, its food is soaked in mud and ruined, and has to be thrown out. Everyone else holds their baskets a lot higher after that.

CHOICE B: CHECK BOTH BANKS
First popup: (Name) wades back and forth across the flood, making sure everyone on both sides is accounted for...
Ending B1 -- FED BY NEIGHBOURS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everyone is accounted for on both sides. The families cut off from their huts are fed and housed by neighbours for the night, and the two halves of the village shout cheerful insults at each other across the water until bedtime.
Ending B2 -- THE HIDDEN STICK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)
On (his/her) third crossing, (name) steps on a sharp stick hidden under the muddy water. It goes deep into (his/her) foot. (He/She) limps out, gritting (his/her) teeth, leaving a red trail, and is helped to the healer. The wound needs care for a while.

CHOICE C: MARK HOW HIGH THE WATER ROSE
First popup: (Name) walks the length of the flood, marking with charcoal on every tree trunk how high the water has reached...
Ending C1 -- THE LOW DIP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Looking at the marks, (name) notices the water always crosses the path at the same spot: one low dip in the ground, no more than a few paces wide. Build that up, and the path would stay dry. It's a useful pattern, and the builders start raising the low dip as soon as the water goes down.
Ending C2 -- CONFUSING MARKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The marks left on the trees disagree: higher here, lower there, and one mark seems to have been made by a child at the wrong height entirely. The villagers decide to wait for more evidence before changing anything.

CHOICE D: LAY STEPPING STONES
First popup: (Name) organizes a crew to haul big, flat stones from the stream bed and lay a raised crossing across the flood...
Ending D1 -- THE CROSSING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Workers haul flat stones and lay a raised crossing before nightfall. It wobbles a little, but everyone gets across dry-footed. The children spend the evening running back and forth across it, shrieking.
Ending D2 -- HUNGRY WORK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
Hauling stones is hungry work. The crew eats an extra meal, then another, and it all comes out of the stores, leaving a little less food. But the crossing is solid, and it stays there long after the flood has gone.

NEW-156. The Lightning-Struck Tree   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) a woodcutter: any villager 18+ (prefer high Building).
EVENT TEXT
CRACK.
The flash and the noise come together, so loud that everyone in the village hits the ground. When they look up, the old mango tree beside the main trail, the one everyone has eaten from since they were children, has been split right down the middle.
Half of it is still standing. The other half leans out over the path at a terrible angle, creaking, groaning, held up by nothing much. Smoke curls up from the blackened heart of the trunk. Ripe mangoes are scattered everywhere.
(Name) looks at the leaning half, and at the people who will need to walk under it, and swallows. Should (name) save the mangoes, keep everyone away from the tree, or try to bring it down safely?
Choice A: Gather the Fallen Mangoes
Choice B: Warn Everyone Off the Trail
Choice C: Study the Burn Marks
Choice D: Clear and Brace the Trunk

CHOICE A: GATHER THE FALLEN MANGOES
First popup: Keeping well clear of the leaning half, (name) and a few others creep around the edges, gathering the mangoes knocked loose by the blast...
Ending A1 -- BEFORE THE BIRDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Quick hands gather the mangoes before the birds and bats can get them, adding a little food to the stores. Some are a little scorched. They taste, (name) reports, "like mango, but braver."
Ending A2 -- THE STOREHOUSE CORNER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
While everyone is busy with the mangoes, the storm's rain pours in through a corner of the storehouse that the thunder shook loose. A basket of stored food is ruined and has to be thrown out.

CHOICE B: WARN EVERYONE OFF THE TRAIL
First popup: (Name) runs to the trail and starts turning people back, waving (his/her) arms and shouting...
Ending B1 -- CLOSED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everyone is safe. The trail is closed with a rope across it until the tree is dealt with, and people take the long way around, grumbling. Nobody walks under the leaning half. The next morning, it falls on its own, harmlessly, onto an empty path.
Ending B2 -- THE FALLING BRANCH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)
While (name) is clearing the trail of debris in the rain, a big branch breaks free from the leaning half and comes down on (him/her). (He/She) is knocked flat. The others drag (him/her) clear and carry (him/her) to the healers; (he/she) is badly bruised and shaken, and will need care for some time.

CHOICE C: STUDY THE BURN MARKS
First popup: Once the storm passes, (name) examines the burned trunk carefully, and then walks around the island looking at other old lightning scars...
Ending C1 -- THE TALLEST TREES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
(Name) notices a pattern: lightning keeps choosing the tallest trees, especially the ones nearest the water. It's a useful lesson about where not to shelter in a storm, and the village teaches every child: in a storm, keep away from tall trees, especially near the shore.
Ending C2 -- NO DIRECTION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The burn marks point in no clear direction, and the other lightning scars on the island don't seem to follow any pattern either. (Name) decides to wait for more evidence, though (he/she) hopes it doesn't come soon.

CHOICE D: CLEAR AND BRACE THE TRUNK
First popup: (Name) leads the workers in cutting away the dangerous half, and propping up what's left...
Ending D1 -- IT MAY FRUIT AGAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The workers cut away the leaning half and brace the standing half with strong poles before nightfall. It looks battered and lopsided, but alive. With luck, it may fruit again. Next season, it does, a little.
Ending D2 -- THREE DAYS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
The clean-up takes three days of hard work, and the workers' meals all come out of the stores, leaving a little less food. But the trail is clear, the stump is braced, and the leftover wood goes into the fires for a month.

NEW-157. The Sudden Cold   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) any villager 18+ (a member of one of the families).
EVENT TEXT
A run of strange, cold nights blows in off the sea. Not cool. COLD. The kind of cold the island almost never sees.
Families wake up shivering under thin sleeping mats. The babies are bundled in everything their parents own. The dogs have all moved into the huts and refuse to leave. Someone, and (name) is fairly sure it's one of the elders, is wearing a basket on their head as a hat.
And out in the fields, the ground is cold and soaking wet, and the root crops are starting to go soft. How can (name) help the village get through the cold?
Choice A: Dig the Roots Before They Rot
Choice B: Visit Every Hut
Choice C: Note Which Nights Turn Cold
Choice D: Weave Thicker Mats

CHOICE A: DIG THE ROOTS BEFORE THEY ROT
First popup: (Name) rounds up anyone with a digging stick and warm enough hands, and they head out into the cold fields...
Ending A1 -- UP IN TIME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Quick work brings the root crops up before the cold, wet ground can rot them, and they go into the dry storehouse, adding a little food. Everyone's fingers are numb. The basket-hat turns out to be very good for carrying yams.
Ending A2 -- THE ROTTEN FRUIT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
The roots are saved, but the cold damp has crept into the storehouse. A basket of stored fruit has gone soft and brown and rotten, and is thrown out.

CHOICE B: VISIT EVERY HUT
First popup: (Name) goes from hut to hut in the frosty dark, checking on everyone, especially the elders and the babies...
Ending B1 -- AROUND THE FIRES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everyone is accounted for. Families share blankets and squeeze in close around the fires, telling stories until the cold breaks. It is cramped and cosy, and several new friendships form over the shared blankets, and at least one feud.
Ending B2 -- THE DEW-SLICK ROCKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)

CHOICE C: NOTE WHICH NIGHTS TURN COLD

Ending C1 -- THE NORTH WIND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
After a few nights, (name) notices that the cold always follows a clear evening with a north wind. Cloudy nights stay warm. It's a useful pattern for knowing when to bank the fires and fetch the extra blankets, and the village never gets caught by a cold night again.
Ending C2 -- NO AGREEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nobody can agree which nights were the coldest. Everyone was too busy shivering to keep proper track. The villagers decide to wait for more evidence. Ideally, they all add, much later.

CHOICE D: WEAVE THICKER MATS

Ending D1 -- WARM BY NIGHTFALL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The weavers turn out thick new mats for every family before nightfall, working until their fingers ache. That night, the village sleeps warm for the first time all week. The dogs, sadly, are evicted.
Ending D2 -- EXTRA FIBRE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
The weavers run out of fibre halfway through. A neighbouring settlement has plenty, but wants food in exchange. Some stored food is traded away, leaving a little less in the stores, and every family gets its warm mat.

NEW-158. The Tide at the Door   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) a resident of the beach huts: any villager 18+.
EVENT TEXT
An unusually high tide creeps up the beach in the night, further than anyone has ever seen it, right up to the row of huts nearest the shore.
(Name) wakes up to the sound of water. Not distant waves: water, right there, lapping over (his/her) doorstep and swirling around the floor. Sandals are floating out to sea. A sleeping mat is drifting gently toward the door.
In the next hut, a family finds a crab sitting in their cooking pot, looking completely at home, as if it has been invited for dinner. The water is still coming in. What should (name) do first?
Choice A: Lift the Stores Up High
Choice B: Check the Beach Huts
Choice C: Mark the Water Line
Choice D: Build Up the Sand Banks

CHOICE A: LIFT THE STORES UP HIGH
First popup: (Name) splashes out and starts heaving baskets onto rafters and shelves, shouting for everyone else to do the same...
Ending A1 -- THE STRANDED FISH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Quick hands lift the baskets out of the water's reach, and as the tide drains away, (name) finds fish stranded in the flooded hollows behind the huts, flapping in the puddles. They're scooped up and add a little food to the stores. The crab in the pot is released, with apologies.
Ending A2 -- THE LOW BASKET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
One low basket in the corner is reached by the water before anyone can move it. The food inside is soaked in seawater and ruined. (Name) looks at it sadly. The crab, meanwhile, refuses to leave the pot.

CHOICE B: CHECK THE BEACH HUTS
First popup: (Name) wades from hut to hut along the shore, making sure everyone is awake and moving...
Ending B1 -- HIGHER HUTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everyone is safe. The beach families gather their belongings and sleep in higher huts up the hill until the water goes down, squeezed in with relatives and friends. By morning, the tide has gone back where it belongs, leaving seaweed on every doorstep.
Ending B2 -- THE TWISTED ANKLE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)
Carrying an armful of belongings up to higher ground, (name) slips on the wet stones by the path and twists (his/her) ankle badly. It swells up like a melon. (He/She) needs looking after for some days, and can't walk on it at all.

CHOICE C: MARK THE WATER LINE
First popup: Once everyone is safe, (name) goes along the huts marking exactly how high the water reached on every post...
Ending C1 -- FULL MOON AND ONSHORE WIND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Comparing tonight with what the old fishers remember, (name) notices the highest tides always come with a full moon and a strong wind blowing onshore. It's a useful pattern for knowing when to move the stores up high, and the village never gets caught by surprise again.
Ending C2 -- DISAGREEING MARKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The water marks on different huts disagree, some much higher than others, because some floors slope and some don't. The villagers decide to wait for the next high tide before drawing any conclusions.

CHOICE D: BUILD UP THE SAND BANKS

Ending D1 -- THE BANK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Workers pile sand and stones into a low bank in front of the huts before nightfall. When the next high tide comes, it laps right up against the bank, and stops. The beach families cheer from their dry doorsteps.
Ending D2 -- LATE SUPPER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
The work runs so late that the evening meal has to be cooked from food that was meant for later in the week, leaving a little less in the stores. But the bank holds.

NEW-159. The Dusty Season   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) the storehouse keeper: any villager 18+.
EVENT TEXT
Dry winds have been blowing for days, carrying fine red dust from who-knows-where. It gets into everything. The tools. The food baskets. The sleeping mats. The inside of everyone's ears.
Every meal crunches. The water tastes of grit. Everyone's hair has turned the same shade of rusty red.
Even the children have stopped complaining, because every time they open their mouths to complain, dust gets in. (Name), the storehouse keeper, is staring at the storehouse door with deep foreboding. How can (name) protect the stores, and the village, from the dust?
Choice A: Seal the Food Baskets
Choice B: Check on the Coughing Neighbours
Choice C: Track Where the Dust Comes From

Ending A1 -- THE FORGOTTEN BUNDLE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Quick work seals the baskets, and at the very back of the storehouse, behind everything, (name) finds a forgotten bundle of dried fruit, still perfectly clean, wrapped tight in leaves by someone long ago. It adds a little food to the stores, and (name) feels like (he/she) found treasure.
Ending A2 -- THE UNSEALED BASKET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
Despite everything, dust gets into one basket that someone left unsealed, and turns the food inside into red, gritty paste. It's ruined, and has to be thrown out. (Name) says some words the children aren't supposed to hear.

CHOICE B: CHECK ON THE COUGHING NEIGHBOURS

Ending B1 -- DAMP CLOTHS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending B2 -- THE DIGGING STICK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name) is INJURED (loses health)

Ending C2 -- EVERYWHERE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D1 -- CLEAN BY NIGHT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Workers clean and cover the tools, mats and storehouse before nightfall, and enormous red clouds of dust billow up from every hut. That night, for the first time in days, dinner doesn't crunch.
Ending D2 -- EMPTIED BASKETS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
Every spare basket is emptied out to use as a cover for something else, and the food that was inside them has to be eaten early or thrown out, leaving less in the stores. The tools, at least, are spotless.

NEW-160. The Calm Before the Storm   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) the navigator: any villager 30+ (prefer the oldest fisher who is not an elder too frail to work).
EVENT TEXT
The sea goes flat. Not calm: flat, glassy, like a sheet of polished stone, all the way to the horizon. The birds go quiet. The insects go quiet. Even the babies go quiet.
Far offshore, a dark wall of cloud is building, taller and taller, the colour of a bruise.
(Name), the navigator, has seen this exactly once before, many years ago. (He/She) does not like it at all. (He/She) says so, loudly, running up and down the beach, until every head in the village has turned to look at (him/her), and then at the clouds. There isn't much time. What should (name) do first?

Choice D: Tie Down Everything That Moves

Ending A2 -- FASTER THAN EXPECTED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
The storm arrives faster than anyone expected, howling in before the racks are half cleared. A basket of stored food is caught out in the rain and the wind, and is ruined.

CHOICE B: COUNT HEADS BEFORE IT HITS

Ending B1 -- ALL SHELTERED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D1 -- RIDING IT OUT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D2 -- THE CRUSHED BASKETS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)

NEW-161. The Second Courtship   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (name1) a widowed villager: any villager 25+ whose partner has died (needs at least one grave), not currently partnered. (name2) a kind fisher: any villager 25+, not partnered, not a close relative of (name1). (name3) an old friend of (name1): any villager 25+. Any sexes.
EVENT TEXT
It has been a few years since (name1) lost (his/her) partner. The grief has softened, slowly, the way grief does, into something (he/she) can carry.
Lately, (name1) has been spending (his/her) evenings with (name2), a kind, quiet fisher. They walk the beach at sunset. They talk about nothing in particular. And (name1) has been laughing, really laughing, more than (he/she) has in a long, long time.
Then, one evening, the guilt arrives. All at once, like a wave. Laughing on the same beach where (he/she) used to walk with someone else...
(Name1) stops coming to the fire. (Name2) waits on the beach at sunset, alone, three nights in a row. (Name1) doesn't know if (he/she) is allowed to be this happy again. What should (he/she) do?
Choice A: Talk It Through in Private
Choice B: Let the Widow Set the Pace
Choice C: Ask an Old Friend's Opinion

CHOICE A: TALK IT THROUGH IN PRIVATE
First popup: On the fourth night, (name1) walks down to the beach. (Name2) is there, as always. (Name1) sits down on the sand a little way off, and takes a deep breath...
Ending A1 -- GUILT AND ALL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name1) tells (name2) everything: the guilt, the memories, how happy (he/she) has been, and how that happiness frightens (him/her). (He/She) doesn't ask for anything in return. (Name2) listens without interrupting, then says simply, "I'll be here at sunset. Whenever you're ready. Or not." They watch the sun go down together, a little further apart than usual.
Ending A2 -- ONLY FRIENDSHIP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Before (name1) can finish, (name2) gently admits that (he/she) only ever hoped for friendship. A good friend to walk with at sunset, nothing more. (Name1) is surprised to find (himself/herself) a little relieved, and accepts it gladly. Their sunset walks carry on, lighter than before.

After a week, (name1) comes back to the beach at sunset. The two of them decide for themselves how and when to carry on, slowly, and nobody hurries them. Weeks later, (name1) brings (name2) to visit (his/her) late partner's grave, and they leave flowers there together.
Ending B2 -- NOT YET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nothing is decided. (Name1) still comes to the fire sometimes, and nods to (name2), and sometimes they sit together, and sometimes they don't. Both seem content to let it wait. Some things can't be hurried, and they both know it.

CHOICE C: ASK AN OLD FRIEND'S OPINION
First popup: (Name1) goes to (name3), (his/her) oldest friend, who knew (his/her) late partner well...
Ending C1 -- LISTENING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

NEW-167. The Partners at Work   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (name1) and (name2) a couple, both 18+, partners as the game records it, both working in research (prefer Research 20+). (head name) the head researcher: any villager 18+ with the highest Research, never the couple.
EVENT TEXT
(Name1) and (name2) both work in the same research hut. It seemed like a lovely idea when they started. They could spend all day together!
They do spend all day together. And lately, every single disagreement about the work follows them home to dinner.
Last night they argued about the proper way to sort seeds (by size? by colour? by which plant they came from?) until the fire went out. Then they kept arguing in the dark. Then they went to bed angry, and woke up, and the first thing (name1) said was "By SIZE."
The other researchers have started eating lunch somewhere else. How can (name1) and (name2) stop bringing the work home?
Choice A: Talk Away from the Hut
Choice B: Spend a Day with No Work at All
Choice C: Ask the Head Researcher

CHOICE A: TALK AWAY FROM THE HUT
First popup: (Name2) takes (name1) by the hand and walks (him/her) to the far end of the beach, as far from the research hut as they can get...
Ending A1 -- HOW IT WEARS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the beach, they each explain how the work is wearing on them, without demanding the other change. (Name1) feels like every disagreement at work is a disagreement about them. (Name2) feels the same. Saying it out loud takes the sting out. They agree on a rule: no seeds after sunset.
Ending A2 -- NOT YET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name1) admits (he/she) would rather not talk about it yet; (he/she) is too tired and too cross, and might say something unkind. (Name2) accepts that. They sit on the sand in silence and watch the waves, which, it turns out, is exactly what they both needed.

CHOICE B: SPEND A DAY WITH NO WORK AT ALL
First popup: The next morning, instead of going to the research hut, (name1) and (name2) go swimming. And fishing. And napping. They do not mention seeds once...
Ending B1 -- AGAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It's a wonderful day. They laugh more than they have in a month. By evening they agree to do it again, regularly, and the next day at work, when the seed argument comes up, they both just laugh. They sort the seeds by size AND colour. It takes twice as long. Nobody minds.
Ending B2 -- DIFFERENT THINGS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Away from the hut, they realize they actually want different things from the work: one wants to study plants, the other wants to study the stars. They still love each other. But maybe, they decide, they don't need to work in the same hut.

CHOICE C: ASK THE HEAD RESEARCHER
First popup: Desperate, the two of them go together to (head name), and lay out the seed question, from both sides, at great length...
Ending C1 -- WITH THEM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Head name) listens patiently to both, and leaves the decision with them. "You both have good points," (he/she) says. "Work it out between you. And please, please do it somewhere other than my hut." They do.
Ending C2 -- MY WAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Head name)'s advice is to sort the seeds (his/her) way, by the moon phase they were picked in, which neither of them had even considered. Neither of them likes it. United at last against a common enemy, the partners follow their own judgment, and go home arm in arm, complaining about (head name).

MIXER SEED NEW-167
Premise: Two partners work in the same research hut, and every disagreement about the work follows them home to dinner. Last night they argued about the proper way to sort seeds until the fire went out, and then kept arguing in the dark.
Roles: partner 1: 18+, researcher | partner 2: 18+, researcher, partner of the first | head researcher: 18+, highest Research
Approaches: Talk Away from the Hut | Spend a Day with No Work at All | Ask the Head Researcher
Outcome pool:
- On the beach they each explain how the work is wearing on them, and saying it takes the sting out. A rule: no seeds after sunset. [answers: Talk Away from the Hut] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: none]
- One is too tired and too cross to talk yet. They watch the waves in silence, which is exactly what they both needed. [answers: Talk Away from the Hut] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: none]
- Swimming, fishing, napping, and not one word about seeds. The next day they sort by size AND colour. It takes twice as long. Nobody minds. [answers: Spend a Day with No Work at All] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
- One wants to study plants, the other the stars. Maybe they don't need to work in the same hut. [answers: Spend a Day with No Work at All] [mood: sad] [EFFECT: none]
- "Work it out between you. And please, please do it somewhere other than my hut." They do. [answers: Ask the Head Researcher] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
- The head researcher says to sort by moon phase. United at last against a common enemy, the partners go home arm in arm, complaining. [answers: Ask the Head Researcher] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
Flavour lines:
- "By SIZE."
- The other researchers eat lunch somewhere else.
- Arguing in the dark after the fire went out.

NEW-168. The Friendship After No   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (name1) and (name2) two friends, both 18+, not close relatives (any sexes). (name3) a mutual friend: any villager 18+.
EVENT TEXT
(Name2) asked (name1) to the moonlight dance. (Name1) said no, kindly, honestly: (he/she) just didn't feel that way.
Now (name1) is terrified the friendship is over.
They have been avoiding each other at the well for a week. This is very difficult, because there is only one well. Yesterday they both arrived at exactly the same moment, froze, and then both turned and walked away in opposite directions, with empty jars. Today, (name1) waited behind a tree for twenty minutes until (name2) left. (Name2), it turned out, was waiting behind a different tree. How can (name1) save the friendship?
Choice A: Clear the Air in Private
Choice B: Go Fishing Like Old Times
Choice C: Talk to a Mutual Friend

CHOICE A: CLEAR THE AIR IN PRIVATE
First popup: (Name1) can't stand it anymore. (He/She) walks up to (name2)'s hut, knocks on the door post, and asks if they can talk...
Ending A1 -- WITHOUT ASKING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name1) explains how (he/she) feels: that (he/she) misses (name2), and hates this, and didn't say no because (he/she) doesn't care. (He/She) doesn't ask for anything in return. (Name2) listens, and then, slowly, smiles. "I miss you too. I've been drinking out of the stream for a week." They walk to the well together.
Ending A2 -- TIME APART. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name2) admits, honestly, that (he/she) is still hurt, and needs some time apart before things can go back to normal. (Name1) accepts that, though it stings. A few weeks later, (name2) nods to (him/her) at the well. Then says hello. Then, one day, waits for (him/her).

CHOICE B: GO FISHING LIKE OLD TIMES
First popup: (Name1) turns up at (name2)'s door with two fishing lines, and doesn't say anything at all. Just holds one out...
Ending B1 -- AGAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name2) looks at the line for a long moment, then takes it. They spend a quiet afternoon fishing off the rocks like they used to, not talking about the dance at all, and catching absolutely nothing. It's perfect. They decide to go again tomorrow.
Ending B2 -- DIFFERENT NOW. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They go fishing, but it isn't the same. Over the afternoon, they discover they want different things from each other now, even though they still care. It's a quiet walk home. They part with a hug at the path, and both know something has changed. But not everything.

CHOICE C: TALK TO A MUTUAL FRIEND
First popup: (Name1) goes to (name3), who is friends with them both, and asks for help...
Ending C1 -- NO SIDES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name3) listens to (name1), and later, to (name2), and doesn't take a side. Then (he/she) invites them both to dinner on the same night, without telling either of them. It's very awkward for about a minute. Then (name2) laughs, and it's all right.
Ending C2 -- MORE CONFUSING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name3)'s advice makes everything much more confusing. Somehow it involves a goat, a misunderstanding from six years ago, and a theory about the moon. (Name1) thanks (him/her), and follows (his/her) own judgment, which is to go and knock on (name2)'s door.

MIXER SEED NEW-168
Premise: A villager kindly said no to a friend's invitation to the moonlight dance, and is now terrified the friendship is over. They have been avoiding each other for a week at the only well, hiding behind different trees.
Roles: friend 1: 18+ | friend 2: 18+, not a close relative | mutual friend: 18+
Approaches: Clear the Air in Private | Go Fishing Like Old Times | Talk to a Mutual Friend
Outcome pool:
- "I miss you too. I've been drinking out of the stream for a week." They walk to the well together. [answers: Clear the Air in Private] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
- The friend is still hurt and needs time apart. Weeks later, a nod at the well. Then hello. Then, one day, waiting for them. [answers: Clear the Air in Private] [mood: sad] [EFFECT: none]
- A quiet afternoon fishing off the rocks like they used to, catching absolutely nothing. It's perfect. [answers: Go Fishing Like Old Times] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: none]
- It isn't the same; they want different things from each other now. Something has changed. But not everything. [answers: Go Fishing Like Old Times] [mood: sad] [EFFECT: none]
- The mutual friend invites them both to dinner on the same night without telling either. Very awkward for about a minute. Then it's all right. [answers: Talk to a Mutual Friend] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
- The mutual friend's advice involves a goat, a misunderstanding from six years ago and a theory about the moon. [answers: Talk to a Mutual Friend] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
Flavour lines:

- Waiting behind a tree. The other is waiting behind a different tree.
- Two fishing lines held out without a word.

NEW-169. The Old Couple's Walk   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (name1) and (name2) an elderly couple: both elders, partners as the game records it. (grandchild name) one of their grandchildren, or any younger villager 10+ if they have none.
EVENT TEXT
Every evening for forty years, (name1) and (name2) have walked the same route along the shore. Every evening for forty years, they have argued about which rock is the halfway rock. (Name1) says it's the big flat one. (Name2) says it's the pointy one with the barnacles. Neither has ever given in. It is, the whole village agrees, the most romantic argument on the island.
Lately, the walk has been getting slower. They turn back a little earlier each week. Neither of them says anything about it. They just argue a little louder about the rock. Their family has noticed. Should someone say something?
Choice A: Let Them Talk on the Way
Choice B: Walk the Old Route Together
Choice C: Ask Their Grandchildren

CHOICE A: LET THEM TALK ON THE WAY
First popup: One evening, about halfway to either rock, (name1) stops walking...
Ending A1 -- GETTING HARD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"It's getting hard," (name1) says at last. "The walk." (He/She) doesn't ask (name2) to give it up. (He/She) just says it. (Name2) is quiet for a moment, then takes (his/her) arm. "It's getting hard for me too." They stand there together, and somehow, saying it makes the walk home easier.
Ending A2 -- A SHORTER WAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name2) admits (he/she) would rather walk a shorter way now. (Name1) grumbles, a little, but accepts it. They start turning back at a nearer rock, and immediately begin arguing about whether THAT is the new halfway rock. Nobody is surprised.

CHOICE B: WALK THE OLD ROUTE TOGETHER
First popup: On a good evening, when neither of them is too stiff, they set off on the full route, slowly, taking all the time in the world...
Ending B1 -- THE HALFWAY ROCK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They enjoy a slow walk all the way to the halfway rock, whichever one it is, and sit on it to watch the sunset, holding hands. "Same time tomorrow?" "Same time tomorrow." The argument about the rock resumes on the way home, with great affection.
Ending B2 -- LONG AND SHORT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Along the way, they discover that one of them wants to keep the long walk and the other really needs the short one. They talk about it more honestly than they have in years. They wouldn't trade each other for anything. They agree to try walking separately part of the way, and meeting at the rock. Either rock.

CHOICE C: ASK THEIR GRANDCHILDREN
First popup: The couple put the question of the walk to (grandchild name), who is delighted to be asked anything by grown-ups...
Ending C1 -- LISTENING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Grandchild name) listens to them both very seriously, and does not tell them what to do. Instead, (he/she) asks to come with them on the walk the next evening. And the next. The walk slows down even more, because (grandchild name) stops to look at every crab. Nobody minds at all.
Ending C2 -- A RACE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Grandchild name)'s suggestion is to settle the halfway rock question once and for all with a race. This is not helpful, so the couple follow their own judgment. But they do, privately, consider the race for a moment.

MIXER SEED NEW-169
Premise: Every evening for forty years, an elderly couple have walked the same route along the shore, arguing about which rock is the halfway rock. Lately the walk has been getting slower, and they turn back a little earlier each week.
Roles: partner 1: any elder | partner 2: any elder, partner of the first | grandchild: 10+
Approaches: Let Them Talk on the Way | Walk the Old Route Together | Ask Their Grandchildren
Outcome pool:
- "It's getting hard. The walk." "It's getting hard for me too." Somehow saying it makes the walk home easier. [answers: Let Them Talk on the Way] [mood: sad] [EFFECT: none]
- They start turning back at a nearer rock, and immediately begin arguing about whether THAT is the new halfway rock. [answers: Let Them Talk on the Way] [mood: funny] [EFFECT: none]
- A slow walk all the way to the halfway rock, whichever one it is, and the sunset, holding hands. "Same time tomorrow?" [answers: Walk the Old Route Together] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: none]
- One wants the long walk and one needs the short one; they walk separately part of the way and meet at the rock. Either rock. [answers: Walk the Old Route Together] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: none]
- The grandchild asks to come on the walk, and stops to look at every crab. Nobody minds at all. [answers: Ask Their Grandchildren] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: none]

Flavour lines:

- The most romantic argument on the island.

NEW-170. The Newcomer's Choice   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (name1) a newcomer: any villager 18+ who joined the village recently (an adult who arrived as a new villager, or any adult if none). (name2) a local villager 18+, unpartnered, not a close relative. (name3) a villager who once arrived as a newcomer too: any villager 25+.
EVENT TEXT
(Name1) arrived in the dry season, with one bag and no plans. (He/She) has been helping out, finding (his/her) feet, never quite unpacking.
And (he/she) has caught (name2)'s eye. The feeling might even be mutual. They keep ending up at the same fire, laughing at the same jokes, walking back the long way.
But (name1) still hasn't decided whether to stay on the island at all. (His/Her) bag is still packed by the door. Both of them know it. Neither of them has mentioned it. Should (name1) say something, or decide about the island first?
Choice A: Speak Plainly by the Shore
Choice B: Show the Newcomer the Island
Choice C: Ask Someone Who Settled Here

CHOICE A: SPEAK PLAINLY BY THE SHORE
First popup: One evening, on the beach, (name1) stops and turns to (name2). "I need to say something. Before I lose my nerve."...
Ending A1 -- NO ANSWER NEEDED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name1) explains how (he/she) feels, about (name2), and about the island, and about the bag by the door, without asking (name2) for an answer. "I just didn't want you to have to guess." (Name2) is quiet for a while. Then says, "Unpack the bag." (Name1) laughs, and doesn't say yes. But (he/she) doesn't say no.
Ending A2 -- NOT QUITE THE SAME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name2) doesn't feel quite the same way, and says so, kindly. (Name1) accepts it. It's hard, but somehow it makes things simpler. A week later, (name1) unpacks the bag anyway. "Not because of you," (he/she) tells (name2). "Because of the island."

CHOICE B: SHOW THE NEWCOMER THE ISLAND
First popup: (Name2) decides that if (name1) is going to make a choice about the island, (he/she) should at least see the best of it first...
Ending B1 -- THE BEST SPOTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They spend the afternoon exploring the island's best spots: the waterfall pool, the cliff where the birds nest, the beach where the sand squeaks. At the end of the day, sitting on the cliff, (name1) admits (he/she) has never seen anywhere so beautiful. They decide to meet again tomorrow. The bag stays packed, but only just.
Ending B2 -- DIFFERENT LIVES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It's a wonderful day. But as they talk, they find they want different things from life: (name2) will never leave the island, and (name1) is not sure (he/she) can ever stay anywhere. They like each other a lot. That doesn't change the rest.

CHOICE C: ASK SOMEONE WHO SETTLED HERE
First popup: (Name1) goes to (name3), who also arrived here once with nothing, and stayed...
Ending C1 -- LEAVES IT TO THEM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name3) listens, nodding, remembering. "I kept my bag packed for two years," (he/she) says. "Then one day I needed something out of it, and I just never put it back." (He/She) leaves the decision to (name1). That night, (name1) takes one thing out of the bag.
Ending C2 -- THE FISHING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name3)'s advice is entirely about how good the fishing is. The lagoon fishing. The reef fishing. The fishing off the rocks at dawn. It goes on for an hour. It's not very helpful, so (name1) follows (his/her) own judgment. But (he/she) does go fishing at dawn, and it is very good.

Roles: newcomer: 18+, recently arrived | local: 18+, unpartnered, not a close relative | settled newcomer: 25+

- One will never leave the island, and one is not sure they can ever stay anywhere. Liking each other doesn't change the rest. [answers: Show the Newcomer the Island] [mood: sad] [EFFECT: none]

- Walking back the long way.

NEW-171. The Record Washed Away   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) the scholar who keeps the records: any villager 18+ (prefer the highest Research). (elder name) an old farmer: any elder.
EVENT TEXT
Somewhere in the night, the roof of the record hut sprang a leak. A small one. It dripped, patiently, for hours, directly onto the stack of bark sheets that hold the village's earliest harvest records: which crops failed, which thrived, which seasons brought rain and which brought hunger.
(Name) opens the door in the morning and freezes.
The charcoal marks are running down the sheets in long grey streaks, like tears. Whole seasons are dissolving in front of (his/her) eyes. The drip goes on dripping. (Name) is staring at it in horror, unable to decide what to grab first. What should (he/she) do?
Choice A: Rescue the Driest Sheets
Choice B: Ask the Oldest Farmers
Choice C: Start a Fresh Harvest Record

CHOICE A: RESCUE THE DRIEST SHEETS
First popup: (Name) snatches up the sheets that are still mostly dry and spreads them out in the sun, then sits down with fresh bark and charcoal and starts copying as fast as (his/her) hand will go...
Ending A1 -- SAVED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
(Name) copies the clearest sheets onto fresh bark before they can fade, working until (his/her) hand cramps and the sun goes down. Much is lost, but much is saved: planting times, crop rotations, a list of which seeds failed in the dry years. It's useful planting knowledge, kept safe for the village. (Name) moves the record hut's stack to a high, dry shelf that very night.
Ending A2 -- PULP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (large)
Before (name) can copy more than a few lines, the last readable sheets soften, sag, and dissolve into grey pulp in (his/her) hands. A great deal of old farming knowledge, generations of it, is lost for good. (Name) sits in the wet record hut for a long time, holding a handful of mush that used to be a hundred harvests.

CHOICE B: ASK THE OLDEST FARMERS
First popup: The records may be ruined, but the people who lived through those harvests aren't. (Name) goes to find (elder name) and the other oldest farmers...
Ending B1 -- THE FORGOTTEN TRICK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
(Name) sits the three oldest farmers down and has them tell everything they remember. Comparing their memories turns up a forgotten trick: planting just before the rains, not just after, so the seeds are already in the ground when the first storm hits. Nobody had done it in years. The farmers try it that season, and it works.
Ending B2 -- DISAGREEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The old farmers disagree about nearly everything. Was the famine year before the big storm or after? Did the yams fail or the taro? One of them insists it was the year of the purple sky, which nobody else remembers. Nobody pretends to know whose memory is right, and (name) writes down all three versions.

CHOICE C: START A FRESH HARVEST RECORD
First popup: (Name) decides that what's gone is gone. What matters is never letting this happen again...
Ending C1 -- CARVED BOARDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
The village starts a careful new harvest record, carved into wooden boards instead of written on bark, and kept under a sound new roof. Every season, the farmers gather to add what they've learned. It's a record that will last for generations, and a better one than the old: this time, they write down why.
Ending C2 -- BETTER UNWRITTEN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As the new record is begun, (name) pauses over one season: the famine year, when the old sheets recorded who went hungry and who didn't make it. (He/She) decides that some things are better left unwritten, and starts the new record with the year after. The families who remember are quietly grateful.

Roles: scholar: any villager 18+ | old farmer: any elder
Approaches: Rescue the Driest Sheets | Ask the Oldest Farmers | Start a Fresh Harvest Record
Outcome pool:
- The scholar copies the clearest sheets onto fresh bark until their hand cramps: planting times, crop rotations, which seeds failed in the dry years. [answers: Rescue the Driest Sheets] [mood: tense] [EFFECT: tech gain (small)]
- The last readable sheets dissolve into grey pulp, and generations of farming knowledge are lost for good. [answers: Rescue the Driest Sheets] [mood: sad] [EFFECT: tech loss (large)]

- A new harvest record carved into wooden boards under a sound roof, and this time they write down why. [answers: Start a Fresh Harvest Record] [mood: warm] [EFFECT: tech gain (normal)]

NEW-172. The Wrong Name   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) any villager 14+ (the name change replaces their first name only). (elder name) any elder.
EVENT TEXT
Years ago, (name) stopped using (his/her) childhood name. (He/She) chose a new one, the one everyone is supposed to call (him/her) now.
Half the village still uses the old one.
Especially the elders. Especially (elder name), who shouts it across the beach at the top of (his/her) voice, every morning, as if it's a tradition. This morning at the well, (name) heard the old name four times before breakfast. One of those times, it was from someone who wasn't even born when (he/she) changed it.
(Name) is standing by the well with (his/her) jar, very, very calm, the way a volcano is calm. Should (name) explain where the old name came from, or finally make everyone use the new one?
Choice A: Keep the Story of the Old Name
Choice B: Ask Who Gave the Old Name
Choice C: Announce the Chosen Name

CHOICE A: KEEP THE STORY OF THE OLD NAME
First popup: (Name) decides that if people are going to remember the old name, they might as well know where it came from. (He/She) gathers a few curious listeners and explains...
Ending A1 -- THE FISHING KNOT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The old name, it turns out, came from an old word for a fishing knot, one so old that nobody uses it anymore. (Name) shows them the knot, the way (his/her) grandmother taught it. It's a good knot, a strong one, and the fishers are delighted. The knot is written down so the village doesn't lose it, and somehow, now that it belongs to the knot, people start using the old name less.
Ending A2 -- THE CRUMBLING SHEET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (small)
The only bark sheet explaining the village's old naming customs, and where names like (name)'s came from, is fetched from the record hut. It's so old and dry that it crumbles while it is being copied, and that bit of old knowledge is lost. (Name) is sad about it, which surprises (him/her).

CHOICE B: ASK WHO GAVE THE OLD NAME
First popup: (Name) goes to (his/her) relatives, and to (elder name), and asks who gave (him/her) the old name in the first place, and why...
Ending B1 -- A NICKNAME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The relatives' stories reveal something nobody remembered: the old name began as a nickname, given by a great-uncle because baby (name) wouldn't let go of his fishing line. It was never meant to be permanent. It's a forgotten detail about how names were once given in the village, and the record keepers write it down. (Elder name), hearing the story, looks thoughtful.
Ending B2 -- NO AGREEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The relatives can't agree on why the name was given. One says it was a great-uncle's idea. One says it was a dream. One says it was a mistake, and the baby was supposed to be called something else entirely. Nobody pretends to know, and (name) gives up.

CHOICE C: ANNOUNCE THE CHOSEN NAME

NEW-173. The Name Lost to Magic   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) any villager 14+ (not a special named role). (friend name) a friend of (name): any villager 14+.
EVENT TEXT

This morning, (name) woke up, and couldn't remember (his/her) own name.
Not for a moment, like everyone does sometimes. Properly. (He/She) knows (his/her) family, (his/her) hut, (his/her) favourite food. But when (friend name) asks, gently, "What's your name?", (name) opens (his/her) mouth, and nothing comes. Only pieces. The first sound, maybe.

Choice B: Ask Their Friends to Remember
Choice C: Carve Every Name Somewhere Safe

Ending B2 -- NO AGREEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

NEW-174. The Family Recipe   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) the family's cook: any villager 18+. Needs at least one grave (the grandmother's; flavour only).
EVENT TEXT
Every feast for as long as anyone can remember, (name)'s grandmother made her famous coconut and taro pudding. It was sweet and smooth and smoky, and people walked from the far side of the island for a bowl.
She died last season. And it turns out she never taught anyone the recipe.
(Name) has tried to make it four times since. The first attempt tasted like wet sand. The second tasted like dry sand. The third exploded. The fourth was eaten by the dog, who was then sick.
The feast is in three days. How can (name) bring the recipe back in time?
Choice A: Write Down What Is Remembered
Choice B: Ask Her Old Friends
Choice C: Start a Recipe Board

CHOICE A: WRITE DOWN WHAT IS REMEMBERED
First popup: (Name) gathers the whole family together, and asks everyone to say everything they remember about watching Grandmother cook...
Ending A1 -- STEP BY STEP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Bit by bit, the steps come back: grate the coconut fresh, never dried; wrap the taro in leaves; cook it in the ground, not the pot. (Name) writes down every step the family can recall, and the pudding, on the fifth try, tastes almost right. It's useful cooking knowledge, saved for the village, and the dog is allowed a very small bowl.
Ending A2 -- SCRUBBED AWAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (small)
Someone remembers that Grandmother used to scratch little marks on the wall beside her cooking spot. They run to look, and find the wall freshly scrubbed clean by a well-meaning cousin, "to tidy up." The marks were the recipe. That part of it is lost, and the cousin is very, very sorry.

CHOICE B: ASK HER OLD FRIENDS
First popup: (Name) goes to Grandmother's oldest friends, the women she cooked beside at every feast for fifty years...
Ending B1 -- A PINCH OF ASH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Her old friends laugh. "You don't know about the ash?" She always added a pinch of ash from the cooking fire to the pot, right at the end. That was where the smoky taste came from. It was the detail everyone had missed. (Name) adds it to the fifth pudding, and the first spoonful makes (him/her) cry.
Ending B2 -- DISAGREEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Her old friends disagree about the recipe. One says honey. One says no honey, never honey. One says it was the leaves, and another says it was the love, which doesn't help at all. Nobody pretends to be sure, and the fifth pudding tastes like slightly sweeter sand.

CHOICE C: START A RECIPE BOARD
First popup: (Name) decides this must never happen to any family again. (He/She) proposes a carved board of every family's recipes...
Ending C1 -- THE RECIPE BOARD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
The village starts a carved board of family recipes, kept in the cooking hut, a careful record for future generations. Every family adds their best dish. The board fills up fast, and the cooks learn a great deal from each other. At the top, in pride of place, is "Grandmother's Pudding (almost)."
Ending C2 -- SECRETS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As the board fills up, (name) realizes some of Grandmother's secrets should stay secret, kept in the family, the way she would have wanted. (He/She) leaves the pudding off the board. Some things should only be learned standing beside someone at the fire.

NEW-175. The Child's First Word   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) a proud parent: any villager 18+ with a young child (under 3) or a baby. The baby is flavour only and is never changed.
EVENT TEXT
(Name)'s baby has said a first word!

Nobody else seems to have heard it.
(Name) has scratched it onto a strip of bark with berry ink, along with the day and the time, and has told everyone in the village. The baby, meanwhile, has refused to say it again. Or anything else. When people crowd around saying "fish? fish?" the baby just looks at them with an expression of enormous smugness. (Name) wants the village to believe it. What should (he/she) do?
Choice A: Keep the Bark Safe
Choice B: Ask Who Else Was There
Choice C: Begin a First Words Board

Ending A2 -- THE DOWNPOUR. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (small)

NEW-176. The Unfinished Portrait   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) an artist: any villager 18+. Needs at least one grave (the sitter's; flavour only).
EVENT TEXT
Clearing out an old hut, (name) finds a roll of bark cloth tucked into the rafters. Unrolled, it's a portrait: a villager who died long ago, painted by an artist nobody can name.
It's only half finished. The painter did the eyes, and one ear, and then stopped. The rest is bare cloth.
But the eyes. The eyes are very, very good. They look straight out of the cloth, warm and amused and alive, as if the person is about to say something. Several villagers have looked at it and had to sit down. What should (name) do with it?
Choice A: Restore the Faded Paint
Choice B: Ask Those Who Knew the Sitter
Choice C: Finish It for the Future

CHOICE A: RESTORE THE FADED PAINT
First popup: (Name) sits with the portrait for days, studying every flake of paint under a magnifying shell, trying to work out how it was made...
Ending A1 -- THE PIGMENT MIX. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
From the tiny flakes, (name) works out the old painter's pigment mix: red earth, crushed shell, burnt coconut husk and something oily that might be fish. (He/She) copies the recipe down, and tries it. The colours are richer than anything the village has used before. It's a useful method, and the village's painters, potters and dyers all start using it.
Ending A2 -- THE TEAR. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (small)
While (name) is cleaning the cloth, very gently, it tears, right across the bottom. Flakes of paint shower onto the floor. The old painter's brushwork is lost, and along with it, everything it could have taught. The eyes, thank goodness, survive. They seem to look at (name) a little reproachfully.

CHOICE B: ASK THOSE WHO KNEW THE SITTER
First popup: (Name) shows the portrait to the oldest villagers, to see if anyone remembers the sitter, or the painter...
Ending B1 -- BY FIRELIGHT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
An old man looks at it for a long time, then laughs, wiping his eyes. He remembers the painter, a strange, quiet woman, who only ever worked at night, by firelight. That explains the colours, which looked wrong in daylight. It's a forgotten detail, and (name) learns something useful about how light changes paint.
Ending B2 -- NOBODY AGREES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nobody agrees on what the sitter looked like. One says the nose was big. One says it was small. One says that isn't the sitter at all, it's the painter's cousin. Nobody pretends to know, and the eyes look on, amused.

CHOICE C: FINISH IT FOR THE FUTURE
First popup: (Name) decides that the portrait deserves to be finished. (He/She) asks everyone who knew the sitter to describe them...
Ending C1 -- THE HUT OF PORTRAITS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
The artist finishes the portrait from the villagers' memories, slowly, carefully, over a whole season. When it's done, the sitter's great-grandchildren come to see it, and cry. It's so well received that (name) starts painting other villagers, and soon there's a whole hut of portraits, a careful record of the village's faces for future generations.
Ending C2 -- UNFINISHED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) picks up the brush. Puts it down. Picks it up again. And decides, in the end, that the portrait should stay unfinished, as the painter left it, and private. It goes back into the rafters, rolled up safe. Only the eyes were ever meant to be seen, (name) thinks.

NEW-177. The Two Histories   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (name1) and (name2) two arguing villagers, any 18+. (scholar name) the record keeper: any villager 18+ (prefer high Research), never the two.
EVENT TEXT
For three days now, (name1) and (name2) have been arguing about the great fire of long ago, the one that burned down half the old village.
(Name1) says the records are right: lightning started it. It's written down. It's official.
(Name2) says (his/her) grandfather swore, on his deathbed, that it was a cooking pot left on the coals by someone who went for a swim.
They have been arguing at breakfast. At lunch. At the well. In the middle of the night, from their separate huts, shouting across the village. Both of them are getting very loud, and (scholar name) is being asked, increasingly desperately, to settle it. How should (scholar name) settle it?
Choice A: Copy the Old Fire Record
Choice B: Gather the Grandparents' Stories
Choice C: Record Both Versions

CHOICE A: COPY THE OLD FIRE RECORD
First popup: (Scholar name) fetches the ancient bark record of the fire, and unrolls it very, very carefully, with (name1) and (name2) breathing down (his/her) neck...
Ending A1 -- HOW THEY REBUILT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The record does say lightning. But it also describes, in detail, how the village rebuilt afterward: wider gaps between huts, fire breaks, water jars by every door. (Scholar name) copies all of it onto fresh bark, saving useful knowledge that the village had half forgotten. (Name1) is triumphant. (Name2) points out that the record was written by someone who wasn't there.
Ending A2 -- CRACKED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (small)
The old record is so dry that it cracks apart as it is unrolled, splitting into pieces that crumble at the edges. A fragile part of the history is lost, including, ironically, the part that said what started the fire. (Name1) and (name2) stare at the pieces. Then at each other. Then, for the first time in three days, they're both quiet.

CHOICE B: GATHER THE GRANDPARENTS' STORIES
First popup: (Scholar name) visits every elder whose family lived through the fire, and writes down every version...
Ending B1 -- BOTH HALF RIGHT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Comparing all the stories turns up a detail everyone had missed: the fire started near the cooking hut, during a lightning storm. Lightning struck the cooking hut. Where, yes, someone had left a pot on the coals. Both sides were half right. (Name1) and (name2) are both furious, and then both laugh, and then go and eat lunch together.
Ending B2 -- CONTRADICTIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The grandparents' stories contradict each other completely: lightning, a cooking pot, a dropped torch, an angry spirit, and one great-aunt who insists there was no fire at all. Nobody pretends to know the truth. (Name1) and (name2) keep arguing, but now there are seven sides.

CHOICE C: RECORD BOTH VERSIONS
First popup: (Scholar name) declares that the village will keep both versions, side by side, and let the future decide...
Ending C1 -- FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
The village writes down both versions side by side, carefully, with the names of who told each one, a careful record for future generations to argue about. In the writing of it, (scholar name) works out a better way of keeping records: always noting who said what, and how they knew. (Name1) and (name2) both sign their versions, with a flourish.
Ending C2 -- THE FAMILIES' STORY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As (scholar name) writes, an old woman comes to ask that some parts of the story be left out: the parts about which families lost people, and who was blamed afterwards. (Scholar name) decides those parts should stay private to the families involved. (Name1) and (name2), hearing why, quietly stop arguing.
