Ending C1 -- SILENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Strangely, instead of getting hotter, the stone cools. By midday it's as cold as river water, and silent. No whispers, nothing. It stays that way. (Name) is almost disappointed. It's just a stone now. (He/She) uses it as a doorstop.
Ending C2 -- THE MAP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As the sun beats down on it, a faint pattern of lines appears on the stone's surface, like rivers on a map. The researchers copy the lines down before they fade. One river seems to end very close to the village, at a spot where there is no river. Yet. Or anymore. Nobody's sure which.

CHOICE D: RETURN IT TO THE HEARTH
First popup: (Name) decides the stone belongs where it was found. (He/She) sets it back in the fire pit, right where it sat for years...
Ending D1 -- A COOKING STONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The whispers stop the moment it's back in its old place. After that, it's just a good, solid cooking stone, holding up pots for the family who uses that fire pit. Sometimes, when the stew is bubbling, they say it sounds like someone humming.
Ending D2 -- THE DREAM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
That night, (name) dreams of the family who once lived around that hearth: a mother stirring a pot, a father mending a net, children chasing a dog around the fire. Nobody in the dream speaks to (name). They don't seem to know (he/she) is there. It's a warm, happy dream, and (name) wakes up missing people (he/she) never met.

MY-034. The Two Identical Travelers   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

EVENT TEXT
Two strangers walk into the village on the same morning, one from the east path and one from the west. Both wear a blue wrap with a frayed hem. Both carry a walking stick with a notch near the top. Both have the very same face, right down to the little scar on the chin.
They stop in the middle of the village and stare at each other. "Who are you?" they both say at once. Each insists they have never met the other in their lives. Both tilt their heads the very same way when puzzled. The whole village is watching, and somehow (name) has ended up standing right between them. What should (he/she) do?

Choice A: Invite Both to Stay
Choice B: Ask About Their Histories
Choice C: Let Them Meet Privately
Choice D: Consult a Storyteller

{#made:Only one stays; the other camps nearby|They both stay}. They choose different names. One takes up net-making, the other gardening, and they live at opposite ends of the village. They never quite become friends, but every morning they wave to each other across the village, the very same wave, at the very same moment. After a while, everyone stops finding it strange. Mostly.
Ending A2 -- ONE GOES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In the morning, one of them is gone. No goodbye, no footprints, just an empty sleeping mat. The other one is pale and shaken. "I dreamed I was walking away," the one who stayed whispers. CHOICE B: ASK ABOUT THEIR HISTORIES

Ending B1 -- THE LULLABY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Their stories are different in every detail: different villages, different families, different lives. Nothing matches. Until (name) asks, on a whim, what song their mothers sang to them. Both of them start humming the very same lullaby, at the very same time, then stop and stare at each other in horror. Neither of them sleeps that night.
Ending B2 -- THE STORM FROM BOTH SHORES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They both tell the story of a great storm when they were small, a storm that tore their villages apart. One saw it from the eastern shore of a far island. The other saw it from the western shore. Same storm, same night, same terror, opposite sides. "Maybe you were twins," someone suggests. "Separated by the storm." Both travelers look at each other for a long, long time.

CHOICE C: LET THEM MEET PRIVATELY
First popup: "This is between the two of you," (name) says, and shoos everyone else away. The two travelers step into an empty hut together, and the door closes...
Ending C1 -- THEY LAUGH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
For a long time, there's silence. Then laughter. Loud, helpless, wheezing laughter, from both of them. When they finally come out, wiping their eyes, they refuse to explain anything at all. "You wouldn't believe us," they say, and set off together down the north path, arm in arm, still giggling.
Ending C2 -- ONLY ONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
After an hour, the door opens, and only one of them comes out. "The other one took the western path," the traveler says calmly. There's no back door to the hut. The western path is muddy after last night's rain, and only one set of footprints leads away along it. The traveler who remains thanks everyone and leaves by the east path, and no one stops (him/her).

CHOICE D: CONSULT A STORYTELLER
First popup: (Name) fetches (name2), the village's best storyteller, who looks from one traveler to the other with great interest...
Ending D1 -- THE OLD TALE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"There's an old tale like this," (name2) says. "A man walks so far from home that he meets himself coming back. One of them is who he was. One is who he will be." The travelers both shiver. That night, one sleeps in the east hut and one in the west, and in the morning both are gone, walking in opposite directions.
Ending D2 -- NOT PROOF. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Resemblance is not proof of magic," (name2) says briskly. "I've seen cousins who look more alike than these two." The travelers seem relieved, and so does the village. Still, after they leave, nobody can explain the scar, or the notch in the stick, or that tilt of the head. The mystery remains, quietly, in everyone's mind.

MY-036. The Empty Seat at the Feast   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older. (child), the hungry child in Ending A2, is a villager under 14 (story only, no effect).
EVENT TEXT
The whole village is gathered for the feast, and the food is piled high on banana leaves all around the fire. In the middle of the laughter and chatter, (name) notices something odd. There's an extra place set at the end of the row: a fresh banana leaf heaped with food and a cup of coconut milk. Nobody is sitting there.
"Who set that?" (name) asks. Nobody knows. Nobody remembers doing it. And every time (name) looks back at it, there's a little less food on the leaf than before. What should (he/she) do?

Choice A: Leave the Seat Undisturbed
Choice B: Invite the Unseen Guest
Choice C: Watch the Plate
Choice D: Remove the Setting

CHOICE A: LEAVE THE SEAT UNDISTURBED
First popup: (Name) decides it's not (his/her) place to clear someone else's seat, whoever they are. (He/She) goes back to (his/her) own food, trying not to stare...
Ending A1 -- EMPTY BY MORNING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The feast goes on late into the night. In the morning, the extra leaf is spotless, licked clean, and the cup is dry. Nobody saw anyone eat. Nobody heard a thing. The villagers quietly wonder about it for a long time, and at the next feast, without anyone saying a word, somebody sets an extra place again.
Ending A2 -- THE STICKY CULPRIT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Later in the evening, (child), very small and very sticky, is found sitting behind the cooking pots with an entire mango in each hand and a coconut-milk moustache. (Child) had set the extra place "for the spirits" and then got hungry waiting for them. (Child) looks extremely guilty. Everyone laughs until they cry, and (child) gets a second mango.

CHOICE B: INVITE THE UNSEEN GUEST
First popup: (Name) stands up, faces the empty seat, and says loudly, "Whoever you are, you're welcome at our fire. Eat, and be our guest."...
Ending B1 -- THE BRIGHTER TORCHES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
For a moment, everything goes quiet. Then a soft, warm breeze passes through the gathering, stirring hair and leaves, and every torch around the feast flares up brighter, all at once. People gasp, then cheer. It's the best feast anyone can remember, and nobody can quite explain why everyone feels so happy.
Ending B2 -- THE TRAVELER IN THE DARK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Thank you," says a voice from the dark, and a tired traveler steps hesitantly into the firelight. The traveler had been standing at the edge of the trees for an hour, too shy to ask to join. The traveler gratefully takes the empty seat, eats every scrap, and tells funny stories until the fire dies. Nobody ever finds out who set the place.

CHOICE C: WATCH THE PLATE

Ending C1 -- THE FRUIT BAT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
For ages, nothing. Then (name) glances away for half a second, and there's a flapping of leathery wings: a fruit bat swoops down from the trees, grabs a whole mango off the leaf and flaps off into the night, squeaking with triumph. (Name) leaps up, shouting. Everyone laughs. It's been doing it all evening, apparently.

CHOICE D: REMOVE THE SETTING

Ending D1 -- NORMAL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D2 -- AT THE DOOR. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-038. The Sea's Three Warnings   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
(Name) is mending a canoe on the beach when a stranger walks up out of the surf, barefoot and soaking, with seaweed tangled in (his/her) hair, as if (he/she) had just strolled out of the waves.
"The sea will give you three signs," the stranger says, very seriously. "Three. And after the third, it will take something back." Then the stranger just stands there, dripping, waiting to see what (name) will do. The sea behind (him/her) is calm and blue. What should (name) do?

Choice A: Watch the Tides
Choice B: Ask What Will Be Taken
Choice C: Ignore the Warning
Choice D: Share the Warning

CHOICE A: WATCH THE TIDES
First popup: (Name) sits up on the dunes for three days, watching the sea for signs. The other villagers think (he/she) has lost (his/her) mind...
Ending A1 -- THREE WAVES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the third day, three strange waves arrive, one after the other, far bigger than anything else that day, rolling up the sand in long, foaming lines. (Name) leaps up, braced for the worst. And then... nothing. The sea goes calm again. No storm, no flood, no disaster. (Name) sits back down, very confused, and eventually goes home for supper.
Ending A2 -- THE BASKETS SAVED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
On the third day, the sea goes strangely still, and pulls back from the shore. (Name) doesn't wait for anything else. (He/She) races down and hauls every basket of dried fish and stored food up the beach, yelling for help. CHOICE B: ASK WHAT WILL BE TAKEN

Ending B1 -- ONLY WHAT WAS BORROWED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger looks at (name) with deep, calm eyes. "Only what was borrowed," (he/she) says. Then the stranger turns and walks back into the surf, and keeps walking, until the waves close over (his/her) head. (Name) runs down to the water's edge, but there's nothing there. Ending B2 -- THE PROVERB. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE C: IGNORE THE WARNING

Ending C1 -- THE RED-STRIPED BASKET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)

Ending C2 -- NOTHING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nothing happens. Not that day, not the next, not that whole season. No signs, no waves, nothing taken. The warning fades into memory, and (name) forgets all about it, until one day years later (he/she) catches (himself/herself) saying it to a child: "The sea gives three signs, you know..."

CHOICE D: SHARE THE WARNING

Ending D1 -- READY FOR ANYTHING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The village takes it seriously. Canoes are dragged up above the tideline and tied down, nets are brought in, stores are moved to higher ground. Ending D2 -- THE SCARY RUMOR. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-042. The Broken Seal   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
Clearing land for a new garden, (name) hacks through the roots of an ancient tree and finds a box tangled deep inside them, wrapped in roots as thick as (his/her) arms. The lid is sealed with dark resin stamped with a sun sinking into a wave.
Scratched into the lid are a few words: 'Do not open until the last light.' (Name) has no idea what the last light means. Sunset? The end of the world? The researchers are arguing about it already, and the children want it opened right now. What should (name) do?

Choice A: Open It at Sunset
Choice B: Open It at Noon
Choice C: Wait Until Night
Choice D: Leave It for Its Owner

CHOICE A: OPEN IT AT SUNSET
First popup: (Name) waits until the very last sliver of sun slips beneath the sea, and then, with the whole village watching, breaks the seal...
Ending A1 -- THE EXPEDITION RECORD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
Inside, wrapped in oiled cloth, is a stack of bark sheets covered in drawings and marks: a record of an old expedition across the island, long before the village was founded. Maps, sketches of plants and animals, notes on where to find water. The researchers stay up all night reading by torchlight, and they learn more about the island in a week than they have in years. Your villagers gain (award) tech points.
Ending A2 -- THE GLOWING CLOUD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The lid lifts, and out drifts a cloud of tiny glowing insects, hundreds of them, rising slowly into the evening air like sparks from a fire. They don't bite. They don't sting. They just float up, and up, and scatter among the treetops, twinkling, until the whole forest edge looks like it's full of stars. The children are speechless. The box is empty.

CHOICE B: OPEN IT AT NOON
First popup: "Last light, first light, who cares? Let's just open it," (name) says impatiently, and cracks the seal in the full blaze of midday...
Ending B1 -- THE NOTE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Inside are three ordinary river stones and a small piece of bark with a note on it. (Name) unfolds it. It reads, in neat old script: "Why couldn't you wait?" Everyone laughs. (Name) does not. (He/She) goes rather pink and puts the stones back in the box.
Ending B2 -- THE BITTER SMELL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: ILL (loses health)
The seal breaks with a hiss, and a sharp, sour smell bursts out from whatever has rotted inside, so strong it makes everyone's eyes water. (Name), who was leaning right over it, gets a full lungful and staggers back, coughing. By evening (he/she) is laid up in the healers' hut with a pounding headache and a churning stomach, and stays there for several days. The healers close the box with a stick and bury it far, far away.

CHOICE C: WAIT UNTIL NIGHT
First popup: (Name) decides 'last light' means the very last light of all, the end of the night. (He/She) sits up with the box under the stars, waiting...
Ending C1 -- THE SILVER SHELL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Just before dawn, when the last stars are fading, (name) tries the lid, and it opens easily, the seal crumbling away like dust. Inside, on a bed of soft moss, lies a single shell that shines silver in the starlight, smooth as a mirror. It's the most beautiful thing (name) has ever seen. (He/She) has no idea what it's for, and decides it doesn't need to be for anything.
Ending C2 -- STILL LOCKED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) waits all night. (He/She) tries the lid at midnight, and before dawn, and at every hour in between. It won't budge. And as the sun rises, (name) notices that the words on the lid are harder to read than they were yesterday, fading, as if the box is slowly forgetting what it says. Maybe (he/she) got it wrong. Maybe it'll never open.

CHOICE D: LEAVE IT FOR ITS OWNER
First popup: (Name) decides this box was hidden on purpose by someone, and isn't (his/hers) to open. (He/She) wraps it in cloth and leaves it in a safe place...
Ending D1 -- CLAIMED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
A few weeks later, a traveler arrives asking about a box buried in the roots of a great tree, an old family keepsake left by a great-great-grandparent. The traveler is overjoyed to find it safe and unopened, and thanks the village again and again for respecting it. "Not everyone would have waited," the traveler says.
Ending D2 -- YEARS PASS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nobody comes. The box sits on its shelf, wrapped in cloth, through one season, then another, then another. Years pass. Children grow up asking about it. (Name) grows older and still doesn't open it. It becomes part of the village, a promise kept to someone nobody knows.

MY-043. The Road of Returning Steps   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older; (name2), in Choice B, is (name)'s friend, another eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
Walking home after dark, (name) passes a tall paperbark tree with a peeling white trunk. A few minutes later, there it is again, its pale shape looming up ahead. (Name) frowns and walks on. A few minutes later: the same tree. Same peeling bark. Same crooked branch.
(Name) turns left. Turns right. Walks straight, very straight, counting steps. Every single time, the pale tree looms up out of the dark in front of (him/her), as if it's waiting. The village fires are visible through the trees, so close (name) can smell the smoke. What should (he/she) do?

Choice A: Mark the Path
Choice B: Walk with a Friend
Choice C: Wait for Dawn
Choice D: Follow a Different Landmark

CHOICE A: MARK THE PATH
First popup: (Name) pulls a strip of cloth from (his/her) wrap, ties it to a branch beside the tree, and sets off again, tying strips as (he/she) goes...
Ending A1 -- THE LOOP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
By the third time around, the strips of cloth tell the story: the path splits in the dark into three trails that curve around and meet again, and there are two paperbark trees, almost identical, at the two ends. (Name) has been going in circles all along. (He/She) finds the way home at last and draws a careful map for the researchers, who learn a lot about how easy it is to get lost, and how to mark trails properly. Your villagers gain (award) tech points.
Ending A2 -- THE WRONG SIDE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) walks a big circle and comes back to the tree. (His/Her) cloth strip is there, tied to the branch. On the wrong side. (He/She) tied it on the left. It's on the right. (Name) tries again, very carefully, tying the strip on the left and checking it twice. When (he/she) comes back, it's on the right again. (Name) sits down at the foot of the tree and stays there until (his/her) knees stop shaking.

CHOICE B: WALK WITH A FRIEND
First popup: (Name) shouts for help toward the village, and after a while (name2) comes crashing through the undergrowth with a torch, grumbling...
Ending B1 -- JUST A TREE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Honestly," (name2) says, linking arms with (name). "It's just a tree. Come on." And they walk home together, past the paperbark, straight to the village, in no time at all. (Name2) laughs about it all the way home. And for once, the tree really is just a tree.
Ending B2 -- BOTH LOST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Honestly," (name2) says. "It's just a tree." Ten minutes later, (name2) stops. "That's... the same tree." The two of them walk in circles until their torch burns out, both swearing that they walked dead straight, until they finally give up and huddle together at the foot of the paperbark, waiting for morning. They never tell anyone how scared they were.

CHOICE C: WAIT FOR DAWN
First popup: (Name) gives up. (He/She) sits down with (his/her) back against the paperbark, wraps (his/her) arms around (his/her) knees, and waits for the sun...
Ending C1 -- EASY IN DAYLIGHT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When the sun comes up, (name) feels very silly indeed. The path home is right there, plain as anything, and it's a three-minute walk. (He/She) sneaks back into the village yawning, hoping nobody noticed (he/she) was gone. Of course, everybody noticed.
Ending C2 -- THE FOOTPRINTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
At sunrise, (name) stands up, stiff and cold, and looks down at the path. There are footprints in the soft earth: (his/her) own, from walking in circles all night. But some of them point the other way, coming toward the tree from the opposite direction, from a direction (he/she) never walked. They're exactly the size of (his/her) feet. (Name) goes home very fast.

CHOICE D: FOLLOW A DIFFERENT LANDMARK
First popup: Forget the tree. (Name) listens for the sound of running water and heads for it, hoping the stream will lead (him/her) home...
Ending D1 -- THE STREAM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It works. The stream leads (name) downhill, babbling cheerfully, and after a while (he/she) comes out at the washing pools just below the village. (He/She) is soaked to the knees, but (he/she) is home, and the paperbark tree is nowhere to be seen.
Ending D2 -- THE THORNS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: INJURED (loses health)
The stream sound leads (name) straight into a thicket of thorny brush in the dark. (He/She) struggles through it, yelping, for what feels like hours, and finally stumbles into the village at midnight looking like (he/she) wrestled a wildcat. The thorns leave long red scratches all over (his/her) arms, and (he/she) is picking them out of (his/her) wrap for days.

MY-044. The Guest Who Left No Name   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older. (child), in Ending B2, is a villager under 14 (story only, no effect).
EVENT TEXT
One morning, a silent visitor in a plain brown wrap appears at the well and starts carrying water. Jar after jar, from the spring to the cooking huts, from the cooking huts to the gardens, without a word, without a rest, as if it were nothing at all.
All day long the visitor works. Nobody asks them to. Nobody knows who they are. By evening, every jar in the village is full, the gardens are soaked and the cooks are delighted. And then, as the sun goes down, the visitor is simply gone, before anyone thought to ask their name. (Name) was the last person to see them. What should (he/she) do?

Choice A: Search for the Helper
Choice B: Leave a Gift at the Well
Choice C: Tell the Story
Choice D: Inspect the Work

CHOICE A: SEARCH FOR THE HELPER
First popup: (Name) sets off down the road the visitor might have taken, asking every traveler and every neighboring village, "Have you seen someone in a plain brown wrap?"...
Ending A1 -- THE NEIGHBORS' THANKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
At the next village along the coast, the people recognize the description at once and break into smiles. "That's one of ours! Always wandering off to help someone." A few days later, a runner arrives at (name)'s village with a basket of sweet potatoes and a message of thanks for the kindness shown to one of their own. "Kindness shown?" (name) says. "They did all the work!"
Ending A2 -- NO ONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nobody has seen anyone matching the description. Not on the roads, not in the villages, not on the shore. (Name) searches for days and comes home empty-handed. The visitor in brown simply isn't anywhere. (Name) can't decide whether that's sad, or wonderful, or both.

CHOICE B: LEAVE A GIFT AT THE WELL

Ending B1 -- THE FRESH ROPE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
By morning, the gift is gone. In its place lies a brand-new well rope, thick and strong and perfectly coiled, made of fibre twisted so tightly it's almost like wood. The old frayed rope has been taken away. Nobody heard a thing. The new rope lasts for years.
Ending B2 -- RETURNED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The gift sits there all night. In the morning, (child) carries it carefully up to (name)'s door. "Somebody lost this," (child) explains solemnly. "I found it at the well." (Name) thanks (child) and laughs, and decides that maybe the helper doesn't need a gift after all.

CHOICE C: TELL THE STORY
First popup: That evening by the fire, (name) tells everyone the whole story of the silent helper, from the first jar of water to the last...
Ending C1 -- THE NEW TRADITION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The story touches everyone. Before long, the village has a new tradition: once a season, each villager does one helpful thing for someone without saying who did it. Mysterious mended baskets, fixed fences, surprise piles of firewood. Nobody ever owns up. Everyone seems very happy about it.
Ending C2 -- THE DOUBTERS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Some villagers are moved. Others just shrug. "Probably a shy traveler who wanted a meal," one says. "Didn't even stay for it, though," someone points out. "Very shy, then." The argument goes on until late. (Name) doesn't mind. (He/She) knows what (he/she) saw.

CHOICE D: INSPECT THE WORK

Ending D1 -- THE BAMBOO CHANNEL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
It wasn't just water carrying. Along the way, the visitor fixed things: a cracked jar, a leaking basin, and best of all, a new channel of split bamboo running from the spring all the way down to the cooking huts, so the water flows there on its own. It's very clever work. The builders study it carefully and copy it all over the village. Your villagers gain (award) tech points.
Ending D2 -- TOO FAST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Everywhere (name) looks, there are repairs. The basins, the jars, the steps down to the spring, all fixed, and fixed well. It's sound work. Good work. But the builders who look at it with (name) shake their heads. "This is a week of work," they say. "Maybe two." The visitor was only here for one day.

MY-045. The Promise Beneath the Tree   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
Beneath the old banyan, whose roots hang down like curtains, (name) meets a stranger with a voice so soft the rustling leaves almost drown it out.
"I can grant you one wish," the stranger says. "Only one. But you must never speak it aloud. Not now, not ever. Just think it." The stranger closes (his/her) eyes and waits. (Name) laughs nervously, then stops, because the stranger isn't laughing. What will (name) wish for, silently, in (his/her) heart?

Choice A: Wish for Abundance
Choice B: Wish for Knowledge
Choice C: Wish for Someone's Return
Choice D: Refuse the Wish

CHOICE A: WISH FOR ABUNDANCE
First popup: (Name) closes (his/her) eyes and wishes, very hard, that the village will never go hungry. When (he/she) opens them, the stranger is gone...
Ending A1 -- THE SILVER SCHOOL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (large)
The very next morning, the lagoon boils with silver. An enormous school of fish has swept in from the open sea, so thick the water seems solid. The fishers cheer from their canoes and haul in net after net after net, laughing like children. It's the biggest catch anyone can remember. (Name) says nothing, as promised, and just smiles. Your villagers gain (award) food.
Ending A2 -- AN ORDINARY HARVEST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next harvest comes, and it's... fine. An ordinary harvest. Not bad, not good. (Name) waits and waits for something magical to happen. Nothing does. (He/She) starts to wonder whether wishing changed anything at all, or whether the stranger was just a stranger. Still, nobody goes hungry that season. Maybe that's the wish, quietly coming true.

CHOICE B: WISH FOR KNOWLEDGE
First popup: (Name) closes (his/her) eyes and wishes to understand things, to know how the world works. When (he/she) opens them, the stranger is gone...
Ending B1 -- THE NET DREAM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
That night, (name) dreams of hands weaving a net, fast and sure, in a pattern (he/she) has never seen: a clever double knot that doesn't slip, with wider gaps so the little fish escape and the big ones don't. When (he/she) wakes, (he/she) can still see it. (He/She) runs to the fishers and shows them. They try it, and it works brilliantly. Your villagers gain (award) tech points.
Ending B2 -- UNANSWERED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nothing changes. (Name) doesn't wake up any smarter. The questions (he/she) always had are still questions. But over the next weeks, (he/she) realizes something: some questions just stay unanswered, even after a wish. And somehow that's all right. (He/She) starts enjoying the questions instead.

CHOICE C: WISH FOR SOMEONE'S RETURN
First popup: (Name) closes (his/her) eyes and wishes, with all (his/her) heart, that someone (he/she) has lost would come home. When (he/she) opens them, the stranger is gone...
Ending C1 -- THE TRAVELER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Three days later, a long-absent traveler walks into the village: someone who left years ago to see the world and was given up for lost. Thin, weathered, grinning, carrying a bag full of stories. Was it the wish? (Name) will never know, and will never say. But (he/she) cries harder than anyone at the welcoming feast. (Story only: the traveler does not join the village.)
Ending C2 -- NO ONE COMES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Nobody comes. Days pass, then weeks. (Name) watches the road every evening, but the person (he/she) wished for doesn't come home. In the end, (name) has to learn to live with not knowing, with the hope and the sadness all mixed together. It's hard. (He/She) does it anyway, one day at a time.

CHOICE D: REFUSE THE WISH
First popup: (Name) shakes (his/her) head. "No, thank you. I don't think I want a wish I can't talk about."...
Ending D1 -- ALREADY KNOWS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger opens (his/her) eyes and smiles warmly. "Then you already know what matters," (he/she) says, and walks away through the hanging roots. (Name) stands under the banyan for a while, puzzled, then goes home feeling oddly light.

Your villagers gain (award) tech points.
Ending A2 -- CONTRADICTIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-051. The Visitor at the Cradle   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: an eligible villager aged 18 or older who has a newborn baby in the family (the baby's parent who is not nursing, or, if both are protected, a grandparent or older sibling 18 or older). Never the nursing parent. The baby is story only, no effect. (name2) is another villager (flavour only, no effect): an old neighbor in Ending A2, (name)'s cousin in Ending C2.
EVENT TEXT
Just a few days after the new baby is born, (name) sees a quiet stranger standing in the shade under the eaves of the family hut. Wrapped in grey. Very still. Watching the doorway. And the moment the stranger appears, the baby, who has been crying for an hour, goes perfectly quiet.
"Who's that?" (name) whispers to the family. They look where (he/she) is pointing. "Who's what?" Nobody else can see anyone there. The stranger hasn't moved. What should (name) do?

Ending D2 -- THE WHITE SHELL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-052. The Box of Winter in Summer   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
A traveling trader sells (name) a small wooden box for a handful of shells. "Very special," the trader says, with a wink, and is gone before (name) can ask why.
It turns out the box is cold. Not cool, cold. Even in the blazing midday sun, frost-like beads of water gather on its sides, and when (name) holds it, (his/her) fingers ache like (he/she) has been fishing in a mountain stream. Nobody in the village has ever felt anything like it. What should (name) do?

Choice A: Open the Box
Choice B: Use It to Cool Food
Choice C: Return It to the Seller
Choice D: Leave It in the Sun

CHOICE A: OPEN THE BOX
First popup: (Name) wedges a thumbnail under the lid and flips it open...
Ending A1 -- THE SPOILED FRUIT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
A blast of freezing air rushes out of the box and rolls across the drying racks next to (name). The fruit laid out there to dry turns brown and soft in moments, slumping and weeping juice, and the smell of it brings every fly in the village at once. (Name) slams the lid shut, but the damage is done. Your villagers lose (award) food.
Ending A2 -- THE COOL MINERAL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Inside, nestled in dry moss, is a lump of pale, glittering mineral that stays cool even after it's taken out into the shade. The researchers are fascinated. They spend weeks testing it, wrapping it, chilling water with it and learning how certain stones pull warmth out of the air around them. Your villagers gain (award) tech points.

CHOICE B: USE IT TO COOL FOOD
First popup: (Name) has an idea. (He/She) puts a portion of the morning's fish inside the cold box and closes the lid, to see whether it'll keep...
Ending B1 -- FRESH UNTIL EVENING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
It works! By evening, when every other bit of fish in the village is going limp and smelly in the heat, the fish in the box is as fresh and firm as when it was caught. It's only a small portion, but the cooks are overjoyed, and that night they make the freshest fish stew anyone has eaten in a long time. Your villagers gain (award) food.
Ending B2 -- FADED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
By the time (name) has fetched the fish and opened the lid, the box isn't cold anymore. Not even cool. Just an ordinary wooden box, warm from the sun. Whatever made it cold has faded before anyone could test it. (Name) is very disappointed and goes looking for the trader to complain.

CHOICE C: RETURN IT TO THE SELLER

Ending C1 -- REFUNDED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) catches the trader at the edge of the village, packing up. "Ah, not for you?" the trader says cheerfully, and hands back the shells without any complaint. Ending C2 -- NO TRADER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE D: LEAVE IT IN THE SUN
First popup: (Name) sets the box on a flat rock in the full blazing sun and waits to see what happens...
Ending D1 -- ORDINARY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Slowly, over the afternoon, the box warms up, until by sunset it's just a box. Ordinary wood, ordinary lid, ordinary temperature. Whatever it was, it's gone now. (Name) uses it to keep sewing needles in, and it never gets cold again.
Ending D2 -- THE FROST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Then, a heartbeat later, they melt away into droplets, and the box is warm. It never happens again.

MY-055. The Silent Market Stall   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
Overnight, a market stall has appeared at the edge of the village. It's made of driftwood and woven palm, with its wares laid out on a red cloth: little glass bottles, carved wooden boxes, tiny figures of birds and fish. A small bell hangs from the roof, without a clapper.
There's no merchant in sight. No sign, no prices, nothing. Just the goods, waiting. A small crowd has gathered, but nobody wants to be the first to touch anything. (Name) is standing closest. What should (he/she) do?

Choice A: Trade for a Bottle
Choice B: Choose a Wooden Box
Choice C: Wait for the Merchant
Choice D: Leave the Goods Untouched

CHOICE A: TRADE FOR A BOTTLE

Ending A1 -- THE OIL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The bottle holds a fragrant golden oil that smells of flowers and honey. The healers test a drop and are delighted: it's wonderful for soothing cracked, sore skin. Within a week, every fisher with chapped hands is begging (name) for a dab. When the bottle runs dry, the healers try very hard to copy it, but never quite manage.
Ending A2 -- CLOUDY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The moment (name) picks it up, the clear liquid inside turns cloudy, swirling grey like a storm in a jar. (Name) watches it swirl for a moment, then sets it carefully aside. (He/She) isn't about to put that on (his/her) skin. Or in (his/her) mouth. Or anywhere. It sits on a shelf, cloudy forever.

CHOICE B: CHOOSE A WOODEN BOX

Ending B1 -- THE HERBS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
Inside is a bundle of preserved herbs, dried and tied with grass, still fragrant: wild ginger, lemon leaf and something peppery nobody recognizes. The cooks are thrilled. They add a pinch to everything for weeks, and the village eats better than it has in ages. Your villagers gain (award) food.
Ending B2 -- YOU ALREADY KNOW. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending C2 -- GONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE D: LEAVE THE GOODS UNTOUCHED

Ending D1 -- NO TRACE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D2 -- THE CARVED BIRD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-056. The Person in the Rain   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
It's raining so hard the drops are bouncing off the paths. Everyone is huddled inside. But as (name) dashes between huts, (he/she) sees someone standing out beyond the village lights, hands folded, looking toward the village.
The stranger is completely still. And completely dry. The rain is pouring down all around, drumming on every leaf and roof, and not a drop seems to be touching the stranger at all. (Name) stops in the downpour and stares, water running into (his/her) eyes. What should (he/she) do?

Choice A: Offer Shelter
Choice B: Ask Why They Are Waiting
Choice C: Approach With a Lantern
Choice D: Leave Them Alone

CHOICE A: OFFER SHELTER

Ending A1 -- THE LEAF CLOAK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger steps forward into the light, and (name) sees it at once: the stranger is wearing a long cloak made of tightly woven leaves, layered like fish scales, and the rain is sliding off it like oil. Not magic, just very, very clever weaving. The stranger seems a little embarrassed by all the attention, and spends the evening by the fire showing the weavers how it's done.
Ending A2 -- VANISHED AT THE DOOR. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger nods and walks toward (name), following (him/her) through the rain to the door of the hut. (Name) turns to open the door. When (he/she) turns back, there's no one there. Just the rain, pouring down on an empty path. (Name) leaves the door open a crack all night, just in case.

CHOICE B: ASK WHY THEY ARE WAITING

Ending B1 -- NOT YET BORN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

(He/She) goes inside and lies awake listening to the rain, thinking about every baby that will ever be born in this village, and who might be waiting for them.
Ending B2 -- THE MISSING COMPANION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE C: APPROACH WITH A LANTERN

Ending C2 -- RETREATING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE D: LEAVE THEM ALONE

Ending D1 -- GONE WITH THE RAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When the rain finally stops, near dawn, (name) peeks out. The figure is gone. The place where it stood is just wet grass and puddles, glittering in the first light. Nothing else is different. (Name) almost wishes (he/she) had gone out.
Ending D2 -- THE DRY FIREWOOD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, everything in the village is soaked through. Every log, every stick, every scrap of kindling. But by (name)'s door sits a neat bundle of firewood, perfectly dry, as if it had been kept indoors all night. MY-057. The Gourd That Would Not Empty   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: any eligible villager aged 14 or older.
EVENT TEXT
A wandering elder stops at (name)'s hut for a drink, and before leaving, presses an old drinking gourd into (name)'s hands. It's smooth and worn, with a stopper of carved wood, and when (name) shakes it, it makes no sound at all.
"It will always hold exactly what is needed," the elder says. "Never what is wanted. Remember that." And off the elder goes, before (name) can say thank you. (Name) pulls out the stopper and peers inside. It's dark in there. What should (he/she) do with it?

Choice B: Use It for Soup

Ending A1 -- ENOUGH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Water flows out of the gourd: cool, clear, and exactly enough. The traveler drinks it all, gasping with relief, and the gourd runs dry at the very last drop. (Name) shakes it. Empty. The next day, when a child comes in from the fields red-faced and parched, it's full again, with exactly a child's worth. (Name) begins to understand.
Ending A2 -- BONE DRY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending C2 -- NO SEAM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE D: RETURN IT TO THE ELDER

Ending D1 -- FOR THE NEXT PERSON. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) catches up with the elder by the river. The elder smiles and takes the gourd back. "Thank you," the old one says. "Not many give it back." Ending D2 -- ALREADY GONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE B: CALL FOR HELP
First popup: "Everyone! Wake up! There's someone out there!" (Name) shouts, banging a cooking pot with a spoon until bleary-eyed villagers stumble out of their huts. Together they link arms and follow the sound into the mist...
Ending B1 -- A LOST TRAVELER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

The traveler has been calling out every name (he/she) could think of, hoping someone in the village would recognize one. By sheer chance, one of them was (name)'s. Ending B2 -- THE VOICE STOPS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

(Name) is sure. Mostly sure. (He/she) spends the rest of the day glancing toward the trees, and when evening comes, (he/she) sleeps with the door firmly shut.

CHOICE C: SPEAK TO THE MIST
First popup: (Name) swallows hard and answers. "I hear you," (he/she) says into the white. "If it's really you... tell me something only you would know."

CHOICE D: WAIT FOR THE MIST TO CLEAR

Ending D2 -- FOOTPRINTS BY THE WELL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-060. The Crown of Driftwood   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one child under 14, not special. The stranger is a visitor, not a villager.
EVENT TEXT
Little (name) comes running up from the beach holding something above (his/her) head like a prize: a crown woven from grey driftwood, threaded with cowrie shells and strands of dried seaweed. It smells powerfully of the tide and is far too big for (him/her). A traveler resting by the fire takes one look at it and goes pale. "Child," the stranger says slowly, "that crown once belonged to a ruler of the sea. Be careful where you put it."
(Name) looks at the crown. The crown, being made of driftwood, does not look back. Still, the other children have gone very quiet, and everyone is waiting to see what happens next. (Name) desperately wants to wear it. But should (he/she)?
Choice A: Let the Child Wear It
Choice B: Ask for the Crown's History
Choice C: Return It to the Sea
Choice D: Preserve It

CHOICE A: LET THE CHILD WEAR IT
First popup: "It's just a crown," one of (name)'s parents says, and plonks it onto (name)'s head, where it promptly slides down over one ear. (Name) straightens it with great dignity and announces that (he/she) is now in charge...
Ending A1 -- THE ROYAL PROCESSION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Within the hour, (name) is leading a royal procession through the village. (His/her) loyal subjects consist of three children, two dogs and a very confused chicken, who did not volunteer. They march around every hut twice, demand tribute (a handful of berries each), and hold court on top of the woodpile until supper. The traveler watches the whole thing with a strange little smile. "Perhaps," the stranger says to no one in particular, "the sea has finally found a ruler who deserves it."
Ending A2 -- DREAMS OF UNDERWATER HALLS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: like + swimming (VV1-VV5: swimming, story only)
(Name) falls asleep that night still wearing the crown, and dreams of tall green halls beneath the waves, where fish swim between pillars of coral and someone sings in a voice like rushing water. (He/she) wakes before dawn, drags (his/her) parents out of bed, and announces that (he/she) must learn to swim. Right now. Today. (Name) spends the whole morning splashing in the shallows, swallowing seawater and grinning, and from then on, nobody can keep (him/her) out of the sea.

CHOICE B: ASK FOR THE CROWN'S HISTORY
First popup: The villagers gather around the fire, and (name) sits right at the front, crown in (his/her) lap. "Tell us," (he/she) says. "Who was the ruler of the sea?"...
Ending B1 -- THE HUMBLE RULER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger tells of a proud ruler who commanded every wave and every fish, until one day a storm took the kingdom away and left the ruler with nothing but driftwood and shells. With those, the ruler wove a new crown and spent the rest of (his/her) days helping fishermen find their way home. "A crown made from what is left," the stranger says, "weighs more than one made of gold." The children are not entirely sure what that means. (Name) decides it means the crown is very important, and refuses to let anyone else touch it.
Ending B2 -- A FESTIVAL DECORATION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Before the stranger can say a word, one of the elders squints at the crown, and then bursts out laughing. "The ruler of the sea? That's the decoration from last year's harvest festival! I made it myself! It blew off the top of the pole and we never found it." The stranger turns a deep shade of red, mumbles something about the light being bad, and leaves quite early the next morning. (Name) keeps the crown anyway. A festival crown is still a crown.

CHOICE C: RETURN IT TO THE SEA
First popup: "If it belongs to the sea," (name) says solemnly, "then the sea should have it back." The whole village follows (him/her) down to the shore, where (he/she) wades out to (his/her) knees and lets a wave carry the crown away...
Ending C1 -- A SHELL IN ITS PLACE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The crown bobs out past the breakers and is gone. Moments later, the next wave rolls in and leaves something at (name)'s feet: a pearly white shell, spiralled like a tiny staircase, unlike any shell the villagers have ever seen on that beach. (Name) holds it up to (his/her) ear and swears (he/she) can hear someone saying thank you. The other children all insist on listening too. They all hear the sea. (Name) still swears it said thank you.
Ending C2 -- IT COMES BACK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, (name) goes down to the beach and finds the crown lying on the sand in exactly the same place (he/she) found it the first time, as neat as if someone had set it down on purpose. (He/she) throws it back. The morning after, it is there again. After the third time, the elders decide the sea has made its feelings very clear, and (name) is allowed to keep it. The traveler, when told, only nods, as if (he/she) had expected nothing else.

CHOICE D: PRESERVE IT
First popup: The villagers decide something this unusual should be kept safe. (Name) carries the crown to the driest hut in the village, and the craftspeople set it carefully on a high shelf, out of reach of goats and children (mostly children)...
Ending D1 -- A FINE PIECE OF WORK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Over the next few days, villagers drop by to admire it. The weavers study how the driftwood was bent without breaking, and the shell-workers marvel at how each cowrie was threaded through a hole no wider than a hair. "Whoever made this," one weaver says, "knew more about their craft than all of us put together." The crown becomes a treasured example of fine island work, and (name) proudly tells anyone who will listen that (he/she) was the one who found it.
Ending D2 -- IT CRUMBLES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Out of the salty sea air, the crown begins to dry. Day by day the seaweed shrivels, the driftwood cracks, and one morning (name) finds nothing on the shelf but a little heap of grey splinters and loose shells. (He/she) is heartbroken and cries for most of the afternoon. That evening, the traveler helps (him/her) thread the loose shells onto a cord, and (name) wears them around (his/her) neck for many years after.

MY-061. The Sleeper Beneath the Hill   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
A traveler passing through the village sits by the fire with (name) and points at the round grassy hill just beyond the huts, the one crowned with a single leaning palm. "Your hill," the traveler says, "is not a hill. An ancient sleeper rests beneath it, and will wake when the island needs help." (Name) laughs politely. The traveler does not.
That night, (name) cannot sleep. The air is still, and yet the ground beneath (his/her) mat seems to rise and fall, slowly, like something breathing. When (he/she) walks out to the hill in the moonlight, the grass on its slopes is warm to the touch, like the flank of a sleeping animal. Something is under there. Should (name) try to find out what, or leave well alone?
Choice A: Listen at the Hill
Choice B: Dig a Small Test Pit
Choice C: Leave the Hill Untouched
Choice D: Tell the Tale at the Fire

CHOICE A: LISTEN AT THE HILL
First popup: (Name) kneels in the warm grass, takes a deep breath, and presses (his/her) ear flat against the ground. At first there is nothing. Then, very faintly...
Ending A1 -- AN UNDERGROUND STREAM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
...a low, rushing rumble. Not breathing at all, but water, a great deal of it, flowing somewhere deep below. (Name) fetches the researchers the next morning, and with ears and sticks and a great deal of crawling about, they trace an underground stream running right beneath the hill. It explains the warmth, the rumbling, and why the well on that side of the village never runs dry. The researchers scribble excitedly for days. The traveler, when told, just shrugs. "Even sleepers need something to drink."
Ending A2 -- A LONG SIGH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...a long, slow sigh, rising up through the stones, the kind a person makes when they roll over in a deep sleep. (Name) lies very still. The sigh fades. Nothing else happens. After a long time, (he/she) gets up, brushes the grass from (his/her) clothes, and tiptoes back to the village, though there is no one around to hear (him/her) tiptoe. From then on, (name) walks around the hill instead of over it. Just in case.

CHOICE B: DIG A SMALL TEST PIT
First popup: "If something's down there, there's only one way to find out," (name) says, and the next morning (he/she) and a couple of curious friends start digging a small pit into the side of the hill. The soil is soft and warm and comes away easily. A little too easily...
Ending B1 -- STRANGE CLAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
An arm's length down, their spades hit a thick layer of clay unlike anything the potters have ever used: smooth, faintly blue, and so fine it feels like butter between the fingers. The potters are ecstatic. Pots made from it come out of the fire hard as stone and ring like bells when tapped. No sleeper is found, but the village gains something very nearly as good, and (name) is very proud of (his/her) hole.
Ending B2 -- THE PIT COLLAPSES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: injured (loses health)
(Name) is waist-deep in the pit when the side of it slumps without warning. Heavy, warm soil pours in around (his/her) legs and pins (him/her) fast. "Help! Get me out!" (Name)'s friends dig frantically with their bare hands, hauling (him/her) free just as more earth slides down, and carry (him/her) to the healers with bruised, aching legs. As they leave, someone glances back at the hill. The collapsed pit has filled in so neatly that it looks as though no one ever dug there at all.

CHOICE C: LEAVE THE HILL UNTOUCHED
First popup: (Name) decides that whatever is under the hill, it has been there a lot longer than (he/she) has, and does not need (his/her) help. (He/she) goes back to bed and pulls the blanket over (his/her) head...
Ending C1 -- THE RUMBLING FADES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It rains heavily for the next three days. When the rain finally stops, so does the rumbling, and the hill goes back to being a perfectly ordinary hill with a perfectly ordinary leaning palm on top. The children roll down its slopes, the goats graze on it, and (name) eventually decides the whole thing was the rain soaking through the ground. (He/she) is almost entirely sure of this.
Ending C2 -- THE WARM PATCH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The breathing stops after a few nights, but one patch of grass near the top of the hill stays warm long after the rest of the ground has cooled. The village cats discover it first, then the dogs, then the oldest elders, who start taking their afternoon naps there and swear it eases their aching bones. (Name) joins them one afternoon and falls into the deepest, most peaceful sleep of (his/her) life. (He/she) dreams of nothing at all, and wakes feeling as though someone very large had been keeping watch.

CHOICE D: TELL THE TALE AT THE FIRE
First popup: That evening, (name) gathers everyone around the fire and repeats the traveler's story, adding a few dramatic pauses and one or two details the traveler definitely did not say...
Ending D1 -- A NEW SONG. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The village musicians love it. By the end of the week, they have turned it into a song about a great sleeper who waits patiently beneath the earth, ready to rise whenever the island needs a friend. The children sing it while they work, the elders hum it while they weave, and it becomes a favorite for long, rainy nights. (Name) insists that the verse about the sleeper's enormous snore was (his/her) idea.
Ending D2 -- NOT EVERYONE IS AMUSED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Half the village loves the story. The other half does not. "So there's a giant under the hill?" one villager says. "And it might wake up? And you want us to sleep next to it?" An argument breaks out that lasts well past midnight, and by morning several families have quietly moved their sleeping mats to the far side of their huts. (Name) learns that a good story and a comforting story are not always the same thing.

MY-062. The Flower That Bloomed for the Dead   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special, who finds the flower. Needs at least one grave or memorial. In VV5, a believer. (botanist name) = the village's plant expert (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
On (his/her) morning walk past the memorial stone, (name) stops short. Overnight, a flower has bloomed right beside it, where yesterday there was only bare earth. Its petals are a deep, glowing orange, the exact colour of the wrap that a beloved villager wore to every single festival before they passed away. Dew sits on the petals like tears.
(Name) stands there a long while. It could be a coincidence. Flowers grow everywhere on Isola. But this one grew here, today, in that colour. (He/she) is not sure whether to feel comforted or unsettled. "Could it be a sign from the one who wore that colour?" (name) thinks. "What should I do?"
Choice A: Tend the Flower
Choice B: Ask a Botanist
Choice C: Leave an Offering
Choice D: Tell the Family

CHOICE A: TEND THE FLOWER
First popup: (Name) fetches a little water in (his/her) cupped hands and pours it gently around the roots. Then (he/she) pulls the weeds away, sets a ring of small stones around it to keep the goats off, and promises to come back tomorrow...
Ending A1 -- IT LASTS AND LASTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Word spreads, and soon someone from the lost villager's family comes to water the flower every morning. And every morning it seems a little brighter. It blooms for weeks, far longer than any flower should. The family begins to linger at the memorial, talking quietly to the bloom as if it could hear, and their grief, which had been so heavy for so long, slowly begins to soften. When the petals finally fall, nobody cries. They simply say thank you.
Ending A2 -- IT LEAVES SEEDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
For a few days the flower glows, and then, as flowers do, it fades. (Name) is sorry to see it go, until (he/she) notices that the dry head is full of tiny black seeds. (He/she) gathers them carefully and plants them all around the memorial. The next season, the whole stone is ringed with deep orange flowers, and the village takes to calling it the festival garden.

CHOICE B: ASK A BOTANIST
First popup: (Name) fetches (botanist name), the village's plant expert, who arrives grumbling about being woken so early, kneels by the flower, and immediately stops grumbling...
Ending B1 -- A RARE SPECIES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
"Well, I never," the botanist breathes. "This is a dusk lily. It blooms only once every few years, and only for a single season. I've read about them, but I've never seen one." The researchers spend the week sketching it, measuring it, and arguing about it, and add pages of new notes to the village's knowledge of plants. "Of course," the botanist adds quietly to (name), when the others have gone, "that doesn't explain why it chose this spot. Or that colour."
Ending B2 -- UNKNOWN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The botanist examines the flower from every angle, sniffs it, counts its petals twice, and finally sits back on (his/her) heels, baffled. "I don't know what this is," (he/she) admits. "I've never seen anything like it." The botanist takes careful notes and a sketch, and promises to keep looking. (He/she) never finds it in any record, and though (he/she) searches the whole island for years, never sees another one.

CHOICE C: LEAVE AN OFFERING
First popup: (Name) goes home, wraps a little cake of sweet mashed fruit in a leaf, the lost villager's favourite, and sets it gently beside the flower. "For you," (he/she) whispers, feeling a little foolish and not caring...
Ending C1 -- UNTOUCHED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, the offering is still there, exactly as (name) left it. Not even the ants have touched it. (Name) is not sure what (he/she) expected, but somehow that feels right too, as though it were being kept rather than refused. (He/she) leaves it there for the rest of the week, and the flower stays bright the whole time.
Ending C2 -- A SMALL BIRD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As (name) watches, a tiny bird with an orange-tipped tail hops down from the memorial stone, pecks at the cake, and flies off with a chunk nearly as big as its own head. It comes back three more times before the cake is gone. (Name) laughs for the first time in days. The lost villager, (he/she) decides, would have found that very funny indeed.

CHOICE D: TELL THE FAMILY
First popup: (Name) goes straight to the lost villager's family and, as gently as (he/she) can, tells them about the flower. They follow (him/her) to the memorial in silence...
Ending D1 -- STORIES AND LAUGHTER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They kneel around the flower, and before long someone starts telling stories. Someone remembers the time the lost villager fell asleep in a canoe and drifted halfway to the reef before anyone noticed. Someone else remembers the terrible, terrible singing. Soon everyone is laughing and crying at the same time, and other villagers wander over to join in. By sunset there is a small crowd at the memorial, and it feels less like a grave and more like a party the lost villager would have loved.
Ending D2 -- TOO PAINFUL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Most of the family is moved and grateful, but one relative goes very still. "Please," (he/she) says quietly, "I can't. Not today." (He/she) walks away without looking back, and the others let (him/her) go. (Name) feels terrible. A few days later, though, (he/she) passes the memorial at dawn and sees that same relative kneeling alone by the flower, watering it with cupped hands. (Name) keeps walking and never mentions it.

MY-063. The Bargain of the Hidden Garden   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (elder name) = one of the village's oldest elders (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
(Name) is gathering firewood when a stranger steps out from between the trees. The stranger wears a veil of fine woven grass that shivers in every breeze, and (his/her) hands smell of crushed mint. "I know of a garden," the stranger says, "where food grows without anyone tending it. I will tell you where it is. I ask only one thing. Do not boast of finding it."
(Name) thinks of the village's half-empty storehouse. (He/she) also thinks that a veiled stranger offering free food in the middle of the woods is exactly the kind of thing the elders warn children about. The stranger waits, perfectly still. Is the stranger telling the truth, or is it a trick? Should (name) take the offer?
Choice A: Accept and Keep Quiet
Choice B: Tell the Village
Choice C: Ask Who Owns the Garden
Choice D: Decline the Offer

CHOICE A: ACCEPT AND KEEP QUIET
First popup: (Name) nods, and the stranger leans close and whispers directions: past the split rock, down the fern gully, and left at the tree that looks like it is waving. (Name) follows them, and finds...
Ending A1 -- A MODEST, SECRET HARVEST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (normal)
...a sunny little clearing bursting with beans, greens and fat yellow squash, all growing in neat rows that no one has planted. (Name) fills (his/her) basket, and keeps (his/her) word. Over the following weeks, small baskets of fresh greens start appearing on doorsteps all over the village, with no note and no explanation. Families who had been going hungry find themselves eating well. Everyone wonders who the mysterious giver is. (Name) just shrugs and looks innocent, which (he/she) is terrible at.
Ending A2 -- ORDINARY WILD PLANTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...a clearing full of perfectly ordinary wild plants: some sour berries, a few tough greens, and a great deal of nettle, which (name) discovers by sitting in it. Hardly a miracle garden. Still, it is a lovely spot, sunny and quiet, and (name) finds (himself/herself) going back there just to sit and think. (He/she) never tells anyone about it. There is not much to boast about anyway.

CHOICE B: TELL THE VILLAGE
First popup: (Name) thanks the stranger, then runs straight back to the village shouting about a magic garden full of food. Promise or no promise, this is too good to keep to (himself/herself). Half the village grabs baskets and follows (him/her) into the forest...
Ending B1 -- THE GREAT HARVEST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (large)
The garden is real, and it is enormous: row after row of beans, yams, squash and fruit, more than the whole village could eat in a season. The villagers organize a careful harvest, taking only what is ripe and leaving the rest to grow, and haul basket after basket home. That night there is a great feast. (Name) is the hero of the evening, though (he/she) catches (himself/herself) glancing at the dark trees now and then, half-expecting to see a veil shivering among them.
Ending B2 -- STRIPPED BARE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
By the time the crowd arrives, the garden has been torn apart. The ground is churned with hoofprints, the plants are trampled flat, and the last bean pod hangs alone on a stripped vine. Wild pigs, says one villager. Someone else points out that pigs do not usually eat a garden right after a stranger asks for it to be kept secret. Nobody says anything for a while. Then they all trudge home, and (name) does not boast about anything for a very long time.

CHOICE C: ASK WHO OWNS THE GARDEN
First popup: "Wait," (name) says. "If I take food from a garden, I'd like to know whose garden it is." The stranger tilts (his/her) veiled head, as if no one has ever asked that before...
Ending C1 -- WHOEVER CARES FOR IT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"It belongs," the stranger says, "to whoever cares for it." Then (he/she) tells (name) the way, steps back between the trees, and is gone. (Name) finds the garden overgrown and choked with weeds, and spends the whole afternoon clearing them, watering the thirsty plants and propping up the bent stalks. When (he/she) leaves, the little garden looks happier than (he/she) has ever seen anything look. It is a long time before it gives (him/her) anything to eat. (Name) keeps coming back anyway.
Ending C2 -- THE OLD NEIGHBOUR'S SECRET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger hesitates, then sighs and lifts the veil, revealing the grinning face of (elder name), one of the village's oldest elders. "It's mine, you nosy thing," (elder name) cackles. "I've tended it for years. I just wanted to see if anyone would ask before helping themselves." The elder shows (name) the garden, and from then on (name) helps tend it twice a week. The mint smell, it turns out, was from (elder name)'s tea.

CHOICE D: DECLINE THE OFFER
First popup: "Thank you," (name) says carefully, "but I'll find my own food." The stranger bows (his/her) veiled head...
Ending D1 -- THE STRANGER LEAVES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...and walks away without a word of complaint, back between the trees, and the forest closes behind (him/her). (Name) finishes gathering firewood and goes home. That evening, (he/she) tells the story at the fire, and several villagers immediately ask why on earth (he/she) said no. (Name) does not have a good answer. (He/she) just has a feeling, and decides that is good enough.
Ending D2 -- A SEED IN THE POCKET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...and steps back into the forest. That night, as (name) undresses for bed, a single seed falls out of (his/her) pocket: round, shiny, and green as a beetle's wing. (He/she) is certain it was not there this morning. (He/she) plants it outside (his/her) hut, half-expecting nothing, and the next morning there is a tiny sprout. (Name) waters it every day and tells no one, and tries very hard not to boast about it.

MY-064. The Threshold Test   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special, with a home. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
At dusk, a stranger in worn sandals stops at (name)'s door and asks politely to come inside. (Name) steps back to let (him/her) in, but the stranger does not move. (He/she) stands just outside the doorframe, hands clasped, toes exactly at the edge of the threshold, and says, "I may not enter until I am invited by name."
(Name) blinks. The cooking fire crackles behind (him/her). The stranger waits with enormous patience, as though (he/she) could stand there all night, and perhaps all of tomorrow too. (Name) has heard old stories about guests who must be invited in. In none of those stories did it go entirely well. Should (name) say the words and invite the stranger in?
Choice A: Offer a Warm Welcome
Choice B: Ask for the Stranger's Name
Choice C: Offer Food Outside
Choice D: Turn the Stranger Away

CHOICE A: OFFER A WARM WELCOME
First popup: "Well, come in then, traveler, come in, you're letting the mosquitoes in!" (Name) says, and the stranger smiles and steps over the threshold as if crossing a river. (He/she) sits by the fire, warms (his/her) hands, and gratefully accepts a bowl of stew...
Ending A1 -- THE FISHER WHO LISTENED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
After supper, the stranger tells a story about a fisher who learned to listen to the birds: which ones dive when the shoals are close, which ones circle when the water is empty, which ones laugh when a storm is coming. It is a lovely story, and by the end of it, (name) realizes it is also a lesson. (He/she) tries it the very next evening, watches the birds, and paddles exactly where they dive. The fishers are amazed, and the new method spreads through the village within a week.
Ending A2 -- GONE BEFORE DAWN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger eats, talks about the weather, praises the stew twice, and falls asleep by the fire, snoring gently. When (name) wakes at dawn, the stranger is gone, (his/her) blanket folded neatly in the corner. There are no footprints in the dew outside. The only sign anyone was there is the empty bowl, scraped completely clean. Whoever (he/she) was, (he/she) certainly liked the stew.

CHOICE B: ASK FOR THE STRANGER'S NAME
First popup: "I'll gladly invite you," (name) says, "but first, what's your name? I can't invite you by name if I don't know it." The stranger seems pleased by the question...
Ending B1 -- A NAME FROM THE INSCRIPTION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger says a name, an old and unusual one, and (name) invites (him/her) in by it. The visit is quiet and pleasant. But the next morning, while working near the old carved stones at the edge of the village, (name) stops dead. There, worn almost smooth by centuries of rain, is that exact name, cut into the oldest stone of all. The researchers have no idea how old it is. When (name) hurries home, the stranger has already gone.
Ending B2 -- AN ORDINARY NAME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger gives a perfectly ordinary name, the kind half the island has, and (name) invites (him/her) in. Over supper, (name) cannot help asking about the threshold business. The stranger bursts out laughing. "It's just a custom where I come from! Rude to walk in uninvited. You lot looked so serious, I didn't have the heart to tell you." The story is told around the village for weeks, mostly at (name)'s expense.

CHOICE C: OFFER FOOD OUTSIDE
First popup: (Name) decides to be kind, but careful. (He/she) does not say the words. Instead, (he/she) brings a bowl of stew and a cup of water and sets them on the step outside the door...
Ending C1 -- GRATEFUL AND GONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger sits right there on the step and eats every bite, then hands the bowl back with a little bow. "Thank you," (he/she) says. "That was kindly done." Then (he/she) shoulders (his/her) pack and walks on down the path, humming. (Name) watches until (he/she) is out of sight, and spends the rest of the evening wondering what would have happened if (he/she) had just said the words.
Ending C2 -- A SHELL ON THE DOORSTEP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When (name) goes to collect the bowl later, the stranger is gone and the stew is untouched, still warm. Beside it, on the doorstep, sits a polished shell the colour of the inside of a sunset. (Name) is fairly sure it was not there before. (He/she) keeps it on the shelf by the door, and from that night on, (his/her) house seems to stay a little warmer than the others, even on the coldest nights.

CHOICE D: TURN THE STRANGER AWAY
First popup: "I'm sorry," (name) says firmly. "Not tonight." The stranger nods as though (he/she) expected it, and turns to go...
Ending D1 -- NOTHING HAPPENS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...and walks off into the dusk. Nothing happens. No curse, no storm, no strange noises in the night. The fire crackles and the stew bubbles and the evening is exactly like every other evening. And yet, for months afterward, whenever someone knocks at the door, (name) finds (himself/herself) wondering who that stranger really was, and wishes (he/she) had found out.
Ending D2 -- THE THIRD BEAM. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...then pauses. "A word of advice," (he/she) says, without turning around. "The third beam from the left. See to it before the rains." And (he/she) is gone. (Name) thinks nothing of it until the next storm, when a horrible crack echoes through the hut and the roof sags. When the builders come to look, they find that one beam has split clean through. It is the third beam from the left.

MY-065. The Lost Page of the World   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
Walking along the tideline, (name) spots a thick greenish bottle half-buried in the sand, its neck stoppered with old wax. Inside is a single page, rolled tight and covered in tiny, careful handwriting that slopes uphill. It describes a place on Isola, a real place, with directions: but it also says that the place "is never quite the same twice, and remembers those who visit."
(Name) reads it three times. The handwriting is old. The bottle is older. And the directions start at a rock (he/she) walks past every single day. (Name) is itching to follow them. But a place that remembers its visitors...? What should (he/she) do?
Choice A: Follow the Directions
Choice B: Copy the Page
Choice C: Show the Elders
Choice D: Return It to the Bottle

CHOICE A: FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS
First popup: (Name) tucks the page into (his/her) wrap and sets off: from the black rock, a hundred paces toward the morning sun, up the dry streambed, through a gap in the rocks that (he/she) has somehow never noticed before...
Ending A1 -- THE OLD OBSERVATORY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
At the top of a hill (name) has never climbed, (he/she) finds a ring of standing stones, and under a fallen roof of slabs, star charts scratched deep into flat stone: whole constellations, the paths of the moon, marks for every season. (Name) runs all the way home. The researchers spend weeks up there copying the charts, and come back with a far better understanding of the seasons and the sky. Nobody can explain how a whole hilltop of standing stones went unnoticed for so long.
Ending A2 -- THE GROVE THAT CHANGES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The directions lead to a grove of trees that (name) knows perfectly well: the village children play there every afternoon. It is a disappointing end to a treasure hunt. But (name) goes back that night to be sure, and stops at the edge. In the dark, the grove is wrong. The trees are in different places. The path bends the other way. A bird is singing that should not sing at night. (Name) backs away slowly, and the next morning, the grove is perfectly ordinary again.

CHOICE B: COPY THE PAGE
First popup: Worried the old page will fall apart, (name) borrows a sheet of bark-paper and some ink from the researchers and sits down to copy every word, very carefully, letter by letter...
Ending B1 -- SAVED JUST IN TIME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
It is a good thing (he/she) does. By the time (name) finishes the last line, the ink on the original has begun to fade in the sunlight, and by evening, the old page is completely blank. But (name)'s copy is perfect, and on the back of the page, (he/she) has also copied a little map that turns out to show the island's springs and streams. The researchers are delighted, and the map is hung in the research hut.
Ending B2 -- THE COPY IS WRONG. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When (name) holds the copy next to the original, (he/she) frowns. The words are not quite the same. A path that bends left in the original bends right in the copy. A tree has become a stone. (Name) is absolutely certain (he/she) copied it exactly. (He/she) copies it again, more slowly. The second copy is different from both. (Name) decides to put the page down and go and do something sensible for a while, like gutting fish.

CHOICE C: SHOW THE ELDERS
First popup: (Name) carries the bottle carefully to the elders' fire. The oldest of them takes out the page, holds it close to the flames, and reads it in silence...
Ending C1 -- THE STORYTELLING TRAVELER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"I know this hand," the old elder says at last, smiling. "When I was a child, a traveler came here who wrote stories about impossible places: islands that moved, caves that sang, paths that changed when you weren't looking. We children adored them. I think (he/she) must have thrown this one into the sea for someone to find." The elder tucks the page into (his/her) own wrap and spends the evening telling the children every story (he/she) can still remember.
Ending C2 -- HISTORY OR FICTION? Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The elders argue all night. One says the page is history, a genuine record of a place that exists. Another says it is a story and nothing more. A third says that on Isola there is not always much difference between the two, which makes the first two even angrier. By dawn, no one agrees on anything except that (name) should not have brought it to them so late at night.

CHOICE D: RETURN IT TO THE BOTTLE
First popup: Something about the page makes (name) uneasy. (He/she) rolls it up again, slides it back into the bottle, presses the wax down firmly, and takes the bottle home to a dry corner of (his/her) hut...
Ending D1 -- SAFE AND DRY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The bottle stays on the shelf, sealed and dry. When the researchers hear about it, they ask to keep it in their hut until they can study it properly, and (name) is happy to hand it over. It sits there to this day, between a jar of strange seeds and a very old turtle shell, waiting for someone clever enough to make sense of it.
Ending D2 -- A DIFFERENT PAGE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, the wax on the bottle is unbroken. But when (name) holds it up to the light, (he/she) can see that the page inside is different. Shaking, (he/she) opens it. It is the same uphill handwriting, but it describes a new place now: a small hut, a dry corner, a shelf, and someone standing in front of it holding a bottle. (Name) puts the bottle down very, very carefully and goes to stay with a friend for a few days.
