MY-066. The Night of the Open Doors   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (neighbour name) = one of (name)'s neighbours (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
In the middle of the night, every unlatched door in the village swings open at exactly the same moment, with one long, creaking sigh. Cold air flows through the huts. Every cooking fire gutters and leans. Villagers sit bolt upright on their sleeping mats, and several of them see the same thing through their open doorways: a tall, cloaked figure walking slowly between the houses, unhurried, as though checking on each one.
(Name) is already standing in (his/her) doorway, heart hammering. The figure is just turning the corner by the storehouse. Some of the elders whisper that the island's old guardians walk through a village once in a lifetime, to see that it is cared for. Whatever is going on, someone needs to do something, and everyone else seems to be hiding under their blankets. Should (name) go after the figure?
Choice A: Follow the Figure
Choice B: Check the Wind
Choice C: Invite the Visitor to Speak
Choice D: Secure the Village

CHOICE A: FOLLOW THE FIGURE
First popup: (Name) grabs a torch and creeps after the figure, keeping to the shadows. It does not look back. It walks to the old food store at the edge of the village, pauses at the door, and seems to look up at the roof...
Ending A1 -- THE ROOF COLLAPSES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
(Name) follows its gaze and sees that the old roof is sagging badly. Without thinking, (he/she) darts inside and drags out as many baskets as (he/she) can carry, yelling for help. Villagers come running and haul out the rest. (Name) has barely stepped out with the last basket when the whole roof gives way with a tremendous crash, right where the food had been. When the dust settles, the cloaked figure is nowhere to be seen. The rescued food is stored in a sounder hut, and somehow there seems to be more of it than anyone remembered.
Ending A2 -- NO WAY OUT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The figure walks around the side of the last hut, and (name) hurries after it, torch held high. There is nothing there. The hut backs right onto a wall of rock, with no gap, no path, no rear exit of any kind. (Name) holds up the torch and looks for a long time at the bare stone. Then (he/she) walks home very quickly, without once looking behind (him/her).

CHOICE B: CHECK THE WIND
First popup: (Name) is a sensible sort of person, and sensible people know that doors do not open by themselves without a reason. (He/she) wets a finger, holds it up, and goes to wake the researchers...
Ending B1 -- A STORM IS COMING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The researchers grumble, but they come, and soon discover that the air has gone strangely heavy, the way it does right before a big storm. "A sudden change in the air like this can push doors open all at once," one explains, yawning. "It means bad weather is coming. Fast." Sure enough, a storm hits before dawn, but the village is ready for it. The researchers write down everything they noticed, so next time they will know the signs. Nobody can explain the cloaked figure, so nobody tries.
Ending B2 -- PERFECTLY STILL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
There is no wind. None at all. The leaves hang motionless, the smoke from the fires rises straight up, and the sea is flat and silent. The researchers check everything twice and find no reason for the doors to have opened. Eventually they go back to bed, leaving (name) standing alone in the perfectly still night, listening to (his/her) own heartbeat.

CHOICE C: INVITE THE VISITOR TO SPEAK
First popup: (Name) steps out into the moonlight, takes a deep breath, and calls out: "Whoever you are, you are welcome here. If you have something to say, say it!" The figure stops...
Ending C1 -- "CLOSE WHAT YOU WISH TO KEEP." Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
A voice answers, quiet and very clear, coming from everywhere and nowhere at once: "Close what you wish to keep." Then the figure is simply gone, and the doors, one by one, creak gently shut. No one in the village can agree on what the words meant. Some think it was a warning. Some think it was advice. A few elderly couples take it as a hint to hold each other a little tighter. All of them latch their doors from then on.
Ending C2 -- THE SLEEPWALKER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-068. The Box of the Last Word   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (elder name) = the oldest elder in the village (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
While clearing out an old abandoned hut at the edge of the village, the one the elders say belonged to a puzzle-maker who loved riddles more than people, (name) uncovers a wooden box under a pile of rotting mats. It is carved all over with tiny open mouths, dozens of them, and its lid is sealed tight with no lock, no hinge, and no keyhole. Scratched into the bottom is a single line: "I open only for a word you have never said."
(Name) shakes it. Something rattles inside. (He/she) has the distinct feeling that the dozens of tiny carved mouths are all waiting to hear what (he/she) will say first. What word could (name) possibly say that (he/she) has never said before?
Choice A: Invent a New Word
Choice B: Speak a Forgotten Language
Choice C: Break the Lock
Choice D: Leave It Closed

CHOICE A: INVENT A NEW WORD
First popup: (Name) thinks hard, screws up (his/her) face, and says the most ridiculous word (he/she) can come up with: "Flobbamunk!" There is a pause. Then...
Ending A1 -- OLD SEEDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
...a soft click, and the lid swings open. (Name) whoops with delight. Inside, wrapped in waxed leaves, is a small collection of old seeds of every shape and colour, some of which nobody in the village recognizes. (Name) plants them along the edge of the garden, and a surprising number of them grow, producing an odd, delicious little crop of speckled beans and squash as long as (name)'s arm. "Flobbamunk" becomes a village word for good luck, and (name) is very proud of it.
Ending A2 -- STILL WAITING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
...a soft click, like someone clearing their throat. But the lid stays shut. (Name) tries "Wibberlow." Click. "Snorpenfeather." Click. "Gumbo-gumbo." Click. Each time, that patient little sound, as though the box were saying, nearly, but not quite. By sunset, half the village is gathered around it shouting nonsense words, and the children have invented a whole new language. The box never opens. Everyone agrees it was the best evening they have had in ages.

CHOICE B: SPEAK A FORGOTTEN LANGUAGE
First popup: (Name) fetches (elder name), the oldest elder in the village, who remembers a few words of an ancient tongue (his/her) own grandmother used to speak. The elder leans close to the box and whispers one of them...
Ending B1 -- THE CARVERS' INSTRUCTIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
The lid opens with a sigh. Inside, rolled tightly in oiled cloth, is a set of instructions for making carving tools, drawn in careful little pictures: how to shape the stone, how to bind the handle, how to sharpen the edge so it holds for a season. The village carvers are overjoyed. Within a month, they have a whole new set of tools, and their work is finer than ever. (elder name) smiles quietly and does not tell anyone what the word meant.
Ending B2 -- THE ECHO. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The box does not open. Instead, from somewhere deep inside it, the word comes back, in a hollow, distant voice, as though spoken from the bottom of a well. (elder name) goes pale and sits down rather suddenly. (Name) asks what the word meant. (elder name) just shakes (his/her) head and asks to be taken home. The box sits on (name)'s shelf from then on, and (name) is very careful about what (he/she) says near it.

CHOICE C: BREAK THE LOCK
First popup: "I've had enough of this," (name) mutters, and fetches a heavy stone. (He/she) brings it down hard on the lid of the box. Crack!...
Ending C1 -- THE SCROLL IS LOST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech loss (small)
The box splinters into pieces. Inside, crushed under the stone, is what is left of a fragile scroll, old paper covered in drawings and notes, now torn into a hundred dusty flakes. The researchers spend days trying to piece it back together and manage only a few scraps, enough to know that it was important and not enough to know why. They also lose a good deal of time that should have been spent on other work. (Name) feels terrible. The researchers make sure (he/she) feels even worse.
Ending C2 -- EMPTY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The lid splits, and the box falls open. Inside is... nothing. An ordinary empty compartment, a bit dusty, with one dead beetle in the corner. The rattle, it seems, was the beetle. (Name) stares at it for a long while, feeling both cheated and relieved. (He/she) burns the broken pieces on the fire that night, and swears that for a moment, the dozens of little carved mouths all seemed to be smiling.

CHOICE D: LEAVE IT CLOSED
First popup: (Name) decides that a box which opens only for a word (he/she) has never said is the kind of box best left alone for now. (He/she) wraps it in a cloth and puts it on a high shelf in the research hut...
Ending D1 -- WAITING FOR SOMEONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The box sits on the shelf for many seasons. Researchers come and go, puzzle over it, try a few words, and give up. Nobody breaks it, and nobody forgets it. It becomes a sort of village challenge: every so often, someone climbs up, whispers a word, and waits for the click. Someday, everyone agrees, someone will find the right one.
Ending D2 -- THE TURTLE SONG. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
A few weeks later, one of the village children wanders into the research hut while singing a nonsense song about a turtle with three hats. As the child reaches the line "and the third hat was a fish!", there is a loud click, and the box on the shelf swings open. Inside is a tiny wooden turtle wearing three carved hats. The child is thrilled. The researchers are speechless. The song is now sung at every festival, though nobody has ever got the box to open a second time.

MY-069. The Watcher on the Cliff   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (elder name) = the oldest elder; (fisher name) = one of the quieter fishers (both named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
For seven nights in a row, a figure has stood on the black cliff above the village, holding a small lantern. The light is steady and never moves, not even when the wind howls off the sea hard enough to bend the palms. Every dawn, the figure and the lantern are gone, and nobody has ever seen either one arrive or leave.
The village is getting jumpy. The children refuse to go to bed, the elders mutter about omens, and (name) has had just about enough of lying awake staring at that little light. Tonight, (he/she) decides, someone is going to find out who is up there. But how?
Choice A: Climb to the Cliff
Choice B: Signal with a Torch
Choice C: Ask Who Keeps Watch
Choice D: Leave a Lantern Below

CHOICE A: CLIMB TO THE CLIFF
First popup: (Name) waits until the moon is high, then starts up the goat track toward the cliff top. The path is steep and crumbling, and the lantern above never flickers. The higher (he/she) climbs, the colder the wind gets, until (he/she) is pulling (himself/herself) up the last stretch hand over hand...
Ending A1 -- THE LOOKOUT SHELTER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) hauls (himself/herself) over the top. The figure is gone, and so is the lantern, but there, tucked into a crack in the rock where the light had been, is a little shelter: a woven roof, a dry floor, a bundle of dried food, a full water skin and a coil of strong rope, all neatly arranged. It is a lookout post for stranded travelers, and someone has been keeping it stocked. (Name) adds a few things of (his/her) own before climbing back down. The light still appears some nights, but no one minds it anymore.
Ending A2 -- THE FALL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: injured (loses health)
Just below the top, the ledge under (name)'s foot crumbles away. (He/she) grabs for the rock, misses, and slides and tumbles down the face of the cliff in a shower of stones. (He/she) lands hard on a ledge far below, badly hurt and unable to climb. (He/she) lies there in the cold until dawn, when villagers hear (his/her) shouts and lower a rope. They carry (him/her) to the healers with a battered body and a badly swollen leg. Looking up from the litter, (name) sees that the lantern is still burning on the cliff above. CHOICE B: SIGNAL WITH A TORCH
First popup: (Name) lights a torch, walks out to the open beach where the figure can see (him/her) clearly, and raises it high above (his/her) head. (He/she) waves it slowly: once, twice, three times...
Ending B1 -- THREE FLASHES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
For a moment, nothing happens. Then, high on the cliff, the lantern blinks: once, twice, three times. (Name) nearly drops the torch. (He/she) waves it again, and again the lantern answers. Soon half the village is on the beach waving torches, and the lantern blinks back patiently at every one of them. Nobody ever finds out who was up there. But from then on, every fisher coming home late looks for that little light, and every one of them makes it home.
Ending B2 -- CLOUDS COVER THE MOON. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The lantern does not answer. (Name) waves the torch until (his/her) arms ache, and still the little light hangs motionless above the cliff. Then a cloud slides across the moon, the whole cliff goes black, and when the moon comes out again, the lantern is gone. It is never seen again. (Name) cannot decide whether (he/she) frightened it away, or whether it simply got the answer it was waiting for.

CHOICE C: ASK WHO KEEPS WATCH
First popup: (Name) decides that if anyone knows about the light, it will be the elders. (He/she) sets out around the village with a basket of sweet buns as a bribe, asking everyone (he/she) meets...
Ending C1 -- THE OLD GUARDIAN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(elder name), the oldest elder in the village, takes a bun, chews it slowly, and looks up at the cliff. "When I was small," (he/she) says, "there was a guardian who kept a lantern up there through every storm, so the canoes could find their way home. My grandmother said (he/she) never missed a single night, not in forty years. When (he/she) died, the light stopped." (elder name) is quiet for a moment. "I suppose someone thought it was time it started again." (He/she) does not say who that someone might be.
Ending C2 -- THE PRIVATE FISHER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
After a whole afternoon of asking, (fisher name), one of the quieter fishers, goes red to the ears and admits it is (him/her). "I go up there to watch the sea at night," (he/she) mumbles. "It's peaceful. Nobody talks to me." (He/she) leaves before dawn because (he/she) has nets to check. CHOICE D: LEAVE A LANTERN BELOW
First popup: (Name) fills a lantern with oil, lights it, and sets it carefully at the foot of the cliff path, where anyone coming down would find it. Then (he/she) goes home and lies awake, watching the two lights through the doorway...
Ending D1 -- THE ROPE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In the morning, (name)'s lantern is gone. In its place lies a coil of rope, beautifully made from braided fibre that the weavers cannot identify, and stronger than anything the village has ever made. Ending D2 -- UNTOUCHED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In the morning, (name)'s lantern is still there at the foot of the path, its oil burned away to nothing. The light on the cliff has gone, as it always does at dawn. No one came down. MY-071. The Visitor's Final Footstep   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (neighbour name) = one of (name)'s neighbours (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
(Name) is walking back from the fields when a tall, thin figure steps onto the path in front of (him/her). The visitor has eyes like wet river stones and looks at (name) as if they have known each other a very long time. "One day," the visitor says, "you will hear my final footstep." Then (he/she) turns and walks away down the path, without a sound.
(Name) looks down. The path is soft mud from yesterday's rain. Where the visitor walked, there are no footprints at all. The old stories say the island's oldest spirits walk without touching the ground. What did the visitor mean? What should (name) do?
Choice A: Follow the Visitor
Choice B: Ask for Meaning
Choice C: Tell the Village
Choice D: Forget the Encounter

CHOICE A: FOLLOW THE VISITOR
First popup: (Name) hurries after the tall figure, but no matter how fast (he/she) walks, the visitor stays exactly the same distance ahead, gliding silently between the trees and leading (him/her) deeper and deeper into the forest...
Ending A1 -- THE HIDDEN CACHE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The visitor stops beside a fallen, hollow log, looks back at (name) once, and steps behind a tree. When (name) reaches the spot, the visitor is gone. But inside the hollow log, wrapped carefully in dry leaves, lies a small bundle of tools: two fine stone adzes and a bone awl, sharp and well made and clearly very old. The builders are thrilled with them, and study how the edges were shaped so they can make more.
Ending A2 -- LOST UNTIL MORNING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Then, between one step and the next, the visitor simply is not there anymore. (Name) turns around. Every tree looks the same. The path has vanished. Darkness falls, and (name) spends a long, cold, frightened night huddled against a tree trunk, listening to every rustle. At sunrise, (he/she) finally stumbles out of the forest, scratched and filthy, to find that (he/she) had been barely a stone's throw from the village the whole time.

CHOICE B: ASK FOR MEANING
First popup: "Wait!" (name) calls. "What does that mean? What final footstep?" The visitor stops, and turns back slowly...
Ending B1 -- "LISTEN WHEN SOMEONE NEEDS YOU." Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Listen," the visitor says, "when someone needs you." Then (he/she) walks on and is gone. (Name) thinks about it all evening, and finds (himself/herself) paying closer attention to the people around (him/her): the friend who has gone quiet, the elder who keeps looking at the sea, the child who never asks for anything. Over the following weeks, more than one villager comes to (name) to talk, and (name) is always ready to listen. (He/she) never sees the visitor again.
Ending B2 -- A FAREWELL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The visitor smiles sadly. "I am leaving Isola," (he/she) says, "for good, I think. I have walked these paths for a long time, and I wanted someone to know I was here. To say goodbye." (Name) does not know what to say. The visitor bows, and (name) bows back, and the visitor walks off toward the beach. That night a canoe with no light is seen slipping out past the reef. In the morning, the soft sand of the beach is smooth and unmarked.

CHOICE C: TELL THE VILLAGE
First popup: (Name) rushes home and tells everyone at the evening fire what happened, and what the visitor said. The villagers listen in silence, and then all start talking at once...
Ending C1 -- WARNING OR RIDDLE? Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Half the village thinks it was a warning, a sign that something terrible is coming, and spend the next week jumping at every sound. The other half is sure it was a riddle and stays up late guessing at answers ("A tree! Something that walks without feet!" "A cloud!" "Grandmother's cooking!"). Nothing terrible happens. Nobody solves the riddle. But the village has a lot of fun arguing about it, and the phrase "final footstep" becomes the local way of saying someone is taking too long.
Ending C2 -- THE DRAMATIC TRAVELER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(neighbour name), one of the neighbours, bursts out laughing. "Tall, thin, eyes like river stones? That's old Pebble-Eyes! (He/she) wanders through every few years and says that kind of thing to everyone. Told my mother the moon would someday ask her a question." Everyone laughs, and (name) laughs too, though (he/she) does not mention the missing footprints. It seems an unfair thing to bring up when everyone is having such a good time.

CHOICE D: FORGET THE ENCOUNTER
First popup: (Name) shakes (his/her) head firmly. It was a strange person saying strange things, and that is all. (He/she) goes home, eats (his/her) supper and resolutely thinks about other things...
Ending D1 -- LIFE GOES ON. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
And it works. The days go by, the crops grow, the fish bite, and nothing at all unusual happens. After a while, (name) genuinely forgets about the tall visitor, and when someone reminds (him/her) of it a season later, (he/she) has to think hard to remember what they are talking about.
Ending D2 -- ONE FOOTSTEP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Weeks later, (name) is walking past an old empty hut when (he/she) hears it: one footstep, heavy, single and certain, right outside the doorway. (He/she) freezes, then looks. There is nothing there but a small swirl of dust, settling slowly on the path. (Name) waits a long time for the next footstep. It never comes. (He/she) walks home very slowly, feeling strangely as if something has finished.

MY-072. The Jar of Two Sunrises   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (cook name) = the head cook; (elder name) = the eldest elder; (storyteller name) = the village storyteller (all named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
While turning over an old field to plant, (name)'s hoe strikes something hard. (He/she) digs it out: a clay jar, crusted with soil and tiny seashells, with two suns painted above a little boat. After all those years in the ground, the paint on the suns still glows orange. When (name) pries the lid up a crack, a smell drifts out, sharp and fresh and unmistakable. It smells of the sea. This field is a half-day's walk from the nearest beach, though the elders say that long ago, before the land rose, the sea came right up to these fields. Should (name) open it?
Choice A: Open the Jar at Dawn
Choice B: Ask About the Painting
Choice C: Carry It to the Shore
Choice D: Keep It Sealed

CHOICE A: OPEN THE JAR AT DAWN
First popup: Two suns, (name) reasons, must mean something about sunrise. So (he/she) waits until dawn, sets the jar facing the first light, and as the sun breaks over the hills, lifts the lid...
Ending A1 -- SALTED FISH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The jar is packed to the brim with dried fish, layered in coarse grey salt and smelling faintly of seaweed. They are perfectly preserved. (Name) cautiously tastes one, chews, and goes wide-eyed. They are delicious. The cooks are amazed, and the fish are shared out for a feast that evening. "Whoever packed these," says (cook name), the head cook, licking (his/her) fingers, "knew exactly what they were doing. I'd like to know how." So would everyone else.
Ending A2 -- THE COASTAL MAP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Inside, rolled tight in oiled skin, is a map: the coastline of Isola, drawn in fine brown lines, with a dotted route snaking around it and little marks for reefs, currents and safe landing beaches. Some of the beaches no one in the village has ever heard of. The fishers and researchers pore over it for days, and soon canoes are using the old route to reach fishing grounds they never knew existed.

CHOICE B: ASK ABOUT THE PAINTING
First popup: (Name) carries the jar to the elders' fire and asks what the two suns and the little boat could mean. The elders pass it from hand to hand, squinting...
Ending B1 -- TWO GENERATIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Two suns, one boat," (elder name), the eldest, says softly. "My grandfather told me about this. It means a parent and a child sailing together, two lifetimes in one canoe. Families used to paint it on jars they buried for their grandchildren to find." (He/she) hands the jar back to (name) very gently. "Someone, a long time ago, hoped this would be found by their family. I think they would be glad it was found by anyone at all." (Name) keeps the jar by (his/her) bed.
Ending B2 -- A DREAMED SUNRISE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(storyteller name), the village storyteller, grabs the jar and launches into a long tale about an ancestor who dreamed of a land where two suns rose at once, and painted it on everything (he/she) owned so (he/she) would never forget it. The tale goes on for most of the night and involves a talking turtle, three marriages, and a very long argument with a volcano. Nobody is sure any of it is true. But the children ask to hear it again the next night, and the next.

CHOICE C: CARRY IT TO THE SHORE
First popup: The jar smells of the sea, so (name) decides it should see the sea. (He/she) walks the half-day to the beach with the jar cradled in (his/her) arms like a baby...
Ending C1 -- WARM, THEN COOL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As (name) reaches the water's edge and the waves wash over (his/her) feet, the jar grows warm in (his/her) hands. Not hot, just warm, like something alive. (Name) stands very still. Slowly, the warmth fades, and the jar is just cool clay again. (He/she) carries it home in silence. Nothing else ever happens with the jar, but (name) swears to anyone who asks that it felt, for a moment, like it was happy to be home.
Ending C2 -- A TRAVELER RECOGNIZES IT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the beach, a traveler mending (his/her) canoe looks up, sees the jar, and drops (his/her) net. "Where did you get that? That's a jar from my island. My people make them, far to the east of here. Two suns for the two sunrises you see when you sail between our islands." (He/she) traces the little boat with one finger. "It's a long way from home." (He/she) and (name) talk until sunset, and the traveler stays in the village for several days, telling everyone about the faraway island.

CHOICE D: KEEP IT SEALED
First popup: (Name) presses the lid firmly back on. Whatever is inside has waited this long; it can wait a bit longer. (He/she) gives the jar to the elders, who place it with the village's collection of old things...
Ending D1 -- A TREASURED RELIC. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The jar takes pride of place among the village's old objects, between a cracked stone axe and a carved shell older than anyone can say. The children like to sit in front of it and make up stories about the two suns, and every one of the stories is different. Nobody ever opens it again. Everyone agrees that some things are better as mysteries.
Ending D2 -- THE SAND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In the middle of the night, there is a sharp crack. In the morning, the jar has split clean down one side, and a little heap of fine white sand has spilled out across the floor, full of tiny broken shells, like a beach at low tide. There is nothing else inside. Just sand. The jar was buried a half-day from the sea, sealed tight, and full of a beach. Nobody can explain it, and the sand is swept up very carefully and kept in a bowl.

MY-073. The Dreamer's Stranger   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (healer name) = one of the village healers (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
For the fifth night running, (name) has the same dream. A crooked guava tree, heavy with fruit. A stranger sitting beneath it, open hands resting on (his/her) knees. And the same question, asked gently, every single time: "What did you leave unfinished?"
(Name) wakes up tired and cross, and tells (his/her) friends about it over breakfast. One of them stops chewing. "A crooked guava? There's one exactly like that past the old fields." (Name) puts down (his/her) bowl. Is it just a dream, or is something calling (him/her)? What should (name) do?
Choice A: Visit the Tree
Choice B: Answer the Question
Choice C: Ask a Healer
Choice D: Ignore the Dream

CHOICE A: VISIT THE TREE
First popup: (Name) walks out past the old fields, and there it is, exactly as in the dream: the same crooked trunk, the same heavy branches, the same patch of shade beneath. (He/she) approaches slowly...
Ending A1 -- THE SURPRISED TRAVELER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Sitting under the tree, eating a guava, is a traveler: an ordinary, dusty, middle-aged traveler who looks up at (name) in some alarm. "I'm sorry," (name) blurts out, "but I've been dreaming about you." The traveler blinks. "That's either very romantic or very worrying." They end up laughing about it and sharing the guavas, and the traveler stays for a few days. (Name) never does find out why (he/she) dreamed of (him/her), and the traveler never asks (name) what (he/she) left unfinished.
Ending A2 -- THE LOST KNIFE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
There is no one under the tree. But in the roots, half-buried in old leaves, something glints. It is (name)'s own knife, the one (he/she) lost two whole seasons ago, (his/her) father's knife, its handle swollen with rain but its blade still sharp. (Name) had searched for it for days and finally given up. (He/she) sits under the tree holding it for a long time. The dream never comes again.

CHOICE B: ANSWER THE QUESTION
First popup: That night, when the stranger asks the question again, (name) does not wake up. (He/she) sits down under the dream tree, and thinks. And thinks. And finally, (he/she) knows...
Ending B1 -- THE OLD FRIENDSHIP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In the morning, (name) packs a basket of fruit, walks to the other end of the village, and knocks on a door (he/she) has not knocked on in years. It belonged to a friend (he/she) fell out with over something so small that neither of them can quite remember it. The door opens. There is a very long, very awkward silence. Then the old friend says, "Is that guava?" and lets (him/her) in. They talk until dark. The dream does not come back.
Ending B2 -- THE FORGOTTEN PROJECT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) remembers: the canoe. Years ago, (he/she) started carving a canoe of (his/her) own, and stopped when work got busy, and somehow never started again. It is still lying behind (his/her) hut under a heap of palm leaves. The next morning, (he/she) drags it out, brushes off the beetles, and picks up the adze. It takes all season. When (name) finally paddles it out past the reef, half the village is on the beach cheering.

CHOICE C: ASK A HEALER
First popup: (Name) is worried that something might be wrong with (him/her). (He/she) goes to the healers' hut and describes the dream in every detail to (healer name)...
Ending C1 -- STRESS AND MEMORY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(healer name) listens carefully and nods. "Dreams that come back again and again are often the mind chewing on something it can't swallow," (he/she) says. "Worry, regret, things you haven't let yourself think about during the day. Rest well, eat well, and let yourself think about it while you are awake. Then perhaps you won't need to dream it." (Name) tries, and after a few nights the stranger stops coming. (He/she) does think about the question, though, rather a lot.
Ending C2 -- UNUSUAL DETAILS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(healer name) begins to explain how stress shapes dreams, then stops as (name) describes the tree. "Crooked guava. Past the old fields. Fruit on the left side only." (healer name) frowns. "You've never been past the old fields, have you?" (Name) shakes (his/her) head. "Then I can't explain how you know the fruit only grows on the left. I can't explain that at all." (healer name) gives (name) a sleeping draught anyway.

CHOICE D: IGNORE THE DREAM
First popup: (Name) decides it is just a silly dream, and (he/she) is not going to let it ruin (his/her) day. (He/she) works extra hard, eats a large supper, and goes to bed determined to dream about something else...
Ending D1 -- THE DREAMS FADE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It takes a few more nights, but the dream slowly fades: the stranger becomes blurrier, the tree smaller, the question quieter, until one night (name) simply dreams about fishing instead. (He/she) wakes up feeling triumphant, and a little bit sorry, as if (he/she) has missed something. But only a little.
Ending D2 -- ONE LAST SMILE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the very last night, the stranger under the tree does not ask the question. (He/she) just looks at (name) and smiles, a kind, patient smile, as though (he/she) knows (name) will figure it out on (his/her) own. Then the dream fades, and the stranger never returns. (Name) wakes up feeling strangely warm, and spends the whole day trying very hard not to think about what (he/she) left unfinished. By evening, (he/she) has started thinking about it anyway.

MY-074. The Old Man at the Storm Gate   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. The old man is a visitor, not a villager. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
The storm hits at midday and does not let up. Rain slants sideways, the palms thrash and howl, and everyone is huddled inside, praying the roofs hold. Peering out through the gap in the door, (name) sees someone standing at the village gate: a bent old man, perfectly still in the gale, his long white hair blowing straight back. He leans on a walking stick carved with a jagged bolt of lightning.
When he sees (name), he raises his voice over the roar of the wind. "May I wait out the storm beneath your roof?" Behind him, the sky flashes white. Should (name) let a stranger in, in the middle of a storm like this?
Choice A: Invite Him In
Choice B: Offer a Blanket Outside
Choice C: Demand He Leave
Choice D: Ask About the Stick

CHOICE A: INVITE HIM IN
First popup: "Come in, come in, quickly!" (Name) dashes out into the rain, takes the old man's arm and hurries him under the communal roof, where the villagers make room for him by the fire...
Ending A1 -- HE SAVES THE ROOF. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
No sooner is he dry than a gust tears one corner of the roof loose, and rain pours in. Before anyone can move, the old man is on his feet. "Rope! There, and there! Tie it to the post, not the beam!" He knows exactly where every rope should go, and climbs the ladder more nimbly than anyone half his age, lashing the roof down while the younger villagers stare. By the time the storm blows itself out, not a single roof in the village has been lost. In the morning, the old man is gone.
Ending A2 -- A BUNDLE OF DRIED FOOD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The old man sits quietly by the fire all night, nodding along to the villagers' stories and laughing at their jokes. When the storm finally passes at dawn, he thanks everyone kindly and sets off down the road. Where he sat, he has left a large bundle wrapped in leaves: dried fish, dried fruit and hard little cakes of nuts and honey, far more food than one old man could ever have carried. Nobody saw him put it there.

CHOICE B: OFFER A BLANKET OUTSIDE
First popup: (Name) is not comfortable letting a stranger in, but cannot leave him out in the wind with nothing. (He/she) runs out with a thick blanket and wraps it around the old man's shoulders...
Ending B1 -- UNDER THE TREE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Thank you," the old man says, smiling with real warmth. "That's very kind." He hobbles to the shelter of the big fig tree beside the gate, wraps himself up, and settles down to wait. In the morning, the storm has passed, the old man is gone, and the blanket is folded neatly on (name)'s doorstep, completely dry, even though it rained all night.
Ending B2 -- THE SPLIT STUMP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The old man thanks (name) and shuffles off toward the trees. A moment later there is a blinding flash and a deafening CRACK, and every villager hits the floor. When they peer out, the old stump beside the gate has been split clean in two by lightning, still smoking, the smell of burnt wood hanging in the rain. The old man is nowhere to be seen. The villagers spend the rest of the storm talking in low voices about that carved lightning bolt.

CHOICE C: DEMAND HE LEAVE
First popup: "We've no room for strangers!" (name) shouts over the wind. "Go on, find somewhere else!" The old man looks at (him/her) for a long moment, then nods, and turns away into the rain...
Ending C1 -- THE STORE ROOF TEARS AWAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (normal)
He has barely disappeared from sight when a monstrous gust howls through the village. With a shriek of tearing thatch, half the roof of the food store is ripped away and flung into the trees. Rain pours in on the baskets inside. By the time the villagers manage to cover them, a good portion of the stored food is soaked and ruined. Some of the villagers say it was just the storm. Others look at (name) in a way (he/she) does not much like.
Ending C2 -- RESTING IN ANOTHER VILLAGE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The storm blows through and passes without doing any real damage. A few days later, a trader comes through and mentions, in passing, that an old man with a lightning stick spent the storm in the next village down the coast. "Lovely fellow. Fixed their roof, told them stories all night. They were sad to see him go." (Name) says nothing, but (he/she) feels quite small for the rest of the day.

CHOICE D: ASK ABOUT THE STICK
First popup: Before (name) decides anything, (his/her) curiosity gets the better of (him/her). "That carving on your stick," (he/she) shouts through the rain. "What is it?" The old man lifts the stick, and lightning flashes behind him as if on cue...
Ending D1 -- THE STORM THAT CHANGED HIS LIFE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"This?" he chuckles, ducking under the roof as (name) waves him in. "I carved it myself, the year a storm like this one sank my canoe and washed me up on a strange beach. I lost everything that day. And then I met my wife on that beach." He smiles fondly at the carving. "So I keep the storm with me. It was the worst day of my life, and the best." Ending D2 -- BEFORE HE WAS BORN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The old man looks down at the carving as though seeing it for the first time. "The lightning?" he says. "It was there before I was born." MY-075. The Stone Boat   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (researcher name) = one of the researchers (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
When (name) hauls in (his/her) fishing net, there is something tangled among the fish: a tiny boat, no longer than (his/her) hand, carved from grey stone. It has a little mast and a seated figure at the stern, holding a paddle. It is surprisingly light. On a whim, (name) sets it on the water, and it floats, bobbing gently, as happily as any piece of wood.
Stone does not float. Everyone knows stone does not float. The other fishers have stopped work to stare, and somebody has already started muttering about bad luck. Is it bad luck, or a lucky find? What should (name) do with it?
Choice A: Test the Boat
Choice B: Keep It as a Charm
Choice C: Return It to the Sea
Choice D: Ask a Traveler

CHOICE A: TEST THE BOAT
First popup: (Name) brings the boat back to the village and the researchers get very excited. They float it in a bowl, then a bucket, then the stream, prodding it, weighing it and arguing loudly...
Ending A1 -- THE AIR CHAMBER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
After a great deal of tapping and listening, (researcher name), one of the researchers, notices a hairline seam along the bottom. The boat has been hollowed out and sealed, leaving a hidden air chamber inside, so cleverly done that the join is almost invisible. "That's why it floats," (researcher name) says, delighted. "Whoever made it was a genius." The idea sets the builders thinking, and they start sealing hollow chambers into their own canoes to make them float higher and steadier.
Ending A2 -- AGAINST THE CURRENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They set the boat in the stream, and instead of drifting down with the water, it turns, all by itself, and glides upstream in a perfectly straight line, against the current. Everyone falls silent. It goes about ten paces, slows, and then sinks, all at once, as if someone had tugged it gently from below. They search the streambed for hours. They never find it. The researchers write a very short report and do not talk about it much.

CHOICE B: KEEP IT AS A CHARM
First popup: Bad luck or no bad luck, (name) likes the little boat. (He/she) threads a cord through a gap under its mast and wears it around (his/her) neck...
Ending B1 -- A FOND FRIEND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: like + the ocean (VV1-VV5: the ocean, story only)
(Name) grows very fond of the little boat. (He/she) talks to the little stone paddler, shows it the best fishing spots, and holds it whenever the waves get rough. Before long (he/she) is spending every spare moment down at the shore, helping fix canoes, watching boats come and go, and carving little wooden boats for the children. Whether the charm brings (him/her) luck, nobody knows, but it certainly brings (him/her) joy.
Ending B2 -- LOST ON AN ORDINARY DAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) wears it for a few weeks, and then one ordinary afternoon, hauling firewood, (he/she) reaches up and it is gone. The cord has snapped. (He/she) retraces every step and searches the whole path on hands and knees. It is never found. (Name) is surprised by how sad (he/she) feels about losing a stone the size of (his/her) hand. (He/she) still reaches for it sometimes, out of habit.

CHOICE C: RETURN IT TO THE SEA
First popup: (Name) decides that something which floats when it should not probably belongs where it came from. (He/she) wades out to the end of the reef, kisses the little boat for luck, and sets it on the water...
Ending C1 -- OUT TO DEEP WATER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stone boat bobs for a moment, then turns its bow away from the shore and drifts steadily out toward the open sea, the little seated figure facing forward as if paddling. (Name) watches it get smaller and smaller until it is just a speck among the waves, then gone. (He/she) stays on the reef for a long time, feeling oddly like (he/she) has just seen someone off on a journey.
Ending C2 -- THE ARROW. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, the stone boat is lying on the sand at the tideline, exactly where (name) will walk past it. It has a new scratch on its hull, fresh and pale against the grey stone: a small, neat arrow, pointing out to sea. (Name) stands holding it for a long time, looking at the horizon. (He/she) decides not to follow the arrow. Not yet, anyway. (He/she) keeps the boat on a shelf facing the window, and the arrow always points at the sea.

CHOICE D: ASK A TRAVELER
First popup: A trader from another island is staying in the village, so (name) brings the little boat to show (him/her). The trader takes one look and claps (his/her) hands...
Ending D1 -- A CHILD'S TOY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"A floater! I haven't seen one of these since I was small!" the trader laughs. "Every child on my island has one. Our carvers make them from a light stone from the volcano, full of tiny bubbles. We float them in the rock pools and race them." (He/she) shows (name) the tiny air holes in the stone. The fishers who muttered about bad luck look rather sheepish, and the village children spend the rest of the week racing the little boat in the tide pools.
Ending D2 -- MESSAGES TO THE DEAD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The trader goes quiet. "My grandmother told me about boats like this," (he/she) says. "In the old days, when someone died at sea, their family would carve a little stone boat and whisper a message into it, then set it on the water. The sea would carry it to them." (He/she) hands it back very carefully. "Someone sent this to someone. Maybe it arrived. Maybe it's still looking." That night, (name) lies awake holding the boat, wondering whose message it carries.

The moth is just a moth. (Name) puts everything back, rehangs the curtain, and stands there in silence for a long time. The voice does not speak again. CHOICE D: LEAVE THE CURTAIN CLOSED

MY-080. The Silver Thread   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
On the forest path, (name) walks face-first into something fine and tight, and steps back, sputtering. It is a thread, silver as moonlight on water, stretched taut between two trees at exactly the height of (his/her) nose. When the wind touches it, it hums. And when (name) follows it with (his/her) eyes, it seems to lead much farther into the forest than the trees themselves could possibly reach. The longer (he/she) looks, the farther apart the two trees seem to be. Old fishers say the spiders on this side of the island spin silk strong enough to hold a canoe, but none of them ever said it hummed. Should (name) follow it?
Choice A: Follow the Thread
Choice B: Cut the Thread
Choice C: Wind It onto a Spool
Choice D: Leave It Alone

CHOICE A: FOLLOW THE THREAD

Ending A1 -- THE LOST CHILD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The thread ends at a stream, tied around a rock. Huddled beside it, cold and wet and very scared, is a small child from the village who went missing that morning while the whole village was out searching the wrong way. "I followed the shiny string," the child sobs. "I thought it would take me home." (Name) wraps the child in (his/her) wrap and follows the thread all the way back. Ending A2 -- THE ABANDONED SHRINE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-081. The Cave of Returned Words   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (researcher name) = the village's most learned researcher (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
Sheltering from a sudden shower, (name) ducks into a small cave in the hillside, barely waist-high, its walls slick and dark. "Phew," (he/she) mutters. And the cave answers. But not with "phew." From the back of the cave, in a voice that is not (name)'s at all, comes: "...mind the left side, it's not safe..."
(Name) freezes. Every sound in here comes back a little too late and a little too clear. And the cave, it seems, does not repeat what is said to it. It repeats what someone else once said. Should (name) stay and listen, or get out of there?
Choice A: Listen to the Echo
Choice B: Speak a Question
Choice C: Bring a Scholar
Choice D: Seal the Cave

CHOICE A: LISTEN TO THE ECHO
First popup: (Name) holds very still and listens. The cave is quiet for a long moment. Then, faintly, the voices begin to come back...
Ending A1 -- THE OLD WARNING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It is an old man's voice, gruff and worried: "Taro! Keep away from the cracked rock on the left! It'll come down on you one day!" Then silence. (Name) looks to the left. The rock there is split with a long crack, and a slab the size of a canoe is hanging by almost nothing. (Name) backs out very slowly and fetches the builders, who prop the slab and seal it with stones. Nobody in the village has ever heard of anyone named Taro, but the elders agree that he was very lucky to have someone looking out for him.
Ending A2 -- A NAME NOT SPOKEN IN YEARS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
A woman's voice, warm and laughing, says a single name, the name of a villager who died many years ago, and whose family has not been able to bear saying it since. (Name) recognizes it at once. (He/she) goes to the family and tells them, gently, what (he/she) heard. That afternoon, three of them crawl into the little cave together and sit in the dark, listening, for hours. CHOICE B: SPEAK A QUESTION
First popup: (Name) takes a breath. "Who are you?" (he/she) asks the dark. The question rolls away into the back of the cave, and (name) waits...
Ending B1 -- (NAME)'S OWN VOICE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The answer comes back in (name)'s own voice, unmistakably (his/her) own, but older, slower and saying words (he/she) has never said: "Don't worry so much. It all works out." (Name) scrambles out of the cave so fast (he/she) bumps (his/her) head on the roof. (He/she) does not go back. But years later, as an old (man/woman), (he/she) catches (himself/herself) saying those exact words to a nervous young villager, and stops, and laughs out loud.
Ending B2 -- AN ORDINARY ECHO. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"...are you... are you... you..." comes back, in (name)'s own voice, exactly as an echo should. (Name) tries again. "Hello?" "...hello... hello..." Perfectly ordinary. (He/she) tries every word (he/she) can think of, and the cave repeats every one of them back, faithfully and without imagination. The rain stops. (Name) crawls out, half relieved and half disappointed, and decides the first voice must have been the wind.

CHOICE C: BRING A SCHOLAR

After a day of crawling, tapping, measuring and getting extremely muddy, (researcher name) emerges triumphant. "Tunnels!" (he/she) announces. "The hill is riddled with tiny tunnels that carry sound from far away, from the old paths, the stream, the other side of the hill, and bend it so it comes out here. Ending C2 -- VOICES FROM ANOTHER CENTURY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE D: SEAL THE CAVE
First popup: (Name) wants nothing to do with a cave full of other people's words. (He/she) tells the elders, who agree that a cave which talks back is not a safe place for curious children, and the builders haul stones up the hill...
Ending D1 -- SEALED AND SAFE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The builders pile stones across the entrance and pack the gaps with clay until not a crack remains. Ending D2 -- STILL WHISPERING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The cave is sealed tight. Nobody can agree on what it is saying. Eventually, the villagers start walking past without stopping, and saying hello as they go, just to be polite.

MY-082. The Traveler's Lost Star   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
Late one night, a traveler stumbles into the village, face lined from years of squinting at the sky, and grabs (name) by the sleeve. "The red star," (he/she) says urgently. "The one low over the sea. Where has it gone?" (He/she) points at a patch of sky just above the horizon.
(Name) looks. Everyone on Isola knows the red star; mothers point it out to their babies, fishers steer by it. And it is not there. The patch of sky where it should be is empty and black. (Name) cannot remember the last time (he/she) looked for it. The traveler is staring at (him/her), desperate for an answer. Where could a star go? What should (name) do?
Choice A: Study the Sky
Choice B: Offer Shelter
Choice C: Ask Why the Star Matters
Choice D: Search the Horizon

CHOICE A: STUDY THE SKY
First popup: (Name) wakes the researchers, who grumble, wrap themselves in blankets, and come out to the beach with the traveler, where they lie on their backs on the sand staring at the sky...
Ending A1 -- THE TURNING SKY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
They watch all night, and night after night for a whole week, marking the stars with sticks in the sand. Slowly, the researchers work it out: the stars move with the seasons, rising earlier each night, and at this time of year the red star sets before it gets dark. "It hasn't gone anywhere," one says, delighted. "We just stopped looking at the right time." The village's understanding of the stars and seasons takes a great leap forward. The traveler stays the whole week and leaves very happy.
Ending A2 -- RIGHT WHERE IT SHOULD BE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They lie on the sand for an hour, seeing nothing but cloud. Then the clouds slide apart, and there it is: the red star, low and steady, exactly where the traveler pointed. The traveler laughs out loud with relief, then laughs harder, then cannot stop laughing, and soon everyone on the beach is laughing too, lying on the cold sand at midnight like a pack of fools. "Clouds," the traveler wheezes. "Just clouds."

CHOICE B: OFFER SHELTER
First popup: "Whatever's happened to the star, you'll not find it tonight," (name) says kindly. "Come in and rest." The traveler hesitates, then follows (him/her) inside to the fire...
Ending B1 -- STORIES OF NAVIGATION. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Over a bowl of hot broth, the traveler talks: about sailing between the islands by the stars, about reading the swell of the sea with the soles of the feet, about the birds that lead the way to land and the clouds that hang over hidden islands. (Name) is spellbound. The village fishers crowd in to listen until the fire burns down. By morning, the traveler is calm again, and sets off saying (he/she) is sure the star will be there tonight.
Ending B2 -- THE KNOTTED CHART. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The traveler sits by the fire for a while, then lies down. In the morning, (he/she) is gone. On the mat lies a scrap of sailcloth with stars drawn all over it, each one marked by a tiny knot tied through the cloth. In the corner, low over a drawn line of sea, is one red knot. (Name) holds the chart up to the next night's sky. It matches every star perfectly, except the red one, which is still not there.

CHOICE C: ASK WHY THE STAR MATTERS
First popup: "Forgive me," (name) says, "but why does it matter so much? It's just one star." The traveler looks at (him/her) as though (he/she) has said something terrible, then sighs and sits down heavily on a log...
Ending C1 -- THE STAR THAT LED HOME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Because it's the one I follow home," (he/she) says. "Every time I've been lost at sea, I've found that star and followed it, and it's led me back to the one I love. If it's gone, how will I get back to (him/her)?" (Name) sits down beside the traveler, and together they wait, and talk, until the sky turns grey. The star never appears. But when (he/she) leaves at dawn, the traveler is smiling. "I suppose I know the way by now," (he/she) says.
Ending C2 -- AN ANCESTOR'S PROMISE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"My great-great-grandmother," the traveler says, "promised our family that as long as the red star shone, we would never be lost. It's been shining every night for a hundred years." (He/she) stares at the empty sky. "And now it isn't." (Name) does not know what to say. After a long while, (he/she) points out, gently, that the traveler did find a village, and a fire, and someone to talk to. The traveler thinks about that for a long time.

CHOICE D: SEARCH THE HORIZON
First popup: (Name) and the traveler climb to the highest point above the village, and a few curious villagers tag along. They stand on the hilltop in the wind, scanning the dark horizon in every direction...
Ending D1 -- THE SIGNAL FIRE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They do not find the star. But low on the horizon, far across the water, someone spots a tiny orange glow: a signal fire on a distant headland, where no one has ever seen a light before. Another settlement! The traveler is thrilled; (he/she) is sure it is a village (he/she) has been trying to find. The next morning, (he/she) borrows a canoe and paddles off toward it. A season later, a canoe from that headland arrives, carrying gifts and greetings.
Ending D2 -- SILENCE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They search until their eyes ache. The star does not appear. Eventually, the villagers drift off to bed, one by one, and (name) is left with the traveler, who stands silently on the hilltop, staring at the empty patch of sky. At dawn, without a word, the traveler bows to (name) and walks away down the hill toward the shore. That night, (name) looks for the red star again. It is there. It is there every night after that.

MY-083. The Beggar with the Golden Seed   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

EVENT TEXT
An old beggar hobbles up to (name)'s door and holds out a cracked palm. In it sits a single seed, the size of a fingernail, shining like a drop of honey. "One golden seed," the beggar croaks, "for one hot meal. A fair trade, I think." When (name) takes it to look, (he/she) nearly drops it. The beggar watches (name) with bright, amused eyes. (Name)'s stomach says the stew in the pot is worth more than any seed. (His/her) curiosity says otherwise. Should (name) make the trade?

The beggar chuckles, takes the seed between two fingers, and taps it gently with a fingernail. It rings, a clear, sweet note, like a tiny bell, that hangs in the air far longer than it should. EVENT TEXT

MY-091. The Unfinished Statue   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

EVENT TEXT
Clearing vines from the hillside, the villagers uncover a statue, half carved, its shoulders wrapped in creepers like a shawl. The stone is grey and pitted with great age; the moss on it is centuries thick. And its half-finished face is (name)'s face. Not a bit like (him/her). Exactly (him/her). Everyone turns slowly to look at (name). (Name) stares at (his/her) own stone face and feels a chill run all the way down to (his/her) toes. "Well," says someone at last, "at least they got your good side." How could a statue this old have (name)'s face? And what should the village do with it?
Choice A: Study the Statue
Choice B: Finish the Carving
Choice C: Ask the Elders
Choice D: Leave It Untouched

CHOICE A: STUDY THE STATUE
First popup: The village carvers gather around the statue, running their hands over the stone, peering at the chisel marks, muttering to each other...
Ending A1 -- THE OLD METHOD. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
"Look at these marks," says (carver name), the head carver. "They didn't chip the stone. They split it, along the grain, with wedges. You can see where they tapped them in." Nobody in the village has ever worked stone that way. The carvers try it on a boulder, and it works beautifully: clean, flat faces, in a fraction of the time. Within a season, their stonework is the finest it has ever been. As for the face, the carvers agree not to talk about the face.
Ending A2 -- JUST A COINCIDENCE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The carvers study the face, and then, one by one, they start to laugh. "It's not just (name)," one says. "From this side it looks like my uncle." "From here it's my grandmother!" "It's a bit like everyone, really." It turns out the half-finished face is so roughly worked that almost anyone can see themselves in it, if they want to. (Name) is enormously relieved, and also, oddly, a little disappointed.

CHOICE B: FINISH THE CARVING
First popup: "Someone started it," (name) says. "Someone should finish it." (carver name), the best carver in the village, agrees, and with (name) sitting as a model, (he/she) picks up the chisel...
Ending B1 -- A SYMBOL OF NOW. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The work takes a whole season. When it is done, the statue stands tall on the hillside, finished at last: half ancient stone, half new, with (name)'s face looking out over the village. The villagers decide it stands for them, for this generation, the ones who found it. The children decorate it with flowers on the first day of every harvest. (Name) finds it very strange to walk past (his/her) own face every morning, but (he/she) gets used to it. Mostly.
Ending B2 -- THE STONE CRACKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the third day of carving, the chisel strikes, and a sharp crack runs straight down the middle of the statue's face, splitting it in two. (carver name) drops the chisel in horror. (Name) touches (his/her) own cheek without meaning to. The statue is left where it stands, split and unfinished, and (carver name) refuses to touch it again. (Name) is perfectly fine. (He/she) checks, several times.

CHOICE C: ASK THE ELDERS
First popup: (Name) brings the eldest villagers up the hill to see the statue. They stand before it in silence for a very long time...
Ending C1 -- FACES RETURN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"There's an old saying," the eldest says at last. "Faces come back. The island remembers everyone who lived here, and every so often it gives one of them back, in a child born many generations later." (He/she) looks at (name) thoughtfully. "Whoever this was, they were someone the island wanted to keep." (Name) does not know what to say to that. (He/she) goes back to the statue alone that evening, and sits with it for a while.
Ending C2 -- THE LONG-DEAD ARTISAN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Ah," says one of the elders, brightening. "This is the work of the Old Carver. You can tell by the wedge marks. (He/she) lived here long, long ago, and made statues of everyone (he/she) loved, and died before (he/she) could finish this one." The elder smiles at (name). "Maybe it was someone in your family. You might be (his/her) great-great-great-great-grandchild, for all we know." (Name) decides (he/she) likes that idea very much.

CHOICE D: LEAVE IT UNTOUCHED
First popup: (Name) has seen quite enough of (his/her) own stone face. "Leave it," (he/she) says. "It's been there this long. It's not hurting anyone." The others agree, and they let the vines fall back over it...
Ending D1 -- PART OF THE HILL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The statue stays where it is among the vines, and slowly becomes part of the hillside again: moss creeps back over its shoulders, birds nest in the crook of its arm, and a small fern takes root behind its ear. Ending D2 -- THE FRESH CHISEL MARK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, a villager passing the statue stops dead and calls everyone over. The crooked smile is now very slightly more crooked. Exactly like (name)'s. No one in the village admits to touching it.

Choice C: Call for Others
Choice D: Refuse the Request

MY-094. The Shore's Unseen Companion   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (friend name) = (name)'s best friend (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
It is low tide, and the beach is empty and gleaming, the wet sand reflecting the sky like glass. (Name) is wandering along the tideline collecting shells when (he/she) hears it: footsteps, crunching softly on the shells, right beside (him/her). Keeping pace. (Name) stops. The footsteps stop. (He/she) takes a step. So do they.
There is nobody there. Not on the sand, not in the dunes, not in the water. Just (name), and the gulls, and a set of footsteps that seem to belong to no one at all. Should (name) speak to whatever it is, or head for home?
Choice A: Speak to the Companion
Choice B: Look for Footprints
Choice C: Walk Toward the Village
Choice D: Leave a Shell Behind

CHOICE A: SPEAK TO THE COMPANION
First popup: (Name) swallows, and says to the empty air beside (him/her), as casually as (he/she) can manage: "Nice day for shells, isn't it?"...
Ending A1 -- "I USED TO WALK HERE." Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
For a moment, there is only the sound of the waves. Then a soft voice, very close, says: "I used to walk here. Every day." It sounds wistful, and kind, and not at all frightening. (Name) does not know what to say, so (he/she) just says, "It's a good place to walk." The voice laughs softly, and then it fades with the tide, and the footsteps do not come again. (Name) walks that beach every day after that, and never feels alone on it.
Ending A2 -- THE HIDDEN FRIEND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Lovely day!" a voice wheezes from behind the nearest dune, and then collapses into helpless laughter. It is (friend name), (name)'s best friend, who has been creeping along behind the dunes the whole time, crunching shells in (his/her) hands to make footstep noises, and is now laughing far too hard to stand up. (Name) chases (him/her) all the way down the beach and pushes (him/her) into the sea. They are still laughing about it years later.

CHOICE B: LOOK FOR FOOTPRINTS
First popup: (Name) turns slowly and looks down at the wet, smooth sand beside (his/her) own feet...
Ending B1 -- THE SECOND SET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
There, right beside (his/her) own prints, is a second set: bare feet, a little smaller than (his/her) own, walking along with (him/her) step for step. As (name) stares at them, a wave rushes up the beach, washes over both sets of prints, and slides back. (Name)'s prints are still faintly there. The others are gone.
Ending B2 -- ONLY (HIS/HER) OWN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
There is only one set of footprints on the sand: (name)'s own, trailing back along the tideline as far as (he/she) can see. (He/she) walks on, slowly, listening hard. The crunching footsteps keep pace. (He/she) looks down again. Still only (his/her) own prints. (Name) decides, on the whole, that this is a very good day to go home early.

CHOICE C: WALK TOWARD THE VILLAGE

They follow (him/her) right up off the sand, along the path and through the trees. And then, at the very edge of the village, beside the first house, they stop. CHOICE D: LEAVE A SHELL BEHIND

The next day, (name) goes back to the rock. The pink shell is gone. MY-095. The Basket of Unknown Fruit   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

EVENT TEXT
A covered basket has appeared outside the food store overnight. Inside, nestled in fresh leaves, are fruits nobody has ever seen: pear-shaped, with skins like purple velvet, and they smell of honey and cut grass. Tucked among them is a note: "For those who dare to taste."
A crowd has gathered. Everyone wants to try one. Nobody wants to be first. All eyes slowly turn to (name), who was unwise enough to be standing nearest the basket and holding one. Should (name) take the first bite?

Choice C: Search for the Giver

Ending A2 -- UNKNOWN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

(Name) chews. (His/her) eyes go wide. "Oh," (he/she) says. "Oh, that's good." The flesh is pink and sweet, with a hint of spice, and the crowd falls on the basket like starving gulls. CHOICE D: PLANT THE SEEDS

Ending D1 -- HEALTHY SPROUTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending D2 -- NOTHING GROWS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) waters them every day. Nothing comes up. Not a single sprout. When (he/she) finally digs one up to look, the seed has simply vanished from the soil, as though it was never there. MY-097. The Book That Wrote Back   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

MY-098. The Stranger at the Funeral Path   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

MY-099. The Hidden Cup of Rain   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
Sheltering from the midday heat in a cave on the dry side of the island, (name) finds a cracked clay cup sitting at the very back, on a ledge of stone. The cave is dry as bone and smells of dust and old smoke. There is no stream, no drip, no damp anywhere. And yet the cup is full to the brim with clear, fresh water that trembles in the light of (his/her) lamp.
Scratched around the rim are a few old words: "Fills each night. Share it." It has been a dry season. The village wells are low. (Name) looks at the cup for a long time. Should (he/she) share it, or keep it for (his/her) own family?
Choice A: Share the Water
Choice B: Study the Cave
Choice C: Keep the Cup Secret
Choice D: Return It to the Cave

CHOICE A: SHARE THE WATER
First popup: (Name) carries the cup carefully back to the path, where a group of thirsty travelers have stopped to rest in the heat. "Here," (he/she) says. "It's not much, but drink."...
Ending A1 -- IT TASTES LIKE HOME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The cup passes from hand to hand. One sip each, (name) thinks, and it will be gone. But somehow there is enough. Everyone drinks, all seven travelers and (name) too, and every single one of them says the same thing afterward, puzzled: "It tastes like home." The water is cold and sweet, though the day is baking. When the cup comes back to (name), there is still a little in the bottom. (He/she) takes it back to the cave, and the next morning, it is full again.
Ending A2 -- ONE DRINK. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The first traveler drinks, and the cup is empty. Just one ordinary cupful of water, gone in a swallow. The others look disappointed but not surprised. (Name) leads them all down to the village instead, where the villagers share what little water they have and point the travelers toward a spring farther along the coast. The cup sits empty on (name)'s shelf. It does not fill again outside the cave.

CHOICE B: STUDY THE CAVE
First popup: (Name) wants to understand how a dry cave can fill a cup. (He/she) fetches the researchers, and they spend a day and a night in the cave, lamps lit, examining every crack in the stone...
Ending B1 -- THE CONDENSATION CHANNEL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Just before dawn, one of the researchers lets out a cry. As the cool night air seeps into the warm cave, tiny beads of water form on the stone above the ledge, and a narrow channel, worn so finely into the rock it is almost invisible, carries every drop down into the cup. "Someone carved this," the researcher breathes. "They knew exactly how to catch the night air." The researchers set to work carving channels of their own, and soon the village has a dew-catcher on every rock face.
Ending B2 -- FULL BY MORNING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They find nothing. No channel, no crack, no source of water anywhere. The researchers empty the cup, sit around it in a circle with their lamps and watch it all night without blinking. Nothing happens. And yet, when the first grey light reaches the cave mouth, the cup is full again, trembling gently, and none of them saw it fill. They pack up their things in silence.

CHOICE C: KEEP THE CUP SECRET
First popup: (Name) thinks of (his/her) own family and how dry the season has been. (He/she) tells no one about the cup, and goes back to the cave each morning to fill (his/her) water skin...
Ending C1 -- IS IT FAIR? Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It works. Every morning the cup is full, and (name) fills (his/her) skin and carries it home, and (his/her) family never goes thirsty. But (name) uses it sparingly, and begins to feel worse and worse about it. Every time (he/she) walks past the low village well and the villagers waiting their turn, (he/she) remembers the words on the rim: "Share it." It is a long, uncomfortable season, and (name) does not sleep well.
Ending C2 -- IT DRIES UP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
On the third morning, (name) arrives at the cave to find the cup bone dry. The next morning, and the next, it is empty, its crack dusty, as though it had never held a drop. (Name) stands in the dark cave with (his/her) empty water skin, reading the words on the rim again: "Share it." (He/she) goes home and tells the whole village. The cup never fills again, but at least (name) has stopped keeping secrets.

CHOICE D: RETURN IT TO THE CAVE
First popup: (Name) decides the cup belongs where it is. (He/she) sets it back on the ledge exactly as (he/she) found it, drinks one careful sip from it, and goes home...
Ending D1 -- FULL AGAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, curious, (name) returns. The cup is full again, to the very brim. (He/she) tells a few trusted villagers, and the cave becomes a quiet place where travelers and thirsty villagers can stop for a single sip on hot days. Nobody ever takes more than one. Nobody ever takes the cup. And every night, it fills.
Ending D2 -- GONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
When (name) returns the next day, the cup is gone. Only a damp circle remains on the ledge where it stood, still cool and wet to the touch in the baking heat. (Name) touches it, and it dries under (his/her) fingertip, and is gone too. (He/she) never sees the cup again. But sometimes, on the very hottest days, (name) finds (himself/herself) unaccountably not thirsty at all.

MY-100. The Stranger's Two Faces   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]

Both of them are sure the visitor was standing right in front of them at the same time. And the visitor, according to the fishers, is still down by the river. Which of them is right? Ending C1 -- NEWS FROM ANOTHER SETTLEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The visitor eats with the family and talks about the settlement (he/she) has come from, a fishing village on the far side of the island where the people paint their canoes blue and hold a festival every year where everyone swaps hats. Ending D2 -- THE CHILD'S DRAWING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-102. The Little God of the Garden   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one child under 14, not special, who insists on the little guardian. (name2) = a parent, guardian or gardener, 18 or older. In VV5, believers.
EVENT TEXT
Little (name) has been insisting for weeks that a tiny person lives under the leaves of the vegetable garden and protects it from slugs. Nobody believed (him/her). Then, one morning, (name2) goes out to water the beans and stops.
In the soft soil between the rows are footprints. Tiny ones, no bigger than a fingertip, pressed neatly into the earth and walking in a line between the beans, all the way to the water barrel. (Name) is standing at the end of the row, arms folded, looking extremely smug. (Name2) doesn't know what to believe. How should (he/she) respond?
Choice A: Watch Quietly
Choice B: Leave a Small Offering
Choice C: Ask the Child to Explain
Choice D: Protect the Garden

CHOICE A: WATCH QUIETLY
First popup: That evening, (name2) and little (name) lie on their stomachs at the edge of the garden, hidden behind the squash leaves, and wait, as still and quiet as two people can be when one of them is very excited...
Ending A1 -- THE ANNOYED FROG. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As the sun goes down, the leaves rustle, and out hops... a little brown frog, with very long, very spread-out toes, which leave very small, very neat footprints in the soil all the way to the water barrel. It sits on the rim of the barrel and glares at them, extremely annoyed to be discovered. (Name) is heartbroken for about a breath, and then decides the frog is the little god's helper. The frog is given a name and a little dish of water of its own.
Ending A2 -- THE TINY CUP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
They watch until the stars come out. Nothing appears. But in the morning, the tiny footprints are back, and this time they stop at the foot of the water barrel, beside a minute clay cup, no bigger than a thumbnail, filled to the brim with water. Neither of them has ever seen it before. Neither of them made it. (Name) is beside (himself/herself) with joy. (Name2) is not quite sure what (he/she) is feeling.

CHOICE B: LEAVE A SMALL OFFERING
First popup: "Well," (name2) says, "if there is a little god looking after our garden, we should say thank you." (Name) is thrilled. Together they set a single berry, a crumb of honey cake and a flower petal on a leaf at the end of the bean row...
Ending B1 -- THE HEALTHY GARDEN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
In the morning, the offering is gone. All of it, the berry, the crumb and the petal, without a trace. And over the following weeks, the garden does better than it ever has: the beans climb higher, the squash grow fatter, and not one slug is seen all season. The harvest is the best the family has ever had. (Name) leaves an offering every evening from then on. (Name2) helps, and does not ask too many questions.
Ending B2 -- STILL THERE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In the morning, the offering is still there, untouched, except for one ant investigating the honey cake. (Name)'s lip trembles. (Name2) kneels down beside (him/her). "Maybe the little god just wasn't hungry," (he/she) says. "Or maybe the little god doesn't need proof that we're grateful. Maybe just knowing is enough." (Name) thinks about this for a very long time. Then (he/she) decides it is a very good answer, and gives the berry to the ant.

CHOICE C: ASK THE CHILD TO EXPLAIN
First popup: (Name2) sits (name) down on an upturned bucket. "All right. Tell me everything. Who is this little god, and what does (he/she) do?"...
Ending C1 -- THE BEETLE-SHELL HAT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) takes a deep breath, and out it all comes. The little guardian is about the size of a thumb, wears a hat made from a shiny green beetle shell, loves worms more than anything, dances when it rains, and sings to the seeds every night so they know to grow. "And (he/she) doesn't like the cat," (name) adds darkly. It is such a wonderful story that (name2) tells it to the whole village that evening, and soon every child on the island is looking for little gods in their gardens.
Ending C2 -- THE CARVED TWIG. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name)'s smug look wavers. Then (he/she) bursts into guilty tears, and pulls a small twig out of (his/her) pocket, carved at one end into the shape of a tiny foot. "I made the footprints," (he/she) sobs. "Nobody believed me. I just wanted you to believe me." (Name2) hugs (him/her) tight. "You know what? I still believe there might be one," (he/she) says. "But next time, just ask me to look harder." (Name) sniffles, and keeps the twig.

CHOICE D: PROTECT THE GARDEN
First popup: Little god or no little god, the footprints have reminded (name2) that the garden fence is falling apart. The next morning, (he/she) and (name) start fixing it, post by post...
Ending D1 -- THE NEXT CROP IS SAVED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (normal)
It is a good thing they do. Two nights after the fence is finished, a pair of hungry wild pigs come snuffling around the garden in the dark, but cannot get through. In the morning their hoofprints circle the whole fence, and not a single plant has been touched. The neighbours, whose gardens have no such fence, are not so lucky. (Name) insists the little god warned them. (Name2) is starting to think (he/she) might be right.
Ending D2 -- NO FURTHER MYSTERY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The fence is mended, the season passes, and the garden grows well enough. No pigs come. No more tiny footprints appear. No little god is ever seen. (Name) grows a little older, and stops talking about it, and starts helping with the weeding instead. But years later, grown up, (he/she) still leaves one berry at the end of the bean row every harvest. Just in case.
