MY-103. The Jar of Silent Thunder   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
In the middle of the old stone circle on the hill, half-buried in the turf, (name) finds a squat grey jar. Its lid is sealed with a knot of cord unlike any the village uses, looped and twisted in a pattern that makes (his/her) eyes hurt to follow.
It is only when the storm rolls in that afternoon that (name) notices the strange thing. Every time the thunder booms overhead, the jar shivers on the ground. It rattles and trembles and dances on the grass. And it makes no sound at all. Not a clink, not a buzz. Perfect, trembling silence. (Name) is itching to know what is inside. Should (he/she) open it?
Choice A: Untie the Knot
Choice B: Study the Jar
Choice C: Carry It Home
Choice D: Leave It at the Circle

CHOICE A: UNTIE THE KNOT
First popup: (Name) kneels by the jar, and very carefully, loop by loop, begins to work at the strange knot, while the thunder rolls overhead and the jar trembles under (his/her) fingers...
Ending A1 -- THE WARM BREATH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The last loop comes free, and the lid lifts by itself with a soft whoosh. A burst of warm air rushes out past (name)'s face, smelling of hot stone and rain, like the breath of a summer storm. And then the jar is still. It does not tremble again, not even when the next thunderclap shakes the hill. It is just an ordinary, empty jar. (Name) is not sure whether (he/she) has let something out, or let something rest.
Ending A2 -- THE RED BEADS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
As (name) pulls the knot loose, it does not just come undone. It unravels, and keeps unravelling, into a long, long thread strung with tiny red beads. (Name) winds it around (his/her) hand. When (he/she) finally counts the beads, there are exactly as many as there are standing stones in the circle. The jar is empty. (Name) wears the beads on (his/her) wrist after that, and they rattle faintly whenever it thunders.

CHOICE B: STUDY THE JAR
First popup: (Name) brings the researchers up to the stone circle during the next storm, and they crouch around the jar in the pouring rain, watching it dance, and arguing loudly over the thunder...
Ending B1 -- IT FEELS THE GROUND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
After several soggy storms, one researcher works it out. "It's not the thunder," (he/she) says, lying flat with an ear to the turf. "It's the ground. The clay responds to shaking in the earth itself, the tiny shivers that travel through the rock when thunder strikes, or a tree falls, or the earth moves far away. It's like an ear for the island." The researchers start making jars of their own from the same clay, so they can feel the ground's tremors coming.
Ending B2 -- IT KEEPS TREMBLING. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The researchers watch it all through the storm, taking notes. And then the storm passes, the sky clears, the sun comes out, and the jar does not stop. It goes on trembling silently on the grass in perfect calm, as though it can still hear thunder that no one else can. It trembles all that day and all the next night. The researchers become a little nervous and go home. The next morning, it is still.

CHOICE C: CARRY IT HOME
First popup: (Name) decides the jar would be safer in the village. (He/she) wraps it in a cloth, hefts it into (his/her) arms, and starts down the hill...
Ending C1 -- THE STRANGE POWDER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Halfway down the hill, a thunderclap shakes the sky, the jar jerks violently in (name)'s arms, and with a crack, it splits clean in half. Out pours a fine, glittering powder, grey and sparkling like crushed stars, which drifts away on the wind before (name) can catch more than a pinch. The researchers study the pinch for weeks and cannot identify it. The two halves of the jar sit on a shelf, and they never tremble again.
Ending C2 -- TOO HEAVY TO CARRY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
With every step away from the stone circle, the jar gets heavier. By the bottom of the hill it is so heavy that (name) is staggering, sweating, bent double. Ten more steps, and (he/she) simply cannot hold it. (He/she) sets it down, gasping, and it sinks a finger's depth into the turf. (Name) leaves it there and goes to fetch help. When (he/she) returns with three strong villagers, the jar is gone from the hillside. They find it back in the middle of the stone circle, exactly where it started.

CHOICE D: LEAVE IT AT THE CIRCLE
First popup: (Name) decides that whatever this jar is, it belongs to the stone circle, not to the village. (He/she) leaves it exactly where it is and heads home through the rain...
Ending D1 -- UNTOUCHED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The jar stays where it is through the next storm, and the next, trembling silently each time the thunder rolls. Villagers start walking up to the circle during storms, just to watch it. It becomes a kind of strange, small village tradition: on stormy days, someone always says, "Shall we go and see the jar?" and they do, and they stand in the rain watching it dance, and nobody ever touches it.
Ending D2 -- THE SECOND JAR. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, (name) walks back up to the circle to check on it. There are two jars. The original, and right beside it a second one, a little smaller, sealed with an identical knot. No one in the village made it. No one carried it up there. When the next storm comes, both jars tremble together, in silence, side by side. (Name) stops visiting the stone circle after that.

MY-104. The Ferryman's Empty Boat   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
At dawn, the lagoon is as flat as glass, with a low mist lying on the water. (Name) is down at the shore early when (he/she) sees it: a small ferry boat gliding across the lagoon toward the far shore, without a ripple. Its paddle lies resting in the bottom of the boat. There is nobody in it.
(Name) watches it touch the far shore, wait there a moment, and then turn and glide all the way back. It bumps gently against the sand right at (his/her) feet, and rocks there, waiting, as if expecting someone to get in. Should (name) get in?
Choice A: Board the Ferry
Choice B: Call to the Rower
Choice C: Watch from Shore
Choice D: Leave the Boat Alone

CHOICE A: BOARD THE FERRY
First popup: Every sensible bone in (name)'s body says no. (Name) steps in anyway. The boat dips under (his/her) weight, then, without anyone touching the paddle, pulls smoothly away from the shore, out into the mist...
Ending A1 -- THE OLD FISHING GROUND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
The ferry glides across the lagoon and out through a narrow channel in the reef that (name) never knew existed, into a little sheltered bay. The water there is thick with striped fish, the kind nobody in the village has caught in years. The boat stops, and waits. (Name) fishes with (his/her) bare hands and a basket until the boat is half full, and the ferry carries (him/her) home again. When (he/she) steps out, it drifts off into the mist. Ending A2 -- DEEP WATER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The ferry glides out past the far shore, past the reef, and keeps going, out into deep water, far from land. (Name) grabs the paddle, and the paddle will not move. (He/she) shouts. The boat does not stop. Finally (name) jumps over the side. (He/she) swims for a very long time against the pull of the water and crawls up the beach at last, shaking, gasping and utterly spent. Behind (him/her), the ferry is already gliding back across the lagoon, empty and calm.

CHOICE B: CALL TO THE ROWER
First popup: "Hello?" (name) calls, peering at the empty boat. "Is anyone there? Who's rowing?" The mist muffles (his/her) voice. For a moment there is only the soft lap of water against the hull...
Ending B1 -- "WHERE DO YOU WISH TO GO?" Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
A voice answers from the empty stern of the boat, quiet and polite, like a ferryman who has asked the same question a thousand times: "Where do you wish to go?" (Name) cannot answer. (He/she) opens (his/her) mouth, and nothing comes out. After a long moment, the boat drifts away from the shore, back into the mist, and does not return. (Name) thinks about the question for many days after. (He/she) is still not sure what (he/she) would have said.
Ending B2 -- THE HIDDEN FISHER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

(He/she) has been lying under the cover pulling the boat along with a long pole pushed against the lagoon floor, to keep out of the cold wind, and fell asleep halfway through. (Name) laughs so hard (he/she) has to sit down in the shallows.

CHOICE C: WATCH FROM SHORE
First popup: (Name) does not go near it. (He/she) sits down on a rock, wraps (his/her) arms around (his/her) knees, and watches the empty ferry very carefully as it pulls away again across the lagoon...
Ending C1 -- THE SUBMERGED ROPE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
As the sun climbs and the mist burns off, (name) sees it: a long rope, running just below the surface of the water from one shore to the other, through a ring on the boat's bow. Someone on the far shore is slowly winding it in. When (name) walks around to look, (he/she) finds a clever wooden winch, hidden in the reeds, built by a fisher from the next village to pull goods across. Ending C2 -- CROSSING UNTIL SUNSET. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The ferry crosses and returns, crosses and returns, all day long, never fast, never slow, never with anyone in it. Villagers come down to watch it. Nobody gets in. MY-105. The Old Woman's Empty Hands   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special, with a home. The old woman is a visitor, not a villager. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT

"I didn't come for the food," she says at last. "I came to learn whether anyone would offer." (Name) stands in the doorway holding a bowl of stew, thoroughly confused. How should (he/she) respond?
Choice A: Ask What She Needs
Choice B: Offer a Meal Anyway
Choice C: Invite Her to Tell Her Story
Choice D: Dismiss Her

CHOICE A: ASK WHAT SHE NEEDS

CHOICE B: OFFER A MEAL ANYWAY

MY-106. The Circle of Unseen Dancers   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
Walking home at dusk, (name) hears music coming from the clearing in the woods: a drumbeat felt more than heard, and laughter, light and many-voiced, like a festival in full swing. But there is no festival tonight. (Name) creeps to the edge of the trees and peers in.
The clearing is empty. Completely empty. But the grass in the middle is flattened in a perfect ring, faintly glowing in the dusk, and the laughter and the drumbeat are coming from the ring itself, as though a crowd of people (name) cannot see are dancing round and round in it, having the time of their lives. The drumbeat is pulling at (name)'s feet. Should (he/she) step into the ring?
Choice A: Join the Dance
Choice B: Bring Musicians
Choice C: Examine the Clearing
Choice D: Leave an Offering

Ending A1 -- EXHILARATED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: like + jumping (VV3-VV5: jumping, a bouncier dance; VV1, VV2: dancing, story only)
(Name) dances alone in the empty ring, spinning and stamping and laughing, and for a while, (he/she) could swear (he/she) feels hands brushing (his/hers) and hears someone laugh right in (his/her) ear. Ending A2 -- LOST TRACK OF TIME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) dances and dances. The music never stops. (He/she) does not feel tired. When the drumbeat finally fades, (he/she) blinks, and finds the sun coming up over the trees. Ending D2 -- THE SOUNDS DO NOT RETURN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE C: ASK WHY THE SUN IS DIM

CHOICE D: CHASE THE BEGGAR AWAY

MY-109. The Stranger Who Spoke to the Tree   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
At the edge of the village stands the oldest tree on Isola: an enormous banyan whose roots hang down from its branches like ropes. Walking past it in the early morning, (name) finds a hooded stranger standing among the hanging roots, both hands pressed flat against the bark as though feeling for a heartbeat, whispering.
The stranger hears (name), and turns. "It has been waiting a very long time for an answer," (he/she) says, nodding at the tree. "Someone needed to ask." (He/she) seems to think this is a perfectly reasonable thing to say. (Name) is curious about this peculiar stranger, and wants to know what (he/she) is talking about.
Choice A: Ask What Was Said
Choice B: Listen to the Tree
Choice C: Offer to Help
Choice D: Send the Stranger Away

CHOICE A: ASK WHAT WAS SAID
First popup: "What did you ask it?" (name) says. "And... what did it say?" The stranger takes (his/her) hands from the bark and smiles...
Ending A1 -- THE RIDDLE OF SEASONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"I asked how to wait," the stranger says. "It answered with a riddle." And (he/she) recites it: "What grows by doing nothing, rests while it works, and is oldest when it begins again?" (Name) puzzles over it all day. So does half the village. The children decide the answer is "a seed." The elders say "a year." The stranger, asked before (he/she) leaves, only says, "Both, and the tree." (Name) still thinks about it every spring.
Ending A2 -- CARE FOR ITS ROOTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"It asked for help," the stranger says simply. "Its roots are choking. Someone should look after them." (He/she) points to the base of the tree, where (name) sees for the first time how the roots are buried in rubbish, vines and fallen branches. The stranger walks away down the path. (Name) does not know if the tree really said anything. But (he/she) goes and gets a rake.

CHOICE B: LISTEN TO THE TREE
First popup: (Name) steps in among the hanging roots, feeling very silly, and presses (his/her) own ear to the great trunk. The stranger watches in silence...
Ending B1 -- ALMOST A VOICE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
At first there is only the creak of wood and the rush of wind through the great canopy far above. Then the wind changes, and the sound changes with it, and for a moment it sounds almost like a voice: low and slow, saying something long, in a language (name) does not know. Then it is just the wind again. (Name) steps back. The stranger nods, as if (name) has finally understood something. (Name) is not at all sure that (he/she) has.
Ending B2 -- THE WHISPERING HOLLOW. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
(Name)'s ear finds a hollow in the trunk, and when (he/she) speaks into it, startled, the tree whispers the words back, slowly, one at a time, from somewhere deep inside. The researchers come running and spend a week studying it. The great banyan, they discover, is hollow almost all the way up, and its curving inner walls carry and bend sound in remarkable ways. They learn a great deal about how sound travels, and the children spend the rest of the season whispering secrets into the tree.

CHOICE C: OFFER TO HELP
First popup: "If the tree needs something," (name) says, "I'll help." The stranger looks genuinely delighted...
Ending C1 -- THE ROOTS IN THE SUN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
(Name) rounds up a dozen villagers, and they spend the whole day around the old banyan, pulling away vines, hauling off dead branches, clearing out rubbish and loosening the packed earth around its roots. By evening, the great roots stand clean and bare in the sun for the first time in generations. The tree looks, somehow, as if it is breathing easier. That season, it grows new leaves all over its oldest branches, and the stranger is seen once more, sitting among the roots, smiling.
Ending C2 -- A PACKET OF SEEDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (small)
(Name) clears the worst of the vines from the roots while the stranger watches, nodding. When (name) finally straightens up, sweating, the stranger presses a small leaf-wrapped packet into (his/her) hand. "From the tree," (he/she) says. "For you." Inside are seeds. They are not banyan seeds. They grow, when (name) plants them, into a patch of sweet yams that feed the household for weeks. The stranger is gone before (name) can ask.

CHOICE D: SEND THE STRANGER AWAY
First popup: (Name) does not like strangers whispering to the village's trees. "That tree belongs to the village," (he/she) says firmly. "Please leave it alone, and move along."...
Ending D1 -- UNCHANGED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger bows, takes (his/her) hands from the bark, and walks off quietly, without argument. The tree remains exactly as it was. Nothing happens. The village goes on, and the great banyan goes on standing over it as it always has, roots hanging like ropes. Sometimes, walking past, (name) finds (himself/herself) wondering what the stranger asked it. (He/she) never finds out.
Ending D2 -- THE FALLEN BRANCH. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger leaves without a word. That night, with no wind at all, a great branch of the old banyan cracks and comes crashing down across the path, right where (name) walks every morning. Nobody is hurt. But the villagers gather around the fallen branch the next day in uneasy silence, and more than one of them wonders aloud whether it was a warning, or an answer.

MY-110. The Returned Lost Child   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 18 or older, not nursing, not special, who finds the child. The returned child is a newcomer under 14, not yet a villager. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
At the edge of the village, (name) sees a small child standing alone among the tall grass, looking at the huts. (Name) knows that face. Everyone over a certain age knows that face. It belongs to a child who vanished from this village years ago, and was mourned, and was never found.
The child has not aged a day. The same hair. The same scar on one knee. The same little shell necklace (he/she) was wearing on the day (he/she) disappeared. The child looks at (name) calmly, as though waiting for something, and the grass sways around (him/her) in the wind. Is it really the lost child? What should (name) do?
Choice A: Welcome the Child Home
Choice B: Ask Where They Have Been
Choice C: Seek an Explanation
Choice D: Give the Child Time

CHOICE A: WELCOME THE CHILD HOME
First popup: (Name) does not stop to think. (He/she) runs to the child, kneels, and takes (his/her) small hands. "Come home," (he/she) says, voice shaking. "Come on, everyone will want to see you." The child lets (him/her) lead the way...
Ending A1 -- EMBRACED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: new villager (child)
The child's family see (him/her) coming up the path, and for a moment, nobody can move at all. Then they are running, and the child is in their arms, and they hold (him/her) for a very long time, and nobody can speak. The village gathers around in stunned silence. There are so many questions, and the child answers almost none of them. But (he/she) eats supper at the family table, and sleeps in the family hut, and in the morning, (he/she) is still there. Whatever happened, the child has come home.
Ending A2 -- RECOGNIZES NO ONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
But as they walk into the village, and people begin to gather and stare and weep, the child grows frightened. (He/she) looks at the faces around (him/her), the family who lost (him/her), and does not recognize a single one. "I don't know you," (he/she) says, pulling away. "Please. I want to go to the other village. My family is there." (Name) and the heartbroken family walk (him/her) to the next village, where a couple run out crying with relief to hug (him/her). Nobody can explain the face, the scar, or the necklace.

CHOICE B: ASK WHERE THEY HAVE BEEN
First popup: (Name) kneels down in the grass, slowly, so as not to frighten the child. "Where have you been all this time?" (he/she) asks softly. The child thinks about it seriously...
Ending B1 -- KIND STRANGERS BEYOND THE HILLS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"With the people beyond the hills," the child says. "They found me when I got lost. They were kind. They fed me and let me play with their goats. But I missed home, so they showed me the way back." (He/she) does not understand when (name) explains that (he/she) has been gone for years. "It was only a little while," (he/she) insists. A party of villagers crosses the hills to thank the strangers. They find an empty valley, a ruined hut, and a single old goat, who follows them home.
Ending B2 -- WHERE THE SEASONS NEVER CHANGED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Somewhere nice," the child says dreamily. "Where it was always the same day. Always warm, never raining, and the fruit was always ripe. Nobody got older there." (He/she) frowns. "I don't know how I got back. I was just walking, and then I was here." The elders go very quiet when they hear this. That night they sit up late around the fire, and nobody will tell the younger villagers what they were talking about.

CHOICE C: SEEK AN EXPLANATION
First popup: Before letting anyone get their hopes up, (name) fetches the elders. They come out to the grass and look the child over carefully, and ask (him/her) a great many questions...
Ending C1 -- A STRIKING RESEMBLANCE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"There's a cousin's line in the village down the coast," one elder says slowly. "They had a child born a few years after ours went missing. Perhaps it's that one, wandered off. Family faces do repeat." The scar, they decide, is a coincidence. The necklace is a common style. It is the sensible explanation, and they walk the child down the coast to ask. The village there has no missing child. But a family there takes the little stranger in, and raises (him/her), and (he/she) grows up happy.
Ending C2 -- MEMORIES ONLY THE FAMILY KNEW. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The elders ask questions only the missing child could answer: the name of (his/her) favourite toy, the song (his/her) mother sang at bedtime, the secret hiding place under the floor of the family hut. The child answers every single one, correctly, without hesitating. The elders look at each other. One of them sits down very suddenly in the grass. Nobody knows what to do next, and the child just waits patiently for them to decide.

CHOICE D: GIVE THE CHILD TIME
First popup: (Name) decides not to overwhelm the child. The village offers (him/her) a quiet hut to rest in, food and a blanket, and leaves (him/her) be, without demanding a single answer...
Ending D1 -- SHELTER WITHOUT QUESTIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The child rests and eats, and over the following days, slowly begins to come out of the hut and play at the edges of the village, watching the other children. Nobody presses (him/her). The family of the missing child visit every day, bringing food and sitting quietly nearby, never asking. After a week, the child takes the mother's hand of (his/her) own accord. Nobody ever learns what happened. In time, nobody needs to.
Ending D2 -- GONE BEFORE DAWN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: disappears (the returned child, no grave)
In the morning, the hut is empty. The blanket is folded neatly. The food has been eaten. And on the pillow lies a small carved turtle, the kind the missing child used to carry everywhere, years ago. It is warm, as if it has only just been put down. The village searches all day, and finds no sign of (him/her) anywhere. The family keep the turtle by their bed, and some nights, they say, it is still warm.

MY-111. The Wandering Herbalist's Box   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special, with a home. (name2) = a villager who falls sick, 14 or older, not nursing, not special (only for Choice A). In VV5, believers.
EVENT TEXT
A traveling herbalist stops at (name)'s door just long enough to press a small lacquered box into (his/her) hands. It is black, painted with tiny white flowers, and smells powerfully of camphor and dried ginger. "Keep this safe for me," the herbalist says. "I'll come back for it when the moon is full." And (he/she) is gone up the road before (name) can ask a single question.
That was two weeks ago. The moon is nearly full. And now (name2) has fallen sick with a fever that the village healers cannot seem to break. Should (name) break (his/her) promise and open the box?
Choice A: Open the Box for an Emergency
Choice B: Keep It Sealed
Choice C: Study the Labels
Choice D: Search for the Herbalist

CHOICE A: OPEN THE BOX FOR AN EMERGENCY
First popup: (Name) hesitates for a long time, then decides a promise is worth less than a life. (He/she) carries the box to the healers' hut and opens it. Inside, packed in tiny compartments, are dozens of dried herbs, powders and roots...
Ending A1 -- THE FEVER BREAKS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The healers recognize a few of the herbs, and after much careful discussion, brew a weak tea from one of them, a feathery grey leaf. They give (name2) a few sips at a time through the night. By morning, the fever has broken. (Name2) sleeps through the next night for the first time in days, and wakes up demanding food, which the healers take to be a very good sign. (Name) closes the box carefully, and hopes the herbalist will understand.
Ending A2 -- THE WRONG REMEDY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: (name2) is ill
The healers try a dark, bitter powder they do not recognize, and it is a mistake. (Name2) becomes dizzy and sick on top of the fever, and spends several miserable days unable to keep anything down. (He/she) recovers in the end, thanks to the healers' care. The healers put the rest of that powder away for good, and write a large warning on its compartment. (Name) feels awful, and spends a lot of time sitting at (name2)'s bedside apologizing.

CHOICE B: KEEP IT SEALED
First popup: (Name) made a promise. (He/she) keeps the box closed on the shelf, and helps the healers care for (name2) in the ordinary way, with cool cloths and broth, through the long nights...

Ending B2 -- NO ONE COMES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

The box sits on (name)'s shelf, sealed, still smelling of camphor and ginger. (Name) keeps it there for years. Every full moon, (he/she) glances at the door. CHOICE C: STUDY THE LABELS

Ending C1 -- A BETTER WAY TO SORT REMEDIES. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
The labels are a revelation, not for what is inside, but for how it is arranged. The herbalist has sorted every remedy by what it treats, how strong it is, and how it should be taken, with little coloured marks that the healers can read at a glance. CHOICE D: SEARCH FOR THE HERBALIST

Ending D1 -- HELPING ANOTHER SETTLEMENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

(Name) runs home with it. (Name2) is better in two days.
Ending D2 -- THE ABANDONED CAMP. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Nobody is there, and from the look of it, nobody has been for days. There is no sign of where the herbalist went. (Name) walks home slowly, worried, and finds that (name2) has begun to recover on (his/her) own. The box goes back on the shelf.

From that night on, the canoe song is always sung all the way through, and the village feels, somehow, a little more complete.

CHOICE B: ASK WHERE THEY LEARNED IT

Ending B1 -- A GRANDPARENT. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

Ending B2 -- BEFORE THE VILLAGE WAS FOUNDED. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

CHOICE C: OFFER HOSPITALITY

CHOICE D: REFUSE TO SING

Ending D2 -- HUMMED ON THE WIND. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none

MY-113. The Garden of the Vanished   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer. (elder name) = a very old, solitary villager (named in the text only).
EVENT TEXT
Far from the usual paths, (name) pushes through a thicket and finds a small hidden garden, ringed by low grey stones. Each stone is carved with a name. Between them grow red and white flowers that sway gently, even though there is no wind.
(Name) reads the nearest names, and goes cold. (He/she) knows some of them. They are the names of people who disappeared from Isola: villagers who went out fishing and never came back, children who wandered into the forest, travelers who were never heard from again. Someone has made a garden for the vanished. And someone, by the look of it, is still tending it. Who? And what should (name) do?
Choice A: Read the Names
Choice B: Tend the Garden
Choice C: Search for Its Keeper
Choice D: Leave It Undisturbed

CHOICE A: READ THE NAMES
First popup: (Name) walks slowly around the ring of stones, reading every name aloud, softly, one at a time. Some (he/she) knows. Many (he/she) does not. And then (he/she) comes to one that stops (him/her) short...
Ending A1 -- MATCHING THE RECORDS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (small)
Several of the names match the old village records exactly: the dates people went missing, the families they left behind. (Name) copies down every name and brings them to the researchers, who spend weeks comparing them against the records, and filling in gaps in the village's history that had been missing for generations. Families who had lost track of distant relatives learn what became of them. The researchers' records are better than they have ever been.
Ending A2 -- A LIVING NAME. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
It is the name of a villager who is still alive. (Name) knows (him/her) well; (he/she) is sitting by the fire back in the village at this very moment. (Name) runs all the way home. When (he/she) gently tells the villager whose name is on the stone, the villager goes very quiet. Then (he/she) says, slowly, "I was lost in the forest as a child. For three days. Everyone thought I was gone." (He/she) asks to be taken to see the stone. (He/she) stands before it a long time, then lays a flower on it, and walks home alive.

CHOICE B: TEND THE GARDEN
First popup: (Name) kneels and begins to pull the weeds from between the stones, gently, and brings water from a nearby stream for the swaying red and white flowers. When (he/she) comes back the next day, (he/she) brings friends...
Ending B1 -- A MEMORIAL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
Before long, the villagers take the little garden under their care. They clear the paths, water the flowers, and bring new ones. Families come to sit among the stones and remember those who never came home, because there were never any graves to visit. For the first time, they have a place to grieve. The garden of the vanished becomes one of the most peaceful places on the island.
Ending B2 -- BLOOMING OUT OF SEASON. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next morning, every flower in the garden is blooming, far out of season, red and white and swaying, more of them than (name) has ever seen. The smell drifts all the way to the village. Some of the villagers call it a blessing, a thank-you from the vanished for being remembered. Others say it is just the water. (Name) does not argue with either side. (He/she) just keeps tending it.

CHOICE C: SEARCH FOR ITS KEEPER
First popup: Someone made this garden. Someone is keeping it. (Name) is determined to find out who. (He/she) searches the paths and thickets around the garden...
Ending C1 -- THE OLD CARETAKER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
In a tiny hut tucked into the hillside, (name) finds (elder name), a very old villager (he/she) has hardly ever spoken to: quiet, solitary, often forgotten. "My brother was the first one," (elder name) says. "Lost at sea when I was young. There was nowhere to grieve for him, so I made a stone. Then I made another, for a friend. And another." (He/she) has been tending the garden alone for sixty years. (Name) asks if (he/she) can help. (elder name) weeps.
Ending C2 -- NO KEEPER. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
There is no one. No hut, no path in, no footprints. And yet every time (name) returns, the paths between the stones are freshly swept. Fresh water has been poured on the roots, still dark in the soil. A broom made of twigs leans against the largest stone, and once, it is in a different place than before. (Name) never sees anyone. (He/she) leaves a thank-you note on the largest stone, and it is gone the next day.

CHOICE D: LEAVE IT UNDISTURBED
First popup: (Name) decides this is not a place for strangers. (He/she) bows to the stones, backs out of the thicket, and tells only the elders what (he/she) found...
Ending D1 -- A QUIET PLACE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The elders agree the garden should be left in peace. It becomes a quiet, half-secret place, known to only a few: somewhere to go and sit when grief gets too heavy, or when someone needs to remember. (Name) goes there sometimes. (He/she) never touches anything. (He/she) just sits among the swaying flowers for a while, and always leaves feeling lighter than when (he/she) came.
Ending D2 -- A NEW STONE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The next time (name) visits, there is a new stone in the ring. Fresh-cut, its edges still sharp, the moss not yet grown on it. The name on it is one nobody in the village recognizes. Nobody has gone missing. Nobody knows that name. (Name) asks the elders, and the researchers, and everyone (he/she) can think of. Nobody ever knows who it was for. And no one can tell whether that person is lost already, or yet to be.

MY-114. The Stranger Who Offered a Choice   [VV1, VV2, VV3, VV4, VV5]
WHO: (Name) = one villager, 14 or older, not nursing, not special. In VV5, a believer.
EVENT TEXT
(Name) wakes at midnight to find a cloaked stranger standing outside (his/her) door in the moonlight. Without a word, the stranger kneels and sets three things on the ground in a row: a sealed bottle of dark green glass, a small chest bound with iron, and a bowl so plain it almost seems to vanish in the moonlight.
"Choose one," the stranger says. "Only one. Whatever you choose is yours." The stranger's face is hidden in the hood. The moon is very bright. And the three gifts sit on the ground between them, waiting. Which should (name) choose?
Choice A: Take the Bottle
Choice B: Take the Chest
Choice C: Take the Bowl
Choice D: Refuse All Gifts

CHOICE A: TAKE THE BOTTLE
First popup: (Name) reaches for the green bottle. It is cool and heavy in (his/her) hand. The stranger nods once, gathers up the chest and the bowl, and is gone. (Name) works the wax seal loose, and pulls out the stopper...
Ending A1 -- THE MEDICINAL OIL. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
A rich, sweet fragrance fills the air, like flowers and resin and warm earth. The bottle is full of a golden oil. (Name) takes it to the healers in the morning, who sniff it, dab it, and test it carefully, and find that it soothes aching joints and burns better than anything they have. They use it sparingly, a drop at a time, and it lasts for years. The old villagers with stiff knees and bad backs bless (name)'s name every winter.
Ending A2 -- THE MIST. Chance 50%. EFFECT: ill
A thick, sweet-smelling mist pours out of the bottle and straight into (name)'s face before (he/she) can turn away. (He/she) coughs and stumbles back, and by morning (he/she) is in bed with a pounding head and a burning fever. The healers keep (him/her) there for several days on rest and broth. When (he/she) finally recovers, the bottle is empty, and smells of nothing at all. (Name) throws it into the sea.

CHOICE B: TAKE THE CHEST
First popup: (Name) chooses the iron-bound chest. It is heavy, and something shifts inside it. The stranger nods, gathers up the other two gifts, and is gone. (Name) drags the chest inside and pries open the lid...
Ending B1 -- TOOLS AND INSTRUCTIONS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: tech gain (normal)
Inside, packed in dry straw, is a set of old tools: chisels, a drill, a strange curved saw, and a fine little hammer, all beautifully made and still sharp. With them is a bundle of bark sheets covered in drawings showing exactly how to use each one, and what to build with them. The builders and researchers are thrilled, and within a season they have learned new ways of working wood and stone that nobody on the island knew before.
Ending B2 -- SPOILED GRAIN. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food loss (small)
Inside is grain: sacks and sacks of it, packed tight. (Name) is delighted for about a breath. Then the smell hits. The grain is mouldy and spoiled through, crawling with weevils. Worse, by the time (name) realizes it, (he/she) has already stacked it in the village storehouse, and the weevils have spread into the good stores beside it. The villagers have to throw out a fair amount of food. (Name) is not popular for a while.

CHOICE C: TAKE THE BOWL
First popup: (Name) looks at the gleaming bottle and the heavy chest, and then picks up the plain bowl. The stranger seems to smile under the hood, gathers the other two gifts, and is gone into the dark...
Ending C1 -- THE FRUIT BENEATH THE TREE. Chance 50%. EFFECT: food gain (normal)
For days, nothing happens. The bowl is just a bowl. Then, one morning, (name) leaves it under the mango tree while (he/she) works in the garden, and when (he/she) comes back, it is heaped with fresh, ripe fruit. (He/she) empties it. The next morning, it is full again. It only works under a tree, (name) discovers, and only once a day, but it never fails. (Name) shares the fruit with everyone, and the bowl becomes the most precious thing in the household.
Ending C2 -- GIVEN AWAY. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The bowl remains empty, day after day. It is just a plain, ordinary bowl. Then (name) notices that a struggling family down the path has nothing to eat from but a cracked old shell. (He/she) gives them the bowl. The family uses it every day for years, for every meal, and never knows where it came from. (Name) never regrets the choice. (He/she) suspects, in fact, that it might have been the right one all along.

CHOICE D: REFUSE ALL GIFTS
First popup: (Name) looks at the three gifts for a long time. Then (he/she) shakes (his/her) head. "Thank you," (he/she) says. "But I don't want any of them."...
Ending D1 -- SMILES AND DEPARTS. Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
The stranger is silent for a moment. Then, under the hood, (name) sees a smile, a warm and genuine one. The stranger picks up the three gifts, bows deeply, and walks off down the path in the moonlight, without the slightest complaint. (Name) goes back to bed, and sleeps better than (he/she) has in months. (He/she) never does learn what was in the chest.
Ending D2 -- "THEN YOUR CHOICE IS YOUR OWN." Chance 50%. EFFECT: none
"Then your choice," the stranger says, "is your own." And between one breath and the next, the stranger, the bottle, the chest and the bowl are all simply gone, vanished into the dark as if they had never been. There is not even a mark on the ground where they sat. (Name) stands alone in the moonlight in (his/her) sleeping wrap, and thinks about that sentence for a very long time.
